title: Classic Beef Biryani
instructions:
1. Marinate beef with yogurt, ginger, garlic and spices for 2 hours.
2. Fry sliced onions in ghee until golden brown.
3. Cook marinated beef until tender.
4. Parboil basmati rice with whole spices.
5. Layer rice over the beef, add saffron milk and fried onions.
6. Cover and cook on low heat (dum) for 25 minutes.
7. Rest 5 minutes, then fluff and serve.

title: Mutton Rezala
instructions:
1. Marinate mutton in yogurt, ginger-garlic paste and salt for 1 hour.
2. Fry whole spices in ghee, add onion paste and cook until golden.
3. Add marinated mutton and cook until oil separates.
4. Add poppy seed and cashew paste with a little water.
5. Slow-cook covered until the meat is tender.
6. Finish with green chili and a splash of rose water.
7. Serve with naan or polao.

title: Shorshe Ilish (Hilsa in Mustard)
instructions:
1. Marinate hilsa pieces with turmeric and salt.
2. Mix mustard paste with a little water and green chili.
3. Heat mustard oil and gently place the fish.
4. Add mustard paste, cover and steam for 8-10 minutes.
5. Drizzle raw mustard oil and rest before serving.
6. Serve with plain rice.

title: Bangladeshi Beef Curry
instructions:
1. Heat oil and temper panch phoron.
2. Add onion paste and cook until golden.
3. Add beef and ground spices, cook 20 minutes.
4. Add water and simmer until the meat is half-done.
5. Add potatoes and cook until tender.
6. Adjust salt and serve with rice.

title: Chicken Khichuri
instructions:
1. Dry-roast moong dal until aromatic.
2. Fry whole spices and onion in ghee.
3. Add chicken and ginger-garlic, cook 10 minutes.
4. Add rice, dal, turmeric and water.
5. Add potatoes and simmer until soft.
6. Serve hot — perfect for a rainy day.

title: Beef Bhuna
instructions:
1. Cook beef with onion, ginger-garlic and spices until water dries.
2. Add oil and fry on medium heat.
3. Keep stirring until the masala coats the meat (bhuna).
4. Sprinkle garam masala and cover for 5 minutes.
5. Serve with paratha or rice.

title: Chicken Roast
instructions:
1. Marinate chicken in yogurt, spices and fried onion.
2. Heat ghee and sear the chicken until browned.
3. Add the marinade and a little water.
4. Cover and cook on low heat until tender.
5. Uncover and reduce the gravy until thick and glossy.
6. Serve with polao.

title: Mishti Doi
instructions:
1. Boil milk and reduce to about three-quarters.
2. Caramelize sugar and add to the milk.
3. Cool to lukewarm, then whisk in yogurt as a starter.
4. Pour into earthen pots and cover.
5. Keep in a warm place for 6-8 hours to set.
6. Chill before serving.

title: Payesh (Rice Kheer)
instructions:
1. Boil milk and add washed rice.
2. Simmer, stirring often, until the rice is soft and milk thickens.
3. Add sugar and cardamom.
4. Stir in ghee, raisins and cashews.
5. Cook 5 more minutes and serve warm or chilled.

title: Aloo Gobi
instructions:
1. Heat oil and temper cumin.
2. Add onion, ginger and garlic; fry until soft.
3. Add tomato and spices.
4. Add potato and cauliflower, toss to coat.
5. Cover and cook on low heat until tender.
6. Garnish with coriander and serve with roti.

title: Daal Tadka
instructions:
1. Boil dal with turmeric and salt until soft.
2. Heat ghee, add cumin, mustard seeds and dried chili.
3. Add onion, garlic and tomato; fry until soft.
4. Pour the tadka over the dal.
5. Simmer 5 minutes and garnish with coriander.

title: Chicken Tikka Masala
instructions:
1. Marinate chicken in yogurt, ginger-garlic and spices.
2. Grill or pan-sear the chicken.
3. Cook onion in butter, add tomato puree and spices.
4. Add cream and simmer into a smooth sauce.
5. Add the grilled chicken and simmer 10 minutes.
6. Serve with rice or naan.

title: Vegetable Fried Rice
instructions:
1. Cook rice and cool completely.
2. Heat oil and scramble the egg; set aside.
3. Stir-fry garlic and vegetables on high heat.
4. Add rice, soy sauce, pepper and salt.
5. Toss in the egg and spring onion.
6. Serve hot.

title: Kabuli Pulao
instructions:
1. Brown the lamb with onion and whole spices.
2. Add water and simmer until tender.
3. Parboil soaked rice and layer over the lamb.
4. Steam (dum) until the rice is fluffy.
5. Saute carrot, raisins and almonds for the topping.
6. Garnish and serve.

title: Chana Masala
instructions:
1. Heat oil and fry onion until golden.
2. Add ginger-garlic and tomato; cook until soft.
3. Add spices and cook until oil separates.
4. Add boiled chickpeas and a little water.
5. Simmer 15 minutes and mash a few chickpeas to thicken.
6. Serve with rice or roti.

title: Beef Tehari
instructions:
1. Cook beef with onion, ginger-garlic and spices until tender.
2. Parboil rice with whole spices.
3. Layer the rice over the beef and its gravy.
4. Add ghee and cook on dum for 20 minutes.
5. Fluff gently and serve.

title: Prawn Malai Curry
instructions:
1. Marinate prawns with turmeric and salt.
2. Fry onion paste with whole spices until golden.
3. Add the ground spices and cook briefly.
4. Pour in coconut milk and simmer.
5. Add the prawns and cook 5-6 minutes.
6. Finish with a pinch of sugar and serve with rice.

title: Mutton Kacchi Biryani
instructions:
1. Marinate mutton with yogurt, ginger-garlic and biryani masala overnight.
2. Fry onions until golden.
3. Parboil rice and drain.
4. Layer marinated mutton, potatoes and rice in a heavy pot.
5. Add saffron milk, ghee and fried onion; seal the lid.
6. Cook on dum for 45 minutes.
7. Rest and serve.

title: Vegetable Khichuri
instructions:
1. Dry-roast moong dal.
2. Temper cumin and fry onion and ginger in ghee.
3. Add vegetables and turmeric; toss.
4. Add rice, dal and water.
5. Simmer until soft and porridge-like.
6. Serve with a dollop of ghee.

title: Roshogolla
instructions:
1. Curdle milk with lemon juice and drain to make chena.
2. Knead the chena until smooth.
3. Roll into small balls.
4. Boil sugar, water and cardamom to make syrup.
5. Drop the balls in and cook 15 minutes.
6. Let them soak and cool before serving.

title: Beef Nihari
instructions:
1. Brown onion in ghee, add ginger-garlic paste.
2. Add beef and sear well.
3. Add yogurt, spices and water; cook slowly for 2-3 hours.
4. Mix flour with water and stir in to thicken.
5. Simmer 20 minutes.
6. Garnish with ginger, chili and coriander.

title: Paneer Butter Masala
instructions:
1. Boil tomato, onion and cashew; blend to a smooth puree.
2. Cook the puree in butter with ginger-garlic and spices.
3. Add cream and a little water.
4. Add paneer cubes and simmer 10 minutes.
5. Crush kasuri methi on top.
6. Serve with naan.

title: Chicken Curry (Bengali Style)
instructions:
1. Heat oil and fry onion until golden.
2. Add ginger-garlic paste and spices.
3. Add chicken and cook until it changes colour.
4. Add tomato and a little water.
5. Simmer until the chicken is tender and gravy thickens.
6. Garnish with coriander and serve with rice.

title: Shakshuka
instructions:
1. Saute onion, capsicum and garlic in oil.
2. Add cumin, paprika and tomato; cook into a sauce.
3. Make wells and crack in the eggs.
4. Cover and cook until the whites set.
5. Garnish with coriander and chili flakes.
6. Serve with bread.

title: Kacchi Biryani
ingredients: 1 kg bone-in mutton, cut into large pieces
750 g aged basmati rice, soaked 30 minutes
1/2 cup warm milk with a pinch of saffron
instructions:
1. Fry the sliced onions in hot mustard oil until deep golden and crisp; set aside half as beresta for layering.
2. Marinate the mutton with yogurt, ginger and garlic paste, biryani masala, chili powder, nutmeg, mace, half the fried onions, 4 tbsp mustard oil and salt; refrigerate at least 4 hours or overnight.
3. Fry the potato quarters in the same oil until lightly golden; set aside.
4. Boil 3 litres of water with salt, sugar, 4 cardamom pods, 1 cinnamon stick, 3 cloves and 1 bay leaf; add the soaked rice and parboil until 70 percent cooked (5-6 minutes), then drain.
5. In a heavy-bottomed pot, spread the marinated mutton with all its marinade at the bottom, arrange the potatoes over it, then cover with the parboiled rice.
6. Sprinkle the rice with saffron milk, kewra water, remaining fried onions, mint and 3 tbsp ghee.
7. Seal the pot tightly with foil or a dough lid, cook on high heat for 10 minutes, then reduce to the lowest heat and steam (dum) for 60-75 minutes until the mutton is tender.
8. Rest 15 minutes without lifting the lid, then gently fluff and serve hot with salad and borhani or raita.

title: Nihari
ingredients: 1.5 kg beef shank with bone marrow pieces
4 tbsp wheat flour or 3 tbsp ready nihari masala
1 bay leaf, 1 cinnamon stick, 4 cloves, 4 green cardamom pods
instructions:
1. Heat half the oil in a large pot and fry the onions until deep golden; reserve half for garnish.
2. Add the beef and sear on high heat for 5-6 minutes until browned.
3. Stir in ginger and garlic paste, then all powdered spices and salt; cook 3-4 minutes.
4. Pour in 3 litres of hot water, add the bay leaf, cinnamon, cloves and cardamom, and bring to a boil.
5. Whisk the wheat flour with 1 cup of water until smooth and stir it into the pot.
6. Cover and simmer on the lowest heat for 5-6 hours, stirring occasionally, until the meat is fall-apart tender and the gravy is silky and thick.
7. For the final tempering, heat the remaining oil, add the reserved onions and garam masala, and pour this sizzling mixture back over the nihari.
8. Garnish with ginger juliennes, green chilies, cilantro and lemon; serve hot with naan or kulcha.

title: Sajji
ingredients: 2 tbsp raw green papaya paste (optional tenderizer)
Lemon wedges and sliced onions to serve
instructions:
1. Wash and pat the chicken dry, then make deep slits over the legs, thighs and breast.
2. Rub the chicken inside and out with coarse salt and leave for 1 hour to cure, then rinse and pat completely dry.
3. Marinate with lemon juice, garlic paste, cumin, black pepper and papaya paste, working it well into the slits; rest 2 hours.
4. Skewer the chicken lengthwise on a metal rod or place it on a roasting rack.
5. Roast over medium charcoal coals for 45-50 minutes, turning every 10 minutes and basting with ghee, until the skin is charred and juices run clear; alternatively roast in an oven at 200 C for about 60 minutes.
6. Rest 10 minutes, sprinkle with chaat masala and serve with lemon wedges, onions and naan or rice.

title: Chapli Kabab
ingredients: 1 kg beef mince with some fat
2 medium onions, very finely chopped and squeezed dry
1 cup cooking oil for shallow frying
instructions:
1. Dry roast the gram flour until fragrant and lightly golden, then cool.
2. Combine the mince, onions, tomatoes, green chilies, pomegranate seeds, gram flour, egg, ginger, garlic, all spices, cilantro and salt; mix well and refrigerate for 1 hour.
3. With oiled hands, shape into flat round patties about 1 cm thick and press a slice of tomato into the centre of each.
4. Heat oil in a wide frying pan over medium heat.
5. Fry the kababs 4-5 minutes per side, pressing gently, until deeply browned with crisp charred edges.
6. Drain on paper towels and serve hot with naan, green chutney and sliced onions.

title: Chicken Tikka
ingredients: 1 kg boneless chicken thighs, cut into 4 cm cubes
1 small piece of charcoal (optional, for smoke)
instructions:
1. Pat the chicken dry and prick all over with a fork.
2. Whisk together yogurt, ginger, garlic, all spices, lemon juice, oil and salt to make the marinade.
3. Coat the chicken in the marinade, cover and refrigerate for at least 4 hours, preferably overnight.
4. Thread the pieces onto skewers, leaving small gaps between them.
5. Grill over hot charcoal or in an oven at 220 C for 20-25 minutes, turning every 8 minutes and basting with butter, until lightly charred and cooked through.
6. Optionally place a burning charcoal in a small bowl among the skewers, drizzle with oil and cover for 5 minutes to infuse smoke.
7. Rest 5 minutes and serve with mint chutney, sliced onions and lemon.

title: Aloo Gosht
ingredients: 750 g mutton or beef, bone-in pieces
1 bay leaf, 1 cinnamon stick, 4 green cardamom pods, 4 cloves
instructions:
1. Heat oil in a heavy pot and fry the onions until deep golden.
2. Add the meat and sear on high heat for 5-6 minutes until browned on all sides.
3. Stir in ginger, garlic, bay leaf, cinnamon, cardamom and cloves; cook 2 minutes.
4. Add tomatoes, coriander, chili, turmeric, cumin and salt; cook until the tomatoes break down and oil separates.
5. Add the yogurt a spoonful at a time, stirring constantly, then fry the masala (bhunai) for 8-10 minutes.
6. Pour in 4 cups of hot water, cover and cook on low heat for 60-75 minutes until the meat is tender (about 30 minutes in a pressure cooker).
7. Add the potatoes and green chilies, cover and cook 15-20 minutes until the potatoes are soft and the gravy has thickened.
8. Sprinkle garam masala and cilantro, rest 5 minutes and serve with roti, naan or plain rice.

title: Karahi
ingredients: 1 kg chicken, bone-in, cut into 12 pieces
instructions:
1. Heat ghee in a karahi or wok over high heat and add the chicken pieces.
2. Sear the chicken for 5-6 minutes until it changes colour and seals.
3. Add ginger and garlic paste and cook 2 minutes.
4. Add the chopped tomatoes and salt, cover and cook on medium heat for 15 minutes until the tomatoes collapse into a thick sauce; pick out and discard the tomato skins.
5. Add black pepper, cumin, chili flakes and kasuri methi; increase heat and fry (bhunai) for 8-10 minutes until the ghee separates.
6. Stir in the green chilies, half the ginger juliennes and cilantro; simmer uncovered 5 minutes.
7. Garnish with remaining ginger and serve hot straight from the karahi with naan.

title: Seekh Kabab
ingredients: 1 medium onion, grated and squeezed very dry
3 tbsp oil plus extra for basting
instructions:
1. Mix all ingredients except the basting oil and blitz in a food processor for 3-4 minutes until smooth and sticky.
2. Cover and refrigerate for 1 hour so the mince firms up.
3. With wet hands, press handfuls of the mixture onto metal skewers, forming even cylinders about 15 cm long.
4. Grill over medium-hot charcoal for 12-15 minutes, turning every 3-4 minutes and basting with oil, until browned and cooked through; alternatively bake at 220 C for 18-20 minutes.
5. Rest 2 minutes, slide off the skewers and serve with green chutney, onion rings and lemon wedges.

title: Haleem
ingredients: 1/4 cup each chana dal, masoor dal, moong dal and urad dal, soaked 4 hours
3 large onions, thinly sliced and fried golden
Garnish: fried onions, ginger juliennes, lemon wedges, green chilies, chaat masala
instructions:
1. Pressure cook the meat with ginger, garlic, turmeric, salt and 3 cups of water for 40-45 minutes until very tender; shred the meat and reserve the stock.
2. Add the soaked wheat and lentils to the pot with 6 cups of water and cook 45-50 minutes until completely soft.
3. Blend or pound the wheat-lentil mixture until smooth and paste-like.
4. Return the shredded meat and its stock to the pot and add the cereal paste, yogurt, half the fried onions, coriander, chili, cumin and salt.
5. Cook on the lowest heat for 45-60 minutes, stirring often and mashing with a heavy spoon until silky and homogeneous; add hot water if too thick.
6. Stir in ghee and garam masala and simmer 10 more minutes.
7. Serve hot topped with fried onions, ginger, cilantro, green chilies, a squeeze of lemon and a sprinkle of chaat masala.

title: Paya
ingredients: 4-6 beef or lamb trotters (paya), cleaned and split
1/4 cup roasted gram flour dissolved in 1 cup water (optional thickener)
instructions:
1. Scrub the trotters with salt and hot water, rinse well, then blanch in boiling water for 5 minutes and drain.
2. Heat oil in a large pot and fry the onions until deep golden.
3. Add the trotters and sear on high heat for 5 minutes, then add ginger and garlic paste and cook 2 minutes.
4. Add coriander, cumin, chili, turmeric and salt; stir in the yogurt gradually and fry (bhunai) for 8-10 minutes until oil separates.
5. Pour in 8 cups of hot water, cover and simmer on the lowest heat for 5-6 hours, topping up water as needed, until the meat is tender and the gravy is thick and gelatinous (about 2 hours in a pressure cooker).
6. Stir in the gram flour slurry and garam masala and simmer 15 minutes until glossy.
7. Garnish with ginger, green chilies, cilantro and lemon; serve piping hot with naan.

title: Lahori Chargha
ingredients: 1 whole chicken (about 1.2 kg), skin on, with deep slits
instructions:
1. Rub the chicken inside and out with salt, then coat thoroughly with a paste of yogurt, ginger, garlic, all powdered spices, lemon juice and oil.
2. Cover and marinate in the refrigerator for at least 4 hours, preferably overnight.
3. Place the chicken with its marinade in a deep pot, cover and steam on medium heat for 20-25 minutes until about 80 percent cooked; drain the liquid and pat the skin dry.
4. Heat oil for deep frying to 180 C.
5. Lower the chicken in carefully and fry 8-10 minutes, turning once, until deep golden and crisp; alternatively roast at 220 C for 25 minutes.
6. Rest 5 minutes, sprinkle with chaat masala and serve with mint chutney, raita and lemon wedges.

title: Sindhi Biryani
ingredients: 1/2 cup warm milk with a pinch of saffron
2 bay leaves, 1 cinnamon stick, 6 green cardamom pods, 6 cloves
instructions:
1. Fry the onions in ghee until deep golden; reserve half for layering.
2. Add the meat and sear on high heat for 5-6 minutes, then add ginger, garlic and whole spices.
3. Add tomatoes and cook until soft, then stir in yogurt, biryani masala and dried plums; fry (bhunai) until oil separates.
4. Add 2 cups of hot water, cover and cook until the meat is tender (40-50 minutes for mutton, 25 for chicken).
5. Add the potatoes and cook 10 minutes until half done; the gravy should be thick.
6. Meanwhile boil the rice in salted water with a few whole spices until 70 percent cooked; drain.
7. Layer the meat curry in a heavy pot, top with mint, cilantro and fried onions, then add the rice; finish with saffron milk, kewra and ghee.
8. Seal and steam on dum: 10 minutes on high, then 30-35 minutes on the lowest heat.
9. Rest 10 minutes, fluff gently and serve with raita and salad.

title: Biryani (Beef)
ingredients: 1 kg beef, bone-in, cut into medium pieces
2 bay leaves, 1 cinnamon stick, 6 green cardamom pods, 2 black cardamom pods, 6 cloves, 1 tsp cumin seeds
1/2 cup warm milk with a pinch of saffron
instructions:
1. Fry the onions in ghee until deep golden; reserve half.
2. Add the beef and sear on high heat until browned, about 6-8 minutes.
3. Add ginger, garlic and whole spices; cook 2 minutes, then add tomatoes and powdered spices.
4. When the tomatoes soften, add the yogurt gradually and fry (bhunai) 10 minutes until the oil separates.
5. Add 3 cups of hot water, cover and cook 60-75 minutes until the beef is tender and about 2 cups of thick gravy remain.
6. Boil the rice in salted spiced water until 70 percent cooked; drain.
7. Layer the beef gravy in a heavy pot, top with half the mint, cilantro and fried onions, then all the rice.
8. Finish with saffron milk, kewra, remaining herbs and onions and a drizzle of ghee.
9. Seal and dum: 10 minutes on high heat, then 40 minutes on the lowest heat; rest 10 minutes, fluff and serve.

title: Korma
ingredients: 4 large onions, thinly sliced and fried deep golden
1/2 cup almonds or cashews, soaked and ground to a paste
4 green cardamom pods, 4 cloves, 1 cinnamon stick, 2 bay leaves, 1 tsp cumin seeds
instructions:
1. Fry the onions in ghee until deep golden and crisp; blend half with 1/2 cup water into a smooth paste and reserve the rest for garnish.
2. In the same ghee, crackle the cumin and whole spices for 30 seconds.
3. Add the chicken and sear on high heat for 5 minutes until lightly golden.
4. Stir in ginger and garlic paste, then the powdered spices and salt; cook 2 minutes.
5. Lower the heat and add the yogurt a spoonful at a time, stirring constantly so it does not split.
6. Add the fried onion paste and nut paste and fry 8-10 minutes until the ghee separates.
7. Pour in 1.5 cups of hot water, cover and simmer 25-30 minutes until the chicken is tender.
8. Finish with cream, kewra and garam masala; simmer 5 minutes, garnish with the reserved fried onions and serve with naan or sheermal.

title: Rogan Josh
ingredients: 1 kg lamb, bone-in, cut into large pieces
4 green cardamom pods, 2 black cardamom pods, 4 cloves, 1 cinnamon stick, 2 bay leaves, 1 tsp cumin seeds
instructions:
1. Heat the oil until it just smokes (if using mustard oil), then lower the heat and crackle the whole spices for 30 seconds.
2. Add the lamb and sear on high heat for 8-10 minutes until well browned on all sides.
3. Stir in ginger and garlic paste and salt; cook 3 minutes.
4. Reduce the heat to low and add the whisked yogurt a spoonful at a time, stirring constantly to prevent splitting.
5. Add the Kashmiri chili, fennel powder and ginger powder; fry 8-10 minutes until the oil turns deep red and separates.
6. Add 2 cups of hot water, cover and simmer gently for 1.5-2 hours, stirring occasionally, until the lamb is fork tender and a layer of red oil floats on top.
7. Adjust salt, rest 10 minutes and serve with steamed rice or naan.

title: Pani Puri
ingredients: For the puris: 1/2 cup fine semolina, 1/2 cup all-purpose flour, 1/4 tsp salt, about 1/3 cup water, oil for deep frying (or 24 store-bought puris)

For the pani: 1 cup mint leaves, 1/2 cup cilantro, 2 green chilies, 1 inch ginger, 2 tbsp tamarind pulp, 1 tsp roasted cumin powder, 1 tsp chaat masala, 1 tsp black salt, 2 tbsp lemon juice, 4 cups chilled water, salt to taste
For the filling: 3 boiled potatoes, cubed, 1/2 cup boiled moong or chickpeas, 1 tsp chaat masala, 1/2 tsp black salt, 2 tbsp chopped cilantro
instructions:
1. Knead the semolina, flour, salt and just enough water into a stiff dough; cover and rest 20 minutes.
2. Roll very thin small discs and deep fry in hot oil, pressing gently so each one puffs up; fry until crisp and cool completely.
3. Blend all pani ingredients with 1 cup of the water until smooth, strain into the remaining chilled water and refrigerate.
4. Toss the potatoes, moong, chaat masala, black salt and cilantro together for the filling.
5. Tap a hole in the top of each puri, stuff with 1 tsp of filling and add a little tamarind chutney.
6. Fill with the chilled pani and serve immediately, one at a time.

title: Samosa
ingredients: For the dough: 2 cups all-purpose flour, 4 tbsp oil or melted ghee, 1/2 tsp carom seeds, 1/2 tsp salt, about 2/3 cup water

For the filling: 4 boiled potatoes, cut into small cubes, 1/2 cup green peas, 1 tsp cumin seeds, 1 tsp coriander powder, 1 tsp red chili powder, 1 tsp garam masala, 1 tsp dried mango powder (amchur), 2 tbsp oil, 1/4 cup chopped cilantro, salt to taste
2 tbsp all-purpose flour mixed with 3 tbsp water (sealing paste)
instructions:
1. Rub the oil or ghee into the flour with carom and salt until crumbly, then add water gradually and knead a stiff dough; rest covered 30 minutes.
2. For the filling, heat 2 tbsp oil, crackle the cumin, add potatoes, peas and all spices; toss 3-4 minutes, mash lightly, stir in cilantro and cool.
3. Roll the dough into 15 cm ovals, cut in half, and form each half into a cone, sealing the seam with the flour paste.
4. Fill each cone with 2 tbsp of filling without overfilling and seal the open edge firmly with the paste.
5. Fry the samosas in moderately hot oil on medium-low heat for 8-10 minutes, turning often, until golden and crisp; slow frying keeps them crisp.
6. Drain on paper towels and serve hot with tamarind and mint chutneys.

title: Gol Gappa
ingredients: For the puris: 1 cup fine semolina, 2 tbsp all-purpose flour, 1/4 tsp baking soda, warm water as needed, oil for deep frying

For the pani: 1 cup mint leaves, 1/2 cup cilantro, 1 inch ginger, 1 green chili, 2 tbsp tamarind pulp, 2 tsp roasted cumin powder, 1 tsp black salt, 1 tsp chaat masala, 2 tbsp lemon juice, 4 cups chilled water, salt to taste
For the filling: 3 boiled potatoes, mashed, 1/2 cup boiled kala chana (brown chickpeas), 1 tsp chaat masala, 1/2 tsp roasted cumin powder, salt to taste
instructions:
1. Knead the semolina, flour, baking soda and enough warm water into a stiff dough; cover and rest 20 minutes.
2. Roll out thin, cut 4 cm rounds and deep fry in hot oil, pressing each gently so it puffs into a hollow ball; fry until golden and crisp.
3. Blend the pani ingredients with 1 cup water, strain into the remaining chilled water and refrigerate 30 minutes.
4. Mix all the filling ingredients together.
5. Crack open each puri at the top, stuff with the potato-chana filling and add a few drops of tamarind chutney.
6. Fill with the chilled pani, add boondi if using, and serve immediately.

title: Dahi Bhalla
ingredients: 1 cup urad dal (split and skinned), soaked 5 hours
3 cups thick yogurt, whisked until smooth
instructions:
1. Drain the soaked dals and grind with cumin and asafoetida into a thick, fluffy batter using very little water.
2. Whip the batter vigorously for 3-4 minutes until light and airy; this keeps the bhallas soft.
3. Drop spoonfuls into medium-hot oil and fry until golden brown all over.
4. Soak the hot bhallas in warm water for 20 minutes, then press gently between your palms to squeeze out the water.
5. Whisk the yogurt with salt, sugar and 1/2 cup water until pourable.
6. Arrange the bhallas in a dish and pour the yogurt over to cover completely.
7. Top with tamarind chutney, roasted cumin, chaat masala, chili powder and cilantro; chill 30 minutes and serve.

title: Chaat
ingredients: 4 large boiled potatoes, peeled and cut into 2 cm cubes
instructions:
1. Heat the oil and fry the potato cubes on medium-high heat until crisp and golden, about 6-8 minutes.
2. Toss the hot potatoes with the chickpeas, cumin, chaat masala, black salt and chili powder.
3. Plate the mixture and drizzle with tamarind chutney and mint-coriander chutney.
4. Spoon over the yogurt if using, then scatter sev, pomegranate arils and cilantro on top.
5. Squeeze lemon over just before serving and eat immediately while crisp.

title: Butter Chicken
ingredients: 800 g boneless chicken thighs (halal-certified), cut into 4 cm cubes
2 tsp dried fenugreek leaves (kasuri methi), crushed
instructions:
1. Whisk yogurt, ginger paste, garlic paste, 1 tsp chili powder, 1/2 tsp garam masala and 1 tsp salt in a bowl. Add chicken, coat well, and marinate at least 1 hour (overnight is best).
2. Heat 2 tbsp oil in a heavy pan over high heat. Sear the marinated chicken in batches until browned and cooked through, about 8-10 minutes per batch. Set aside.
3. In the same pan, melt 40 g butter. Add tomatoes, cashews and remaining chili powder. Cook 15 minutes until the tomatoes collapse and oil separates at the edges.
4. Cool slightly, then blend until completely smooth and pass through a sieve for a silky gravy.
5. Return the gravy to the pan with the remaining butter. Simmer on low heat 10 minutes, stirring often.
6. Add the seared chicken, sugar, remaining garam masala and salt. Simmer 10 minutes over low heat.
7. Stir in cream and crushed kasuri methi. Simmer 5 more minutes, rest 10 minutes, and serve hot with naan or steamed rice.

title: Palak Paneer
ingredients: 250 g paneer, cut into 2 cm cubes
instructions:
1. Blanch spinach in boiling water for 2 minutes, then transfer straight into ice water to lock in the green colour.
2. Blend spinach with green chilies into a smooth puree without adding extra water.
3. Heat 1 tbsp ghee in a pan and lightly fry paneer cubes until pale gold on a few sides. Remove and keep in warm water.
4. Add remaining ghee to the pan, crackle cumin seeds, then fry onion until golden, 6-8 minutes.
5. Add ginger-garlic paste and cook 1 minute, then add tomato puree, turmeric, coriander powder and salt. Cook until the masala darkens and ghee separates, about 8 minutes.
6. Lower the heat, add spinach puree and simmer 8-10 minutes, stirring occasionally.
7. Drain paneer and fold it in with cream and garam masala. Simmer 3 minutes and serve hot with roti or jeera rice.

title: Chole Bhature
ingredients: 1.5 cups dried white chickpeas, soaked overnight
4 tbsp mustard oil or vegetable oil
2 tbsp oil plus more for deep frying
instructions:
1. Drain the soaked chickpeas and boil with the tea bags in plenty of water for 45-50 minutes until very soft. Discard tea bags and reserve 1 cup cooking liquid.
2. Heat 4 tbsp oil in a wide pan. Add bay leaves, black cardamom and cumin seeds; when fragrant, fry onions until deep golden, about 10 minutes.
3. Add ginger-garlic paste, cook 1 minute, then add tomato puree, chole masala, coriander powder, chili powder, anardana, turmeric and salt. Fry until oil separates, about 8 minutes.
4. Add boiled chickpeas with the reserved liquid. Simmer 20 minutes, mashing a few chickpeas against the pan to thicken the gravy.
5. For bhature, mix flour, semolina, yogurt, sugar, baking soda, salt and 2 tbsp oil with about 3/4 cup warm water. Knead 10 minutes into a soft, elastic dough.
6. Cover and rest the dough 2-3 hours in a warm place.
7. Divide into 6 balls and roll each into an oval about 15 x 20 cm.
8. Slide into oil heated to 180 C, press gently so it puffs, and fry until golden on both sides. Serve hot bhature with chole, sliced onion and green chili.

title: Dal Makhani
ingredients: 1 cup whole black urad dal, soaked overnight
instructions:
1. Drain the soaked urad dal and rajma. Pressure cook with 4 cups water and salt for 25-30 minutes until completely soft and creamy.
2. Mash some of the dal against the pot to create a thick, creamy body.
3. Melt 3 tbsp butter in a heavy pan. Fry ginger-garlic paste for 1 minute, add chili powder, then tomato puree. Cook 10 minutes until darkened and thick.
4. Add the cooked dal with a little of its cooking water. Simmer on the lowest heat 40-45 minutes, stirring often so it does not catch at the bottom.
5. Stir in garam masala, cream and kasuri methi. Simmer 10 more minutes.
6. Finish with 1 tbsp butter, rest 10 minutes, and serve with naan or steamed rice.

title: Dal Tadka
instructions:
1. Rinse toor dal until the water runs clear. Pressure cook with 3 cups water, turmeric and salt for 15-20 minutes until soft, then whisk until smooth.
2. Heat ghee in a small pan over medium heat. Add cumin and mustard seeds; when they pop, add dried chili and garlic slices and fry until the garlic turns golden.
3. Add onion and fry 5 minutes until soft and lightly browned.
4. Add tomato, green chilies, curry leaves and chili powder. Cook 4-5 minutes until the tomato breaks down.
5. Pour the sizzling tadka over the hot dal and stir well.
6. Simmer 5 minutes, adding hot water to reach a pourable consistency.
7. Finish with garam masala and coriander leaves. Serve with steamed rice or roti.

title: Idli
ingredients: 2 cups idli rice or parboiled rice
Coconut chutney and sambar, to serve
instructions:
1. Rinse rice, dal and fenugreek seeds separately. Soak rice in water for 6 hours; soak dal with fenugreek for 4 hours.
2. Grind the urad dal with just enough fresh water until fluffy and light, 5-6 minutes.
3. Grind the rice to a slightly coarse batter. Combine both batters with salt, mixing well by hand to aerate.
4. Cover loosely and ferment 8-12 hours in a warm spot until doubled and full of bubbles.
5. Grease idli plates with oil. Stir the batter gently and spoon it into the moulds.
6. Steam over simmering water for 10-12 minutes until a skewer inserted comes out clean.
7. Rest 2 minutes, unmould with a wet spoon, and serve hot with coconut chutney and sambar.

title: Dosa
ingredients: 2 cups idli rice or short-grain rice
Sambar and coconut chutney, to serve
instructions:
1. Soak rice, dal and fenugreek together for 6 hours, reserving 2 tbsp of soaked rice to grind with the batter.
2. Grind everything with water to a smooth, pourable batter slightly thinner than idli batter.
3. Add salt, mix by hand, cover and ferment 8-12 hours until risen and bubbly.
4. Heat a cast iron tawa until a drop of water dances on it. Wipe lightly with an oiled cloth.
5. Pour a ladle of batter in the centre and spread in a spiral outward into a thin circle.
6. Drizzle 1 tsp oil around the edges and cook 2-3 minutes until the underside is golden and the edges lift.
7. Fold or roll the dosa and slide onto a plate. Serve immediately with sambar and chutney; repeat with remaining batter.

title: Masala Dosa
ingredients: Prepared dosa batter from 2 cups rice and 1/2 cup urad dal, fermented
4 large potatoes, boiled and roughly mashed
Butter or oil for the tawa
instructions:
1. Heat 4 tbsp oil in a pan. Pop mustard seeds, then fry chana dal until golden.
2. Add green chilies, ginger and curry leaves; saute 30 seconds.
3. Add onion and cook 5 minutes until translucent.
4. Stir in turmeric, mashed potatoes, salt and water. Mix well and cook 5 minutes until soft but not wet. Fold in coriander leaves.
5. Heat the tawa and pour a ladle of batter, spreading into a thin round.
6. Drizzle oil around the edges and cook 2 minutes until the base sets and turns golden.
7. Spread 3 tbsp of potato masala over one half of the dosa.
8. Fold the dosa over the filling, slide onto a plate, and serve hot with sambar and coconut chutney.

title: Chicken Manchurian
ingredients: 500 g boneless chicken (halal-certified), cut into thick strips
2 tbsp cornflour mixed with 1/4 cup water
instructions:
1. Marinate chicken with soy sauce, ginger-garlic paste, egg, cornflour, flour, white pepper and a pinch of salt for 30 minutes.
2. Heat frying oil to 175 C. Fry chicken in batches 5-6 minutes until golden and cooked through; drain. Fry once more for 1 minute for extra crispness.
3. Heat 3 tbsp oil in a wok over high heat. Fry garlic, ginger and green chilies for 30 seconds until aromatic.
4. Add onion squares and toss 1 minute so they stay crunchy.
5. Add soy sauce, chili sauce, ketchup, vinegar, sugar, white pepper and stock. Bring to a boil.
6. Stir the cornflour slurry and pour it in, cooking until the sauce thickens and turns glossy, about 1 minute.
7. Toss in the fried chicken until fully coated. Finish with spring onions and serve immediately with fried rice or noodles.

title: Chilli Chicken
ingredients: 1 tbsp cornflour mixed with 2 tbsp water
instructions:
1. Toss chicken with soy sauce, ginger-garlic paste, egg, cornflour, flour, black pepper and salt. Rest 30 minutes.
2. Deep fry at 175 C in batches for 5-6 minutes until crisp and cooked through. Drain well.
3. Heat 3 tbsp oil in a wok on high heat. Fry garlic for 20 seconds, then add onion petals, capsicum and green chilies. Toss 2 minutes so the vegetables stay crunchy.
4. Add soy sauce, chili sauce, ketchup, vinegar, sugar and water; bring to a fast boil.
5. Stir in the cornflour slurry and cook until the sauce clings to a spoon, about 1 minute.
6. Return the fried chicken and toss vigorously 1-2 minutes until every piece is glazed.
7. Scatter spring onions and serve hot as a starter or with fried rice.

title: Hakka Noodles
ingredients: 2 spring onions, whites and greens separated
instructions:
1. Boil noodles in well-salted water until just al dente, 4-5 minutes. Drain, rinse under cold water and toss with 1 tbsp oil so they do not stick.
2. Heat remaining oil in a wide wok until very hot and lightly smoking.
3. Add garlic and spring onion whites; stir 20 seconds.
4. Add cabbage, carrot, capsicum and beans. Stir-fry on the highest heat 3-4 minutes so they stay crisp.
5. Push vegetables aside, add soy sauce, vinegar, chili sauce, white pepper, sugar and salt to the hot wok and let it sizzle 15 seconds.
6. Add noodles and toss continuously for 2 minutes until evenly coated and heated through.
7. Finish with spring onion greens, give a final toss and serve hot, plain or with chilli chicken.

title: Paneer Tikka
ingredients: 400 g paneer, cut into 3 cm cubes
1 tomato, deseeded and cut into squares
200 g thick yogurt, hung for 2 hours
Chaat masala and mint chutney, to serve
instructions:
1. Whisk hung yogurt with ginger-garlic paste, chili powder, tandoori masala, roasted besan, ajwain, mustard oil, lemon juice and salt into a thick marinade.
2. Gently fold in paneer, capsicum, onion and tomato. Marinate 1 hour in the fridge.
3. Soak wooden skewers in water for 30 minutes, or use metal skewers.
4. Thread paneer alternately with the vegetables, leaving small gaps.
5. Preheat oven to 220 C. Place skewers on a lined tray and bake 15-18 minutes, turning once, until lightly charred at the edges.
6. Baste with melted butter halfway through. Alternatively cook on a hot grill pan, turning until charred on all sides.
7. Rest 5 minutes, sprinkle with chaat masala and serve hot with mint chutney and onion rings.

title: Vindaloo
ingredients: 800 g boneless chicken or lamb (halal-certified), cut into 4 cm pieces
8 dried Kashmiri red chilies, deseeded and soaked in warm water
instructions:
1. Grind the soaked chilies, garlic, ginger, cumin, peppercorns, mustard seeds, cloves, cinnamon, turmeric, vinegar, sugar and 1 tsp salt into a smooth paste, adding a little water if needed.
2. Coat the meat with the paste and marinate at least 2 hours, preferably overnight in the fridge.
3. Heat oil in a heavy pot and fry onions until deep golden, about 10 minutes.
4. Add the marinated meat with all its paste and sear on high heat 5 minutes, stirring so it does not burn.
5. Add potatoes and hot water, scraping the base clean. Cover and simmer 35-40 minutes until the meat is tender.
6. Uncover and reduce the gravy until thick, dark and glossy with oil floating on top, about 10 minutes.
7. Rest 10 minutes, garnish with coriander and serve with steamed rice or roti. The vinegar delivers the classic tang with no alcohol needed.

title: Naan
ingredients: 1/4 to 1/2 cup warm water as needed
2 tbsp chopped coriander and 4 minced garlic cloves (optional, for garlic naan)
instructions:
1. Mix flour, yeast, sugar and salt in a large bowl. Add warm milk, oil and enough warm water to form a soft, slightly sticky dough.
2. Knead 8-10 minutes until smooth and elastic. Cover and rise 1.5-2 hours until doubled.
3. Punch down and divide into 6 equal balls. Rest 15 minutes.
4. Roll each ball into an oval about 20 cm long and 5 mm thick, dusting lightly with flour.
5. For garlic naan, press minced garlic and coriander gently into the surface.
6. Bake on a preheated pizza stone or baking sheet at the oven maximum, 250 C, for 3-4 minutes until puffed with golden spots, or cook on a very hot tawa flipping once, then char for a few seconds directly over a flame.
7. Brush hot naan with melted butter, stack in a clean cloth and serve warm with curry.

title: Afghan Naan
instructions:
1. Combine both flours, yeast, sugar and salt in a large bowl. Add warm water gradually and knead 10 minutes into a soft, pliable dough.
2. Cover and rise 1.5 hours until puffy.
3. Divide into 4 pieces. Roll each into the classic Afghan oval, about 30 x 15 cm.
4. Dimple the surface all over with your fingertips so it bakes with soft and crisp patches.
5. Brush generously with milk or water and scatter sesame and nigella seeds on top.
6. Bake on a preheated stone at 230 C for 8-10 minutes until golden in patches and lightly crisp.
7. Brush with a little oil or butter, wrap in a cloth and serve warm with kebabs, mantu or tea.

title: Qabili Palaw
ingredients: 800 g lamb shoulder (halal-certified), cut into large pieces
1/2 tsp saffron in 3 tbsp warm water (optional)
instructions:
1. Fry onions in oil in a heavy pot until deep golden, 10-12 minutes.
2. Add lamb and brown on all sides, 6-8 minutes.
3. Add cumin, cardamom, cinnamon, cloves, peppercorns, bay leaves, water and salt. Cover and simmer 60-75 minutes until the lamb is fork-tender.
4. Lift out the lamb, strain the broth and reserve 3.5 cups.
5. Melt ghee in a wide pan, fry carrots 3 minutes, then add raisins and nuts and toast 2 minutes. Remove half for garnish.
6. Dissolve the sugar in the pan until caramelized, pour in a ladle of broth and swirl into a syrup.
7. Add the reserved broth and drained rice to the pot, bring to a boil and cook until the water is absorbed, about 10 minutes.
8. Place the lamb on the rice, scatter the carrot mixture, drizzle saffron water, seal with foil and a lid, and steam on very low heat 25 minutes.
9. Turn out onto a platter, crown with the lamb and reserved nuts, and serve with salad and broth on the side.

title: Mantu
ingredients: For yogurt sauce: 400 g plain yogurt
For meat sauce: 200 g ground beef (halal-certified)
instructions:
1. Knead flour, salt and water into a firm dough. Cover and rest 30 minutes.
2. Mix the filling beef with chopped onions, pepper and salt.
3. For the meat sauce, fry grated onion in 2 tbsp oil until golden, add ground beef and brown well, then stir in tomato paste, turmeric, pepper, salt and 1/2 cup water. Simmer 15 minutes until thick.
4. Whisk yogurt with crushed garlic and salt.
5. Roll the dough into a 2 mm thin sheet and cut into 6 cm squares.
6. Place a teaspoon of filling in each square and pinch opposite corners together to form a four-pointed dumpling, sealing the edges firmly.
7. Arrange mantu in a well-oiled steamer without touching. Steam 25-30 minutes until the dough turns translucent and glossy.
8. Spread half the yogurt on a warm platter, arrange the mantu on top, then spoon over remaining yogurt and the meat sauce.
9. Dust with dried mint and chickpeas and serve immediately.

title: Ashak
ingredients: For filling: 500 g leeks or green onions (or gandana), finely chopped
For yogurt sauce: 500 g plain yogurt
For meat sauce: 300 g ground beef (halal-certified)
Dried mint and coriander leaves, to garnish
instructions:
1. Knead flour, salt and water into a smooth dough and rest 30 minutes.
2. Toss the chopped leeks with oil, salt, pepper and ground coriander for the filling.
3. For the meat sauce, fry onion in oil until golden, add ground beef and brown well, then stir in tomato paste, coriander, pepper, salt and 1/2 cup water. Simmer 15 minutes into a rich sauce.
4. Mix yogurt with garlic and salt.
5. Roll the dough very thin, about 1.5 mm, and cut into 7 cm squares.
6. Place a heaped teaspoon of leek filling on each square, fold into a triangle and press the edges firmly to seal.
7. Boil the ashak in salted water in small batches for 4-5 minutes until they float and the dough is cooked; lift out with a slotted spoon.
8. Layer yogurt on a platter, arrange the hot ashak over it, spoon more yogurt on top and finish with the meat sauce.
9. Sprinkle dried mint and coriander and serve warm.

title: Bolani
ingredients: For filling: 4 medium potatoes, boiled and mashed
instructions:
1. Knead flour, salt, oil and warm water into a soft dough. Cover and rest 1 hour.
2. Mix the mashed potatoes with green onions, coriander, chilies, salt, pepper and ground coriander.
3. Divide the dough into 6 balls. Roll each into a thin 25 cm round.
4. Spread a quarter of the filling over half of each round, fold into a half-moon and press the edge firmly to seal.
5. Heat a generous layer of oil in a wide skillet over medium heat.
6. Fry the bolani 3-4 minutes per side until blistered, crisp and golden in patches, adding more oil as needed.
7. Drain briefly on paper towel and cut into wedges.
8. Stir the dip ingredients together and serve alongside the hot bolani.

title: Shorshe Ilish
ingredients: 4 tbsp mustard seeds (3 tbsp yellow, 1 tbsp black), soaked 30 minutes
instructions:
1. Drain the mustard seeds and grind with 4 green chilies and a splash of water into a fine, slightly grainy paste.
2. Rub the fish steaks with turmeric, chili powder, salt and 2 tbsp of the mustard paste. Rest 15 minutes.
3. Heat mustard oil in a wide pan until it just shimmers; heating it well mellows its sharpness.
4. Sizzle nigella seeds and 6 whole green chilies for a few seconds.
5. Add the remaining mustard paste and a pinch of turmeric; fry 1-2 minutes on low heat until the raw smell disappears.
6. Lay the fish in a single layer, spoon sauce over and add hot water. Cover and simmer 10-12 minutes, turning once, until the fish is cooked and oil rises to the surface.
7. Drizzle 1 tbsp raw mustard oil, rest 5 minutes, garnish with coriander and serve with hot steamed rice.

title: Hilsa Fish Curry
ingredients: 2 medium eggplants, cut into thick wedges
instructions:
1. Rub the fish steaks with 1 tsp turmeric and salt; rest 15 minutes.
2. Heat 4 tbsp mustard oil and fry the eggplant and potato wedges until lightly golden; remove and set aside.
3. Add remaining oil to the pan, sizzle nigella seeds and green chilies.
4. Fry the onion paste 6-8 minutes until golden, then add ginger and garlic pastes and cook 2 minutes.
5. Add chili, cumin and coriander powders with a splash of water; fry 2 minutes.
6. Add tomatoes and cook until they melt into the masala, about 5 minutes.
7. Return the eggplant and potato, pour in hot water and simmer 8 minutes until the vegetables are half-cooked.
8. Slide in the hilsa steaks gently, cover and simmer 10-12 minutes, spooning gravy over without breaking the fish.
9. Adjust salt, finish with coriander and a drizzle of raw mustard oil, and serve with plain steamed rice.

title: Pitha
ingredients: 1 cup grated date palm jaggery or regular jaggery
Muslin cloth or banana leaf, for the steamer
instructions:
1. Bring water to a boil in a wide pot and line a steamer basket with muslin cloth or banana leaf.
2. Mix rice flour with salt and sprinkle 2-3 tbsp water over it; rub with fingertips until the flour is evenly damp and sandy.
3. Sieve the damp flour so it is light and lump-free.
4. Spread half the flour in an even 1 cm layer on the cloth.
5. Scatter jaggery and coconut evenly over the flour layer.
6. Cover with the remaining flour and press very lightly.
7. Cover and steam 12-15 minutes over medium heat until the pitha sets and smells toasty.
8. Cut into wedges, lift carefully and serve warm with extra grated coconut. Best eaten fresh off the steam.

title: Bhuna Khichuri
ingredients: 1 cup basmati or aromatic short-grain rice
Green chilies and coriander leaves, to finish
instructions:
1. Dry roast the moong dal in a pan until fragrant and lightly golden, 4-5 minutes; set aside.
2. Heat ghee in a heavy pot. Add bay leaves, cardamom, cinnamon, cloves and cumin seeds; sizzle 30 seconds.
3. Fry onions until deep golden, 8-10 minutes.
4. Add ginger and garlic pastes, cook 1 minute, then add turmeric, cumin powder, chili powder and salt with a splash of water.
5. Add rice and roasted dal and stir 3-4 minutes to toast and coat in the masala.
6. Add potatoes and cauliflower, pour in hot water and bring to a boil.
7. Cover and simmer 20-25 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the dal and rice are soft and the mixture is thick and glossy. Add hot water for a looser texture if preferred.
8. Rest 10 minutes, top with green chilies and coriander, and serve with fried eggs or beef bhuna.

title: Chomchom
ingredients: 3 tbsp lemon juice diluted in 3 tbsp water
1/2 cup khoya or thickened milk, for stuffing (optional)
instructions:
1. Boil the milk, lower the heat and add the lemon water gradually, stirring until the curds separate completely.
2. Strain through muslin, rinse under cold water and hang 30 minutes to drain into chhana.
3. Knead the chhana with the flour for 8-10 minutes until completely smooth and pliable.
4. Roll into 12 oval cylinders about 5 cm long, tapering the ends.
5. Make the syrup: boil sugar, water and cardamom for 8 minutes until slightly thick.
6. Slide the chomchom into the rolling syrup, cover and boil gently 20-25 minutes; they will swell nearly double. Add hot water if the syrup thickens too much.
7. Cool in the syrup 2 hours, then drain.
8. Split each lengthwise, stuff with a little khoya if using, roll the cut sides in coconut and garnish with pistachios. Chill before serving.

title: Firni
ingredients: 4 tbsp basmati rice, soaked 1 hour (or 4 tbsp rice flour)
instructions:
1. Drain the soaked rice and grind with 2 tbsp milk into a smooth paste.
2. Bring the milk to a boil in a heavy pot, add cardamom and simmer 10 minutes, stirring.
3. Lower the heat and whisk in the rice paste slowly so no lumps form.
4. Cook 20-25 minutes on low heat, stirring often, until thickened and the raw rice taste is gone.
5. Add sugar and cook 5 more minutes until glossy.
6. Stir in saffron, half the nuts and rose water; cook 2 minutes.
7. Pour into small clay bowls, cool to room temperature, then chill 3-4 hours.
8. Serve cold, topped with the remaining nuts.

title: Gulab Jamun
ingredients: 1/4 cup warm milk, approximately, for kneading
Oil or ghee, for deep frying
instructions:
1. Make the syrup first: boil sugar, water and cardamom for 10 minutes until slightly sticky. Add lemon juice and rose water and keep warm on the lowest heat.
2. Mix milk powder, flour, semolina and baking powder. Rub in the melted ghee until crumbly.
3. Add warm milk a spoonful at a time and knead gently into a soft, smooth dough. Do not over-knead.
4. Rest 15 minutes, then roll into 18-20 smooth balls with no cracks.
5. Heat oil to 150 C; the balls must fry slowly so they cook through.
6. Fry in small batches, stirring the oil gently, for 8-10 minutes until deep mahogany brown all over.
7. Lift straight into the warm syrup.
8. Soak at least 2 hours, ideally overnight, until juicy through. Serve at room temperature with pistachios.

title: Rezala
ingredients: 800 g mutton (halal-certified), bone-in pieces, or chicken
2 tbsp poppy seeds, soaked and ground
15 cashew nuts, ground to a paste
instructions:
1. Marinate the meat with yogurt, half the ginger-garlic paste, poppy seed paste, cashew paste, white pepper and salt for 1 hour.
2. Heat ghee in a heavy pot. Add green and black cardamom, cinnamon, cloves and shah jeera; sizzle 30 seconds.
3. Add the marinated meat and cook on medium heat 10 minutes, stirring constantly so the yogurt does not split.
4. Add the remaining ginger-garlic paste and half the fried onions; cook 5 minutes.
5. Add 1 cup hot water, cover and simmer 40-50 minutes until the meat is tender and the gravy turns creamy white.
6. Stir in milk, kewra water and green chilies. Simmer uncovered 10 minutes until the sauce coats a spoon.
7. Crush the remaining fried onions over the top, garnish with coriander and serve with rumali roti, paratha or pulao.

title: Kacchi Biryani (Mutton)
ingredients: 1 kg mutton (halal-certified), leg or shoulder, cut into large pieces
750 g aged basmati rice, soaked 45 minutes
1/2 cup warm milk with a pinch of saffron (or a few drops of orange food colour)
Whole spices for rice: 4 green cardamom pods, 1 cinnamon stick, 4 cloves, 2 bay leaves, 1 tsp shah jeera
Extra fried onions and coriander leaves, to garnish
instructions:
1. Whisk yogurt with ginger and garlic pastes, chili powder, turmeric, salt, white pepper, cardamom, nutmeg and mace powders. Coat the mutton thoroughly and marinate at least 2 hours, overnight is best.
2. Fry the potatoes in oil until deep golden on all sides; set aside.
3. Parboil the soaked rice with the whole spices and salt for exactly 4-5 minutes until 60-70 percent done; drain immediately.
4. In a heavy, wide pot, spread the marinated mutton in an even layer over the base.
5. Arrange the fried potatoes over the meat and scatter half the fried onions.
6. Layer the parboiled rice on top, then the remaining fried onions, saffron milk in patches, kewra water and dots of ghee.
7. Seal the pot with foil or a tight lid. Cook on high heat 10 minutes, then on the lowest heat 50-60 minutes with a tawa under the pot to prevent scorching.
8. Rest sealed for 15 minutes, then open and gently lift the layers so the rice stays fluffy.
9. Garnish with fried onions and coriander and serve hot with borhani, salad and lemon wedges.

title: Chicken Khichuri (Murgir Khichuri)
ingredients: 2 cups chinigura or kalijira aromatic rice, rinsed and drained
1 cup moong dal, dry-roasted until lightly golden
750 g bone-in chicken, cut into 8 pieces
instructions:
1. Heat mustard oil until it just smokes, then lower the heat; fry the sliced onions until deep golden and remove half for garnish.
2. Add bay leaves, cinnamon, cardamom, cloves and cumin seeds to the remaining onions; sizzle for 30 seconds.
3. Rub the chicken with 1 tsp turmeric, 1 tsp chili powder, 1 tsp salt and 1 tbsp each of ginger and garlic paste; rest 15 minutes.
4. Add the chicken to the pot and fry over medium-high heat for 8-10 minutes until browned.
5. Stir in the remaining ginger-garlic paste, turmeric, chili powder and cumin; cook 3 minutes until the oil separates.
6. Add the potato chunks and slit green chilies; toss for 2 minutes.
7. Add the rice and roasted moong dal; stir-fry 3-4 minutes so every grain is coated in spice.
8. Pour in 6 cups hot water and salt; bring to a boil, then cover and simmer 20-25 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the rice is soft and creamy.
9. Adjust with a little hot water for a loose, porridge-like consistency; simmer 5 more minutes.
10. Rest 10 minutes, then top with the reserved fried onions and serve with lemon wedges.

title: Chicken Roast (Kuro-R Roast)
ingredients: 1 kg bone-in chicken (legs and thighs), skin removed
1 cup fried onions (beresta), plus extra to serve
instructions:
1. Prick the chicken all over with a fork; rub with 1 tbsp ginger paste, 1 tbsp garlic paste, the turmeric, 1 tsp chili powder and 1 tsp salt; marinate 1 hour.
2. Whisk the yogurt with the fried onions, remaining ginger-garlic paste, remaining chili powder, cumin, garam masala, nutmeg, mace and sugar into a smooth marinade.
3. Coat the chicken in half the yogurt marinade; rest 30 minutes.
4. Heat the ghee and mustard oil in a heavy pot; add bay leaves, cardamom and cinnamon; sizzle 30 seconds.
5. Sear the chicken pieces over medium-high heat for 5-6 minutes per side until deeply browned; remove and set aside.
6. Add the remaining yogurt marinade to the pot; cook over medium heat 8-10 minutes, stirring, until oil separates at the edges.
7. Return the chicken with any juices; add the slit green chilies and 1/2 cup hot water; cover and simmer 25-30 minutes until tender.
8. Uncover and reduce over medium heat until the gravy is thick, glossy and clings to the chicken.
9. Drizzle with kewra water and rest 10 minutes off the heat.
10. Serve with paratha, polao or naan, topped with extra fried onions.

title: Bun Kabab
ingredients: 1/4 cup chana dal, boiled until soft
1 onion, finely chopped, plus extra rings to serve
instructions:
1. Mash the boiled chana dal; mix with the mince, chopped onion, ginger-garlic paste, green chilies, chili powder, cumin, garam masala, coriander, 1 egg and salt.
2. Knead the mixture well for 5 minutes until smooth and sticky.
3. Shape into 4 round patties; chill 20 minutes to firm up.
4. Shallow-fry the patties in oil over medium heat 4-5 minutes per side until dark brown and cooked through.
5. Beat the remaining 2 eggs; pour thin omelets in the same pan sized to fit the buns.
6. Toast the buns cut-side down in the pan until golden.
7. Spread tamarind chutney on the bottom bun and mint chutney on the top bun.
8. Layer omelet, kabab patty and onion rings; close the bun and press gently.
9. Serve hot with extra chutney.

title: Pakora
instructions:
1. Whisk the gram flour with salt, chili powder, turmeric, cumin seeds and baking soda.
2. Add cold water gradually to make a thick, coating batter; whisk 2 minutes to aerate.
3. Fold in the onions, potatoes, spinach, green chilies and ginger; rest the batter 10 minutes.
4. Heat oil to 175 C (a drop of batter should sizzle and rise).
5. Drop small clumps of batter with vegetables into the oil; do not overcrowd.
6. Fry 4-5 minutes, turning, until golden and crisp.
7. Drain on paper towels.
8. Serve hot with mint chutney or tamarind chutney.

title: Piaju
instructions:
1. Drain the soaked dal; blend with the garlic, ginger and 2 green chilies to a coarse, thick paste using minimal water.
2. Mix in the chopped onion, remaining green chilies, turmeric, chili powder, cumin powder, rice flour, salt and coriander.
3. Rest the mixture 15 minutes.
4. Heat oil to 170-175 C.
5. Shape small flat patties about 5 cm wide with wet hands.
6. Fry 4-5 minutes per side until deep golden and crisp outside, soft inside.
7. Drain on paper towels.
8. Serve hot with mustard sauce or ketchup.

title: Boondi
ingredients: 3/4 cup water, approximately, for the batter
Oil or ghee, for deep frying
Slotted spoon with 5 mm holes (boondi jhara)
instructions:
1. Make the syrup: boil the sugar with 3/4 cup water until it reaches a 1-string consistency, about 8-10 minutes; add cardamom and saffron; keep warm on low heat.
2. Whisk the gram flour with water gradually to a smooth, thick pouring batter; add the baking soda; rest 10 minutes.
3. Heat oil to 170 C.
4. Hold the perforated spoon above the oil; pour a ladle of batter through it so small drops fall into the oil.
5. Fry the boondi 1-2 minutes until pale golden, stirring gently; do not let them brown.
6. Lift with a slotted spoon and drop straight into the warm syrup.
7. Repeat until all the batter is used.
8. Mix in the melon seeds, raisins and nuts.
9. Let the boondi soak 20-30 minutes, tossing occasionally, until moist but separate.
10. Serve warm or at room temperature.

title: Falooda
ingredients: 2 tbsp falooda sev (or thin vermicelli), boiled 3 minutes and drained
1 tbsp basil seeds (tukmaria), soaked in 1/2 cup water for 20 minutes
2 tbsp chopped jelly cubes (any halal flavor)
2 scoops vanilla or kulfi ice cream
1 tbsp dried rose petals, to garnish (optional)
instructions:
1. Boil the falooda sev 3 minutes until just soft; drain and rinse under cold water.
2. Soak the basil seeds in water 20 minutes until swollen; drain.
3. Whisk the chilled milk with the rose syrup.
4. In two tall glasses, layer the sev, basil seeds and jelly cubes.
5. Pour the rose milk over to fill the glasses three-quarters full.
6. Top each glass with a scoop of ice cream.
7. Garnish with pistachios, almonds and rose petals.
8. Serve immediately with a long spoon and straw.

title: Lassi
ingredients: 2 tbsp chopped pistachios and almonds, to garnish
instructions:
1. Combine the yogurt, milk, sugar and cardamom in a blender.
2. Blend 1-2 minutes until smooth and frothy.
3. Add the ice cubes and blend briefly until crushed and mixed.
4. Pour into chilled glasses.
5. Garnish with the nuts and saffron.
6. Serve immediately. For salted lassi, replace the sugar with 1/2 tsp salt, 1/2 tsp roasted cumin powder and a few mint leaves.

title: Chai (Masala Tea)
ingredients: 2 tsp loose black tea leaves (or 2 tea bags)
instructions:
1. In a saucepan, bring the water to a boil with the ginger, cardamom, cinnamon, cloves and pepper.
2. Boil the spices 3-4 minutes so the water is well infused.
3. Add the tea leaves and simmer 2 minutes until the water turns deep amber.
4. Add the milk and simmer 3-4 minutes, letting it rise and froth; stir gently.
5. Strain into cups through a fine sieve.
6. Serve hot with biscuits or rusk.

title: Borhani
ingredients: 1 tsp yellow mustard seeds, ground fine
instructions:
1. Whisk the yogurt until completely smooth with no lumps.
2. Add the chilled water gradually, whisking to a thin, pourable consistency.
3. Mix the ground mustard with 1 tbsp water to a paste; stir into the yogurt.
4. Add the roasted cumin, black salt, regular salt, sugar and garlic paste; whisk well.
5. Stir in the green chilies, mint and coriander.
6. Chill 30 minutes so the flavors develop.
7. Whisk again before serving.
8. Serve cold over ice, traditionally alongside biryani or tehari.

title: Jorda (Mihi Dani)
ingredients: 2 cups chinigura or kalijira aromatic rice, rinsed and drained
1/4 tsp orange food color or a few saffron strands
instructions:
1. Heat the ghee in a heavy pot; fry the almonds and cashews until golden; remove and set aside.
2. Add the bay leaves, cardamom and cinnamon to the ghee; sizzle 30 seconds.
3. Add the drained rice and fry over medium heat 5-6 minutes until glossy and nutty.
4. Add 3 cups water mixed with the food color (or saffron) and salt; bring to a boil.
5. Cover and cook on low heat 12-15 minutes until the rice is tender and the water is absorbed.
6. Sprinkle the sugar evenly over the rice; cover and steam on the lowest heat 10 minutes so the sugar melts into a light syrup.
7. Gently fold in the crumbled khoya, raisins and fried nuts.
8. Turn off the heat and keep covered 10 minutes.
9. Fluff with a fork; top with mihi dana and grated coconut.
10. Serve warm as a celebration dessert.

title: Halwa
instructions:
1. Heat the ghee in a heavy pan; fry the nuts, melon seeds and raisins until golden; remove and set aside.
2. Add the semolina to the same ghee; roast over medium-low heat 10-12 minutes, stirring constantly, until golden and nutty.
3. Meanwhile warm the milk with the sugar and cardamom until the sugar dissolves; keep hot.
4. Carefully pour the hot milk into the roasted semolina (it will bubble), stirring continuously.
5. Cook over low heat 5-7 minutes, stirring, until the halwa thickens and leaves the sides of the pan.
6. Stir in half the fried nuts and raisins.
7. Rest covered 5 minutes; the halwa will loosen slightly.
8. Serve warm, garnished with the remaining nuts.

title: Tandoori Chicken
ingredients: 1 kg chicken (4 leg quarters, or 1 whole chicken cut into 8), skin removed
3 deep slits cut into each piece
1 tbsp tandoori masala or garam masala
Lemon wedges and onion rings, to serve
instructions:
1. Rub the chicken with the lemon juice and 1 tsp salt; rest 20 minutes.
2. Mix the yogurt with the ginger-garlic paste, chili powder, turmeric, coriander, tandoori masala, mustard oil and remaining salt into a smooth marinade.
3. Coat the chicken thoroughly, pushing marinade into the slits; marinate at least 4 hours, ideally overnight.
4. Preheat the oven to 220 C (or a grill to medium-high).
5. Place the chicken on a rack over a tray; brush lightly with oil.
6. Roast 25-30 minutes, turning once, until charred in spots and cooked through (internal temperature 74 C).
7. Optional: finish 2-3 minutes under the broiler for extra char.
8. Rest 5 minutes; sprinkle with chaat masala and coriander.
9. Serve hot with lemon wedges, onion rings and mint chutney.

title: Seekh Kebab (Beef)
ingredients: 750 g beef mince with about 20 percent fat
1 small onion, grated and squeezed dry
2 tbsp gram flour, dry-roasted until nutty
Metal skewers, or wooden skewers soaked 30 minutes
instructions:
1. Mix the mince with all ingredients except the oil; knead vigorously 8-10 minutes until smooth and sticky.
2. Cover and refrigerate 1 hour to firm up.
3. Preheat the grill or oven to 220 C.
4. With wet hands, mold handfuls of the mixture onto skewers, pressing into long, even cylinders.
5. Brush the kebabs lightly with oil.
6. Grill 12-15 minutes, turning every 3-4 minutes, until browned on all sides and cooked through.
7. Rest 3 minutes, then slide off the skewers.
8. Serve hot with mint chutney, sliced onions and lemon, or wrapped in paratha.

title: Fish Pakora
ingredients: 500 g firm white fish fillets (basa, cod or tilapia), cut into strips
Lemon wedges and mint chutney, to serve
instructions:
1. Rub the fish strips with the lemon juice, 1/2 tsp turmeric, 1/2 tsp chili powder and 1/2 tsp salt; rest 15 minutes.
2. Whisk the gram flour, rice flour, carom seeds, remaining turmeric and chili powder, ginger-garlic paste, green chili, coriander, baking soda and remaining salt.
3. Add cold water gradually to make a thick, coating batter.
4. Heat oil to 175 C.
5. Dip the fish strips in the batter, letting excess drip off.
6. Fry in batches 3-4 minutes until golden and crisp; drain on paper towels.
7. Optional: fry a second time for 1 minute for extra crunch.
8. Serve hot with lemon wedges and mint chutney.

title: Sharwarma
ingredients: 1 kg boneless chicken thighs (or beef sirloin), thinly sliced
1 cup tahini sauce (tahini whisked with lemon juice, garlic and water)
instructions:
1. Whisk the yogurt, lemon juice, olive oil, garlic, all the spices and salt into a marinade.
2. Coat the sliced chicken well; marinate at least 2 hours, overnight is best.
3. Sear the strips in batches over high heat in a wide pan 6-8 minutes until browned and cooked through, or grill until charred at the edges.
4. Rest the meat 5 minutes, then chop finer if desired.
5. Warm the flatbreads on a dry pan.
6. Spread tahini sauce over each bread.
7. Layer the meat, tomatoes, cucumbers and pickles.
8. Roll tightly into wraps; toast seam-side down on the pan 1-2 minutes until crisp.
9. Slice in half and serve with extra tahini sauce.

title: Tehari
ingredients: 500g chinigura or kalijeera rice, washed and soaked 30 minutes
2 bay leaves, 1 cinnamon stick, 6 cardamom pods, 6 cloves, 1 tsp whole cumin
instructions:
1. Marinate the beef with ginger-garlic paste, turmeric, chili powder, yogurt, and salt for 30 minutes.
2. Heat mustard oil to smoking point, lower the heat, and fry the onions until golden.
3. Add the whole spices and bay leaves, then the marinated beef; fry on high heat 8-10 minutes until browned.
4. Add cumin and coriander powders and sugar; pour in 1 cup hot water, cover, and cook 40-45 minutes until the beef is tender.
5. Add the soaked rice and stir gently for 3-4 minutes so every grain is coated in oil and masala.
6. Add hot water (about 1.5 times the rice), salt, and the green chilies; bring to a boil.
7. Cover and cook on low heat 15-18 minutes until the rice is done and liquid is absorbed.
8. Sprinkle garam masala and give dum on the lowest heat for 10 minutes.
9. Serve hot with beef rezala, egg curry, or chutney.

title: Morog Polao
ingredients: 1 whole chicken (about 1 kg), cut into 8 bone-in pieces
500g chinigura rice, washed and soaked 30 minutes
1 cinnamon stick, 4 cardamom pods, 4 cloves, 2 bay leaves, 1 tsp shahi jeera
instructions:
1. Marinate the chicken with yogurt, ginger-garlic paste, turmeric, chili powder, and salt for 1 hour.
2. Heat ghee and fry the onions until golden; remove half for garnish.
3. Add the whole spices, then the marinated chicken; fry on high heat about 8 minutes until sealed and lightly browned.
4. Add the potatoes, sugar, and 1/2 cup water; cover and cook 10 minutes until the chicken is 80 percent done.
5. Add the soaked rice and stir gently for 3 minutes to coat in the masala.
6. Add hot water and salt; bring to a boil and add the green chilies.
7. Cover and cook on low heat 15 minutes until the rice absorbs the liquid.
8. Pour the milk over the top, sprinkle garam masala and the reserved fried onions; give dum 10 minutes on a tawa over the lowest heat.
9. Serve warm with borhani or a simple salad.

title: Beef Polao
ingredients: 500g kalijeera or chinigura rice, washed and soaked 30 minutes
2 bay leaves, 1 cinnamon stick, 6 cardamom pods, 6 cloves, 1 tsp shahi jeera
instructions:
1. Marinate the beef with ginger-garlic paste, turmeric, chili powder, yogurt, and salt for 1 hour.
2. Heat oil and fry the onions until deep golden; add the whole spices and bay leaves.
3. Add the marinated beef and bhuna on high heat 10-12 minutes until browned and the oil separates.
4. Add cumin and coriander powders, sugar, and 1 cup hot water; cover and cook 45 minutes until the beef is tender.
5. Add the soaked rice and stir gently for 3-4 minutes on medium heat.
6. Add 3 cups hot water and salt; bring to a rolling boil.
7. Cover and cook on low heat 15-18 minutes until the rice is fluffy and the liquid is absorbed.
8. Add the green chilies and garam masala; give dum 10 minutes on a tawa over the lowest heat.
9. Fluff gently and serve with raita, salad, or chutney.

title: Murgir Jhal Fry
ingredients: 2 bay leaves, 3 cardamom pods, 3 cloves, 1 cinnamon stick
instructions:
1. Marinate the chicken with ginger-garlic paste, turmeric, 1 tsp chili powder, lemon juice, and salt for 30 minutes.
2. Heat mustard oil and fry the onions until deep golden.
3. Add the whole spices and bay leaves, then the chicken; fry on high heat 8-10 minutes until browned.
4. Add the remaining chili powder, cumin, and coriander powders; stir 2 minutes.
5. Lower the heat and add the whisked yogurt slowly, stirring constantly for 3-4 minutes.
6. Add 1/2 cup hot water, cover, and cook 15 minutes until the chicken is tender and oil rises to the surface.
7. Add the green chilies and garam masala; simmer uncovered 3 minutes for a thick, fiery jhal gravy.
8. Rest 5 minutes and serve hot with plain rice, paratha, or ruti.

title: Kosha Mangsho
ingredients: 2 bay leaves, 4 cardamom pods, 4 cloves, 1 cinnamon stick
instructions:
1. Marinate the mutton with yogurt, ginger-garlic paste, turmeric, 1 tsp chili powder, and salt for 1-2 hours.
2. Heat mustard oil and fry the potatoes until golden; remove and set aside.
3. Fry the onions in the same oil until deep golden brown; add the bay leaves and whole spices.
4. Add the marinated mutton and bhuna on high heat 12-15 minutes until the oil separates.
5. Add cumin, coriander, and the remaining chili powder along with sugar; keep frying 5 minutes.
6. Pour in 1 cup hot water, cover, and cook on low heat 45-50 minutes until the mutton is tender.
7. Return the fried potatoes and cook 10 more minutes until the gravy is thick and glossy.
8. Sprinkle garam masala and rest 5 minutes.
9. Serve hot with luchi, paratha, or steamed rice.

title: Daab Chingri
ingredients: 1 large tender green coconut (daab) with 1-2 cups coconut water inside
2 tbsp mustard seeds, soaked 30 minutes and ground with 2 green chilies
3 tbsp grated coconut flesh from the daab
instructions:
1. Cut open the top of the tender coconut, pour out and reserve the coconut water, and scoop out some soft flesh.
2. Marinate the prawns with the mustard paste, turmeric, sugar, salt, chopped onion, mustard oil, and a few green chilies for 20 minutes.
3. Mix the grated coconut flesh into the marinated prawns.
4. Pour the prawn mixture back into the empty daab shell.
5. Pour the reserved coconut water over the prawns, filling no more than three-quarters.
6. Seal the opening with the coconut top fixed with dough or foil.
7. Steam the sealed daab in a large pot with 2 inches of water for 25-30 minutes.
8. Rest 5 minutes and break the seal at the table.
9. Eat the prawns straight from the daab with steamed rice.

title: Macher Jhol
ingredients: 6 pieces rui or katla fish steaks (about 700g)
1 tsp turmeric powder plus extra for the fish
instructions:
1. Rub the fish with turmeric and salt; rest 15 minutes.
2. Shallow fry the fish in mustard oil until light golden on both sides; remove.
3. Fry the potato wedges in the same oil until the edges brown; remove.
4. Temper the nigella seeds and bay leaves; add tomato, ginger paste, turmeric, chili, cumin, and coriander powders; bhuna until the oil separates.
5. Add water and salt; bring to a boil and return the fried potatoes; simmer 5 minutes.
6. Slip in the fried fish and green chilies; simmer 5-6 minutes so the jhol stays light and pourable.
7. Adjust salt and consistency; the gravy should be thin, not thick.
8. Garnish with coriander and serve with steamed rice.

title: Rui Machher Kalia
ingredients: 2 bay leaves, 4 cardamom pods, 4 cloves, 1 cinnamon stick
instructions:
1. Rub the fish with turmeric and salt; shallow fry until golden and set aside.
2. In the same oil, temper the bay leaves and whole spices.
3. Fry the onion paste until deep golden and the oil separates, about 8-10 minutes.
4. Add the ginger-garlic pastes and fry 2 minutes.
5. Beat in the yogurt with chili, cumin, and turmeric powders; bhuna on medium heat 6-8 minutes until the masala is glossy.
6. Add 1 cup water, salt, and sugar; simmer 5 minutes into a rich gravy.
7. Gently slide in the fried fish and spoon gravy over; cook covered on low heat 6-8 minutes.
8. Add the green chilies and garam masala; rest 5 minutes.
9. Serve with gobindobhog rice or plain steamed rice.

title: Ilish Macher Paturi
ingredients: 4 tbsp yellow mustard seeds, soaked 30 minutes
4 green chilies (for the paste) plus 6 slit
instructions:
1. Wash the hilsa pieces and rub with turmeric, salt, and half the mustard oil; rest 15 minutes.
2. Grind the soaked mustard seeds with 4 green chilies and a little water into a smooth paste.
3. Mix the mustard paste, poppy seed paste, coconut, remaining oil, and salt; coat each fish piece thickly.
4. Wilt the banana leaves over a low flame so they fold without cracking.
5. Place one fish piece with 2 green chilies on each leaf, fold into a parcel, and tie with string.
6. Steam the parcels in a steamer over medium heat for 20-25 minutes.
7. Rest 5 minutes and open the parcels at the table.
8. Serve hot with steamed rice so the mustard oil coats the grains.

title: Doi Maach
ingredients: 2 bay leaves, 4 cardamom pods, 1 cinnamon stick
instructions:
1. Rub the fish with turmeric and salt; shallow fry lightly and set aside.
2. Fry the onions in the same oil until golden; add the bay leaf and whole spices.
3. Add the ginger-garlic pastes and fry 2 minutes.
4. Lower the heat and add the whisked yogurt gradually with chili and cumin powders, stirring so it does not split.
5. Bhuna 6-8 minutes until oil beads appear on the masala.
6. Add 1/2 cup water, salt, and sugar; simmer 4 minutes.
7. Gently place the fish in the gravy and spoon the doi sauce over; cook covered on low heat 8 minutes.
8. Add the green chilies and garam masala; rest 5 minutes.
9. Serve with steamed rice.

title: Sorshe Chingri
ingredients: 4 tbsp mustard seeds, soaked 30 minutes and ground with 3 green chilies
instructions:
1. Marinate the prawns with turmeric, salt, and 2 tbsp of the mustard paste for 15 minutes.
2. Heat mustard oil to smoking point, lower the heat, and splutter the nigella seeds.
3. Add the prawns and fry on high heat 3-4 minutes until they turn opaque and curl.
4. Dissolve the remaining mustard paste and poppy seed paste in 1/2 cup water and add to the pan.
5. Add salt, sugar, and the slit green chilies; simmer 4-5 minutes until the gravy thickens slightly.
6. Drizzle 1 tsp raw mustard oil on top for sharpness.
7. Rest 5 minutes off the heat.
8. Serve hot with steamed rice.

title: Chingri Macher Malai Curry
ingredients: 500g large prawns (bagda or tiger prawns preferred)
2 green cardamom pods, 2 cloves, 1 cinnamon stick, 2 bay leaves
instructions:
1. Marinate the prawns with turmeric and salt for 15 minutes; shallow fry briefly, 2 minutes per side, and remove.
2. Heat ghee and temper the bay leaves and whole spices.
3. Fry the onion paste until light golden.
4. Add the ginger paste, turmeric, and chili powder; bhuna 3-4 minutes.
5. Add the coconut milk, water, salt, and sugar; simmer on low heat 5 minutes so it does not split.
6. Slip in the prawns and cook only 4-5 minutes so they stay juicy.
7. Add the slit green chilies and rest 5 minutes.
8. Serve with steamed rice or polao.

title: Shukto
ingredients: 1 bitter gourd (ucche or korola), thinly sliced
instructions:
1. Fry the bori in mustard oil until puffed and golden; remove.
2. Fry the bitter gourd slices with a pinch of salt until browned; remove to soften the bitterness.
3. In the remaining oil, splutter the panch phoron and bay leaves.
4. Add the raw banana, potato, sweet potato, drumstick, and beans; fry with turmeric for 5 minutes.
5. Add 1 cup water, salt, and sugar; cover and cook 10-12 minutes until the vegetables are tender.
6. Stir in the mustard paste and milk; simmer 3-4 minutes until the gravy is creamy and coats the vegetables.
7. Return the bitter gourd and bori; mix gently.
8. Finish with a spoon of ghee and rest 2 minutes.
9. Serve first, in traditional Bengali order, with steamed rice.

title: Aloo Posto
ingredients: 4 tbsp white poppy seeds (posto), soaked 30 minutes
2 green chilies (for grinding with the posto)
instructions:
1. Grind the soaked poppy seeds with 2 green chilies and minimal water into a smooth paste.
2. Heat mustard oil and splutter the nigella seeds.
3. Add the potatoes with turmeric and salt; fry 5-6 minutes until the edges soften.
4. Add the poppy seed paste and stir-fry 3-4 minutes until the raw smell disappears and the paste coats the potatoes.
5. Add 1/2 cup water and sugar; cover and cook on low heat 8-10 minutes until the potatoes are done with a thick posto coating.
6. Add the slit green chilies.
7. Drizzle 1 tsp raw mustard oil on top.
8. Rest 2 minutes and serve with steamed rice and dal.

title: Dhokar Dalna
ingredients: 1 tsp ginger paste (for the cakes) plus 1 tbsp for the gravy
1/2 tsp turmeric powder plus 1 tsp for the gravy
1 tsp sugar plus 1 tsp for the gravy
2 tbsp ghee (for the cakes) plus 1 tbsp to finish
instructions:
1. Grind the soaked chana dal coarsely with coconut, ginger paste, green chilies, and minimal water.
2. Heat ghee and cook the paste with turmeric, sugar, and salt, stirring 10-12 minutes until very thick and it leaves the pan sides.
3. Spread on a greased plate about 1.5 cm thick; cool and set for 30 minutes, then cut into diamonds.
4. Shallow fry the diamonds until golden on both sides; set aside.
5. For the gravy, heat mustard oil and splutter cumin seeds and bay leaves.
6. Add ginger paste, cumin powder, coriander powder, turmeric, and chili powder with a splash of water; bhuna 2-3 minutes.
7. Add 1.5 cups water, salt, and sugar; simmer 5 minutes into a medium gravy.
8. Slide in the fried dhokar and simmer gently 5-6 minutes so they absorb the gravy without breaking.
9. Finish with ghee and garam masala; serve with luchi or rice.

title: Mochar Ghonto
ingredients: 2 cups banana blossom (mocha), chopped, boiled and mashed
instructions:
1. Remove the outer bracts and hard stems of the banana blossom; chop finely, boil with turmeric and salt until soft, then drain and mash.
2. Fry the bori in mustard oil until golden; remove and set aside.
3. Fry the potato cubes in the same oil until browned; remove.
4. Splutter the panch phoron; add ginger paste and green chilies.
5. Add the mashed mocha with turmeric and cumin powder; bhuna 6-8 minutes on medium heat, stirring often.
6. Return the potato, add coconut, sugar, and salt; cook 5 more minutes until dry with a ghonto (mash) texture.
7. Crush the fried bori coarsely over the ghonto and mix.
8. Finish with ghee and garam masala.
9. Serve with steamed rice and dal.

title: Kopi Dalna
ingredients: 1 medium cauliflower, broken into medium florets
instructions:
1. Soak the cauliflower florets in salted turmeric water for 10 minutes; drain well.
2. Fry the florets and potatoes in oil until light golden; remove.
3. Splutter cumin seeds and bay leaves in the remaining oil.
4. Add ginger paste, turmeric, cumin powder, and chili powder with a splash of water; bhuna 2 minutes.
5. Add 1.5 cups water, salt, and sugar; bring to a simmer.
6. Return the cauliflower and potatoes; cover and cook 10-12 minutes until tender.
7. Keep the gravy light and pourable, as dalna should be; adjust consistency.
8. Finish with ghee and garam masala.
9. Serve with steamed rice or roti.

title: Pabda Macher Jhal
ingredients: 1 tsp turmeric powder plus extra for the fish
instructions:
1. Rub the pabda lightly with turmeric and salt; rest 10 minutes.
2. Heat mustard oil and fry the fish very gently, 2 minutes per side, as pabda is delicate; remove carefully.
3. Splutter the nigella seeds; add tomato, ginger-free jhal base of turmeric, chili, and cumin powders; bhuna until the oil separates.
4. Add 1 cup water and salt; simmer 3 minutes.
5. Return the fish gently and spoon the gravy over; cook 5-6 minutes on low heat without stirring much.
6. Add the green chilies and simmer 2 minutes.
7. Garnish with coriander and rest 2 minutes.
8. Serve hot with steamed rice.

title: Pangash Bhuna
ingredients: 1 tsp turmeric powder plus extra for the fish
2 bay leaves, 3 cardamom pods, 3 cloves, 1 cinnamon stick
