instructions:
1. Rub the fish with turmeric, a pinch of chili powder, and salt; rest 15 minutes.
2. Shallow fry the fish until golden on both sides; remove.
3. Fry the onions in the same oil until deep golden; add the whole spices and bay leaves.
4. Add the ginger-garlic pastes and fry 2 minutes.
5. Add chili, cumin, and coriander powders with a splash of water; bhuna until the oil separates.
6. Add 1/2 cup water and simmer 3 minutes into a thick gravy.
7. Return the fish and coat with the gravy; cook covered on low heat 6-8 minutes.
8. Add the green chilies and garam masala; rest 5 minutes.
9. Serve with ruti, paratha, or rice.

title: Murgi Musallam
ingredients: 1 whole chicken (1.2-1.5 kg), cleaned, skin on
2 bay leaves, 1 cinnamon stick, 4 cardamom pods, 4 cloves
instructions:
1. Marinate the whole chicken inside and out with yogurt, ginger-garlic paste, turmeric, 1 tsp chili powder, and salt for 2 hours.
2. For the stuffing, fry the chopped onions in ghee; add the keema with cumin, chili powder, and salt; cook until dry, then fold in the halved boiled eggs and cool.
3. Fill the cavity with the stuffing and sew or skewer it closed; tie the legs together.
4. Heat the remaining ghee and brown the chicken carefully on all sides.
5. Remove the chicken; in the same pot fry the sliced onions with bay leaf and whole spices until golden.
6. Add the remaining chili and coriander powders and 1 cup water; simmer 5 minutes into a gravy.
7. Place the chicken in the gravy, cover, and cook on low heat 40-45 minutes, turning once and basting often.
8. Uncover and raise the heat to reduce the gravy until it coats the chicken; sprinkle garam masala.
9. Rest 10 minutes, carve at the table to reveal the stuffing, and serve with polao or paratha.

title: Chotpoti
ingredients: 2 cups dried white peas (matar), soaked overnight and boiled until soft
Fresh coriander and mint leaves, chopped
instructions:
1. Boil the soaked white peas until soft but not mushy; drain.
2. Mix the tamarind pulp with 1 cup water, jaggery, salt, and a pinch of chili powder to make the sour tok pour.
3. Toss the warm peas with mustard oil, salt, and half the roasted cumin.
4. Add the diced potatoes and eggs; mix gently.
5. Stir in the onion, cucumber, green chilies, and half the coriander and mint.
6. Pour the tamarind tok over and mix lightly, reserving some for topping.
7. Sprinkle chaat masala, the remaining cumin, and chili powder on top.
8. Serve in bowls topped with extra tok, coriander, and crushed papri if desired.

title: Jhal Muri
ingredients: 2 tbsp tamarind pulp or 1 tbsp lemon juice
instructions:
1. In a large bowl, combine the onion, tomato, green chilies, potato, and coconut slivers.
2. Add mustard oil, tamarind pulp, and salt; mix well.
3. Add the roasted cumin, chaat masala, and chili powder.
4. Just before serving, add the puffed rice and chanachur.
5. Toss quickly with both hands or a large spoon so the muri stays crisp.
6. Taste and adjust the sour, salty, and spicy balance.
7. Finish with coriander and an extra drizzle of mustard oil.
8. Serve immediately in paper cones or bowls before it softens.

title: Muri Ghonto
ingredients: 1/2 cup gobindobhog or kalijeera rice, washed
1 tsp turmeric powder plus extra for the fish head
2 bay leaves, 4 cardamom pods, 4 cloves, 1 cinnamon stick
instructions:
1. Rub the fish head with turmeric and salt; fry in mustard oil until deep golden on both sides, break into chunks, and remove.
2. Fry the potato cubes lightly in the same oil; remove.
3. Fry the onions until golden; add the whole spices and bay leaves.
4. Add the ginger-garlic pastes, chili powder, and cumin powder; bhuna 3 minutes.
5. Return the fish head pieces and fry 3-4 minutes so the masala coats them.
6. Add the washed rice and stir 2-3 minutes to toast lightly.
7. Pour in hot water, add salt, cover, and cook on low heat 15-18 minutes until the rice is done and the liquid is absorbed.
8. Add the green chilies and garam masala; give dum 5 minutes.
9. Serve hot as a side with plain steamed rice and dal.

title: Mutton Rogan Josh
instructions:
1. Heat oil until lightly smoking, lower the heat and add bay leaves, cardamom, cloves, cinnamon and shah jeera; let them crackle.
2. Add mutton and sear on high heat for 8-10 minutes until browned on all sides.
3. Add garlic paste and salt and saute 2 minutes.
4. Dissolve Kashmiri chili powder in 1/2 cup water and add to the pot; cook until the oil turns deep red.
5. Lower the heat and add whisked yogurt gradually, stirring constantly so it does not split.
6. Add 2 cups hot water, cover and simmer 1.5 hours until the mutton is tender (or pressure cook 30-40 minutes).
7. Stir in fennel powder and dry ginger powder and simmer uncovered 10 minutes until the gravy is glossy with oil floating on top.
8. Sprinkle garam masala, rest 10 minutes and serve with steamed rice or roti.

title: Goat Curry
ingredients: Fresh coriander leaves and ginger juliennes to garnish
instructions:
1. Fry onions in oil until deep golden; remove half for garnish.
2. Add cumin, bay leaves, cardamom, cloves, cinnamon and peppercorns to the oil, then add goat meat and sear 8 minutes.
3. Add ginger-garlic paste and cook 2 minutes.
4. Add coriander, chili powder, turmeric and salt and stir well.
5. Add yogurt gradually on medium heat and bhunofy (fry) 8-10 minutes.
6. Add tomatoes and cook until soft and oil separates from the masala.
7. Add 2 cups hot water and pressure cook 35-40 minutes (or simmer covered 1.5 hours) until the goat is tender.
8. Uncover, reduce the gravy to your liking, add garam masala and green chilies.
9. Garnish with reserved fried onions, ginger juliennes and coriander; serve with naan or rice.

title: Chicken Chettinad
instructions:
1. Dry roast the red chilies, coriander seeds, fennel, cumin, peppercorns, star anise, kalpasi and poppy seeds until aromatic.
2. Add grated coconut and roast until golden; cool and grind with a little water into a smooth paste.
3. Heat sesame oil, crackle fennel seeds and add curry leaves.
4. Saute onions until golden, then add ginger-garlic paste and cook 2 minutes.
5. Add chicken and turmeric and sear on high heat 5 minutes.
6. Add tomatoes and cook until soft and mushy.
7. Add the ground Chettinad masala paste and fry 5-6 minutes until oil separates.
8. Add 1 cup water and salt, cover and simmer 20-25 minutes until the chicken is tender.
9. Garnish with coriander leaves and serve hot with rice, parotta or dosa.

title: Kerala Chicken Curry
instructions:
1. Heat coconut oil and crackle mustard seeds with a few curry leaves.
2. Saute onions until golden brown.
3. Add ginger paste, garlic paste and green chilies and cook 2 minutes.
4. Lower the heat and add turmeric, chili powder, coriander powder and pepper; fry 30 seconds.
5. Add tomato and cook until soft.
6. Add chicken and salt and sear 5 minutes on high heat.
7. Pour in thin coconut milk, cover and simmer 20 minutes until the chicken is cooked.
8. Add thick coconut milk and heat gently 3-4 minutes without boiling.
9. Rest 10 minutes, garnish with curry leaves and coriander and serve with appam, puttu or rice.

title: Hyderabadi Chicken Biryani
ingredients: 2 tsp biryani masala or garam masala
1/2 tsp saffron soaked in 1/4 cup warm milk
instructions:
1. Whisk yogurt with ginger-garlic paste, chili powder, turmeric, biryani masala, salt, half the fried onions and half the herbs; add chicken and marinate 4 hours or overnight.
2. Boil 3 litres water with bay leaves, cardamom, cloves, cinnamon, star anise, shah jeera and salt.
3. Add soaked rice and cook until 70 percent done (grain should break with slight resistance); drain well.
4. In a heavy-bottomed pot, spread the marinated chicken evenly at the bottom.
5. Layer half the parboiled rice over the chicken; sprinkle fried onions, mint, coriander, kewra water, half the saffron milk and 2 tbsp ghee.
6. Add the remaining rice and top with remaining saffron milk, ghee and herbs.
7. Seal the pot with foil and a tight lid; cook on high heat 5 minutes, then on the lowest heat (dum) 35-40 minutes.
8. Rest 10 minutes before opening, then gently fluff the layers.
9. Serve hot with mirchi ka salan and raita.

title: Lucknowi Mutton Biryani
ingredients: 1/2 tsp saffron soaked in 1/4 cup warm milk
instructions:
1. Marinate mutton with yogurt, ginger-garlic paste, red chili powder, half the garam masala, salt and half the fried onions for 4 hours.
2. Cook the marinated mutton with 1 cup water on low heat until tender and the gravy is thick (pressure cook 30-40 minutes if needed).
3. Boil water with bay leaves, cardamom, cloves, cinnamon, shah jeera and salt.
4. Add rice and parboil to 70 percent done; drain.
5. In a heavy pot, spread the cooked mutton with its thick gravy at the bottom.
6. Layer the parboiled rice over the mutton.
7. Top with saffron milk, kewra water, ghee, remaining fried onions and fresh herbs.
8. Seal the pot and cook on dum (lowest heat) for 30-35 minutes.
9. Rest 10 minutes, gently fluff and serve with raita and salad.

title: Kolkata Mutton Biryani
ingredients: 2 tsp biryani masala or garam masala
1/2 tsp saffron soaked in 1/4 cup warm milk
instructions:
1. Marinate mutton with yogurt, ginger-garlic paste, red chili powder, nutmeg, mace, biryani masala, salt and half the fried onions for 4 hours or overnight.
2. Cook the marinated mutton with a little water until tender and the gravy is thick (pressure cook 30-40 minutes).
3. Fry potato quarters in ghee until golden on all sides; boil eggs if using.
4. Parboil the soaked rice in salted water with bay leaves, cardamom, cloves and cinnamon until 70 percent done; drain.
5. In a heavy pot, layer the cooked mutton with its gravy, then the fried potatoes and eggs.
6. Cover with the parboiled rice.
7. Top with saffron milk, kewra water, remaining ghee and fried onions.
8. Seal the pot and cook on dum (lowest heat) 35-40 minutes.
9. Rest 10 minutes, fluff gently and serve with raita and salad.

title: Ambur Chicken Biryani
ingredients: 600 g seeraga samba rice (or basmati), washed and soaked 20 minutes
10 dry red chilies, soaked in warm water
instructions:
1. Grind the soaked red chilies with ginger and garlic into a smooth paste.
2. Marinate chicken with half the paste, curd, turmeric and salt for 1 hour.
3. Heat oil and ghee in a heavy pot; add bay leaf, cardamom, cloves, cinnamon and star anise.
4. Saute onions until golden, add tomatoes and cook until soft, then add the remaining chili paste and fry until oil separates.
5. Add the marinated chicken and cook 10 minutes on high heat.
6. Add mint and coriander leaves, then pour in 1.2 litres hot water; bring to a boil and check salt.
7. Add the soaked rice and cook on medium heat until the water is almost absorbed.
8. Cover tightly and cook on dum (lowest heat) 15 minutes until the rice is fluffy and done.
9. Rest 10 minutes, fluff gently, squeeze lemon over the top and serve with brinjal curry or raita.

title: Malabar Fish Curry
ingredients: 750 g kingfish or seer fish steaks
3 pieces kudampuli (Malabar tamarind), soaked in warm water
instructions:
1. Soak the kudampuli in 1/2 cup warm water for 15 minutes.
2. Heat coconut oil and crackle mustard seeds and fenugreek seeds.
3. Saute shallots, ginger, garlic, green chilies and curry leaves until soft.
4. Lower the heat and add chili powder, coriander powder and turmeric; fry briefly without burning.
5. Add the thin coconut milk along with the kudampuli and its soaking water; bring to a gentle boil.
6. Slide in the fish steaks and simmer uncovered 10-12 minutes, spooning the gravy over the fish.
7. Add thick coconut milk and heat through without letting it boil hard.
8. Finish with fresh curry leaves and a drizzle of coconut oil; rest 15 minutes before serving with steamed red rice.

title: Kerala Fish Molly
instructions:
1. Marinate the fish with turmeric, salt and lemon juice for 15 minutes.
2. Shallow fry the fish lightly in coconut oil, 2 minutes per side; set aside.
3. In the same oil crackle mustard seeds.
4. Saute onions until translucent, then add ginger, garlic, green chilies and curry leaves.
5. Add turmeric and black pepper and fry 30 seconds.
6. Pour in the thin coconut milk and simmer 5 minutes.
7. Gently add the fried fish and cook on low heat 8-10 minutes.
8. Add the thick coconut milk and tilt the pan to mix instead of stirring; heat 3 minutes.
9. Finish with curry leaves and a drizzle of coconut oil and serve with appam or bread.

title: Fish Amritsari
ingredients: 700 g boneless fish fillets (basa or surmai), cut into 2 inch pieces
Chaat masala, lemon wedges and onion rings to serve
instructions:
1. Marinate the fish with lemon juice, salt, ginger-garlic paste, red chili powder and turmeric for 20 minutes.
2. Whisk besan, rice flour, yogurt, ajwain, Kashmiri chili powder, garam masala, baking soda, salt and enough water into a thick batter; rest 10 minutes.
3. Heat oil to 180 C for deep frying.
4. Coat each fish piece in the batter.
5. Deep fry in batches until golden and crisp; drain on paper towels.
6. Fry all pieces a second time for 1 minute for extra crispness.
7. Sprinkle chaat masala over the hot fish and serve immediately with green chutney, lemon wedges and onion rings.

title: Tandoori Pomfret
ingredients: 2 whole pomfret (about 500 g each), cleaned and scored
Chaat masala, lemon wedges and onion rings to serve
instructions:
1. Rub the fish with lemon juice and salt, including inside the scores; rest 15 minutes.
2. Mix yogurt, ginger-garlic paste, Kashmiri chili powder, garam masala, ajwain, roasted besan, mustard oil and salt into a thick marinade.
3. Coat the fish thoroughly inside and out with the marinade.
4. Refrigerate 1-2 hours to absorb the flavours.
5. Preheat the oven to 220 C and place the fish on a greased rack over a tray.
6. Grill 15 minutes, baste with butter, then flip and grill 12-15 minutes more.
7. Char under the broiler 2-3 minutes for smoky edges.
8. Sprinkle chaat masala and serve hot with lemon wedges and onion rings.

title: Prawn Balchao
ingredients: 10-12 dried Kashmiri red chilies, soaked in warm water
instructions:
1. Rub the prawns with salt and turmeric and rest 15 minutes.
2. Pan-fry the prawns 2-3 minutes until just pink; set aside.
3. Grind the soaked chilies, garlic, ginger, mustard seeds and cumin with the vinegar into a smooth paste.
4. Heat oil and fry the sliced garlic until golden.
5. Saute the onion until light brown.
6. Add the ground paste and fry 8-10 minutes until the oil separates and the raw smell disappears.
7. Add tomatoes, sugar and salt and cook until mushy.
8. Return the prawns with green chilies and cook 8-10 minutes until the masala clings to them and oil floats on top.
9. Cool completely, pack into a sterilized glass jar and refrigerate 2 days for the flavours to mature before serving as a pickle-style side with rice.

title: Goan Fish Curry
ingredients: Marble-sized ball of tamarind (or 1 tbsp tamarind pulp)
instructions:
1. Grind the coconut, red chilies, coriander seeds, cumin, peppercorns, turmeric, tamarind, garlic and green chili with a little water into a fine paste.
2. Heat coconut oil and saute the shallots until golden.
3. Add the ground paste and fry 5-6 minutes until the oil separates.
4. Add 2 cups water and simmer 10 minutes to cook the masala.
5. Season with salt and adjust the sourness to taste.
6. Slide in the fish steaks and simmer gently 8-10 minutes without boiling hard.
7. Rest 10 minutes and serve hot with steamed rice.

title: Dhaba Chicken
ingredients: Fresh coriander leaves and lemon wedges to serve
instructions:
1. Heat oil and crackle cumin seeds, bay leaves, cardamom, cloves and cinnamon.
2. Fry the onions until deep golden brown.
3. Add the chicken and sear on high heat 5-6 minutes.
4. Add ginger-garlic paste and cook 2 minutes.
5. Add coriander powder, chili powder, turmeric and salt, then stir in the yogurt gradually and bhunofy 5 minutes.
6. Add the tomatoes and cook 10-12 minutes until mushy and oil separates.
7. Add 1 cup hot water, cover and cook 20-25 minutes until the chicken is tender.
8. Crush kasuri methi between your palms and add with garam masala and green chilies; simmer 3 minutes.
9. Garnish with coriander and lemon and serve with tandoori roti or paratha.

title: Chicken 65
ingredients: 600 g boneless chicken, cut into 1.5 inch pieces
Fresh coriander and lemon wedges to serve
instructions:
1. Marinate the chicken with yogurt, ginger-garlic paste, red chili powder, turmeric, garam masala, lemon juice and salt for 1 hour.
2. Add the egg, corn flour and rice flour and mix until every piece is well coated.
3. Heat oil to 180 C and deep fry the chicken in batches until crisp and cooked through; drain.
4. Heat 2 tbsp oil and crackle the mustard seeds.
5. Add curry leaves and green chilies and fry until the leaves are crisp.
6. Sprinkle in the Kashmiri chili powder.
7. Toss the fried chicken in this tempering until evenly coated.
8. Squeeze lemon over the top, garnish with coriander and serve hot with onion rings.

title: Chicken Korma
ingredients: 1 tbsp poppy seeds, soaked in warm water
instructions:
1. Fry the onions in ghee until deep golden; remove half and grind it with the cashews and poppy seeds using a little water.
2. In the same pot add cardamom, cloves, cinnamon, bay leaf and shah jeera, then add the chicken and sear 5 minutes.
3. Add ginger-garlic paste and cook 2 minutes.
4. Lower the heat and add yogurt gradually along with coriander powder, chili powder, turmeric and salt; bhunofy 8 minutes.
5. Add the fried onion and nut paste and cook 5 minutes until the oil glistens on top.
6. Add 1 cup hot water, cover and simmer 20-25 minutes until the chicken is tender and the gravy is creamy.
7. Stir in garam masala, kewra water and cream and simmer 3 minutes.
8. Garnish with coriander and serve with sheermal, naan or rice.

title: Mughlai Chicken
ingredients: Few saffron strands soaked in 2 tbsp warm milk (optional)
instructions:
1. Grind the soaked almonds, cashews and melon seeds with a little water into a smooth paste.
2. Heat ghee and fry the onions until golden; add cardamom, cloves, cinnamon and bay leaf.
3. Add the chicken and sear on high heat 5 minutes.
4. Add ginger-garlic paste and cook 2 minutes.
5. Add yogurt along with coriander powder, chili powder, turmeric and salt; bhunofy until oil separates.
6. Add the nut paste and cook 5 minutes on low heat.
7. Add 1 cup hot water, cover and simmer 25 minutes until the chicken is tender.
8. Stir in cream, saffron milk, nutmeg and garam masala; simmer 3 minutes.
9. Garnish with coriander and serve with naan or paratha.

title: Mutter Mushroom
instructions:
1. Saute the mushrooms in butter on high heat until their water dries and the edges brown; set aside.
2. Heat oil and crackle cumin seeds.
3. Fry the onions until golden, then add ginger-garlic paste and cook 1 minute.
4. Add tomato puree, coriander powder, chili powder and turmeric and cook until oil separates.
5. Add peas and 1/2 cup water and cook 5 minutes.
6. Return the mushrooms to the pan and simmer 8 minutes.
7. Crush and add kasuri methi along with garam masala and cream; simmer 2 minutes.
8. Garnish with coriander and serve with roti or rice.

title: Chana Saag
ingredients: 2 cups cooked chickpeas (or 400 g can, drained)
1 tsp amchur powder or 1 tbsp lemon juice
instructions:
1. Heat oil and crackle cumin seeds.
2. Fry the onion until golden brown.
3. Add ginger-garlic paste, tomatoes, coriander powder, chili powder, turmeric and salt; cook until soft and oil separates.
4. Add the chickpeas with 1/2 cup water and simmer 10 minutes, mashing a few chickpeas to thicken the gravy.
5. Add the chopped spinach and cook 6-8 minutes until wilted and blended in.
6. Add garam masala and amchur and simmer 2 minutes.
7. Garnish with coriander and serve with roti, paratha or rice.

title: Baingan Bharta
ingredients: 3 tbsp mustard oil (or any cooking oil)
instructions:
1. Rub the eggplants with a little oil and roast over an open flame or at 220 C in the oven, turning often, until the skin is charred and the flesh is soft (25-30 minutes).
2. Cool, peel off the skin and mash the flesh coarsely.
3. Heat oil and crackle cumin seeds.
4. Fry the onions until golden, then add ginger-garlic paste and green chilies.
5. Add tomatoes, chili powder, turmeric, coriander powder and salt; cook until soft and mushy.
6. Add the mashed eggplant and roast on medium heat 10-12 minutes, stirring often.
7. Add garam masala and coriander leaves and mix 2 minutes.
8. Serve hot with roti, paratha or dal and rice.

title: Bharli Vangi
ingredients: 2 tbsp goda masala (or 1 tbsp garam masala plus 1/2 tsp cinnamon powder)
instructions:
1. Slit each brinjal into quarters from the base without separating the pieces; soak in salted water 10 minutes.
2. Mix crushed peanuts, sesame seeds, coconut, goda masala, chili powder, turmeric, coriander powder, jaggery, tamarind pulp, chopped onion, salt, half the coriander and 2 tbsp oil into a thick stuffing.
3. Stuff the mixture carefully into the brinjals and reserve any leftover masala.
4. Heat oil in a wide pan and crackle mustard seeds with hing.
5. Place the stuffed brinjals in a single layer and saute gently 5 minutes, turning carefully.
6. Add the reserved masala and 1 cup water, then cover.
7. Cook on medium-low heat 20-25 minutes until the brinjals are tender and oil floats on the gravy.
8. Garnish with coriander and serve with bhakri, chapati or steamed rice.

title: Gatte Ki Sabji
instructions:
1. Mix 1 cup besan with ajwain, cumin, chili powder, turmeric, garam masala, hing, 2 tbsp oil, salt and enough water to knead a stiff dough.
2. Roll the dough into thin finger-sized cylinders (gatte).
3. Boil the gatte in salted water 8-10 minutes until they float and are cooked; drain, reserving the water.
4. Cut the boiled gatte into 1 cm pieces.
5. Heat ghee and crackle cumin seeds with hing.
6. Lower the heat and add the whisked yogurt mixed with 2 tbsp besan, coriander powder, chili powder, turmeric and salt, stirring constantly so it does not split.
7. Cook 6-8 minutes until the gravy thickens and oil appears on the sides.
8. Add the gatte pieces with 1/2 cup of the reserved boiling water and simmer 8-10 minutes.
9. Crush and add kasuri methi with garam masala, garnish with coriander and serve with bajra roti or steamed rice.

title: Kande Pohe
ingredients: 1 large potato, peeled and diced small
2 tbsp fresh grated coconut and chopped coriander to garnish
instructions:
1. Place poha in a colander and rinse under running water for 30 seconds; drain completely, sprinkle salt and sugar, and set aside to soften for 10 minutes.
2. Heat oil in a kadhai and fry peanuts until golden; remove and keep aside.
3. In the same oil, add mustard seeds; once they pop, add curry leaves, green chilies and chopped onions; saute until translucent.
4. Add diced potato with 3 tbsp water, cover and cook 8-10 minutes until tender.
5. Sprinkle turmeric and a little salt; stir well.
6. Gently fold in the softened poha, cover and steam on low heat for 3-4 minutes.
7. Add lemon juice and fluff with a fork; mix in fried peanuts.
8. Garnish with coconut, coriander and sev; serve hot with lemon wedges.

title: Ker Sangria
instructions:
1. Wash ker and sangri thoroughly and soak overnight (8 hours) in plenty of water.
2. Pressure cook the soaked ker-sangri with 2 cups water and a pinch of salt for 3-4 whistles until tender; drain.
3. Heat mustard oil until it just smokes, then lower the heat and add cumin and fenugreek seeds.
4. Add the cooked ker-sangri along with turmeric, chili powder and coriander powder; saute 3-4 minutes.
5. Add 1/2 cup water and simmer 8-10 minutes until the mixture is almost dry.
6. Stir in amchur, jaggery and salt; cook 2-3 minutes until glossy and well coated.
7. Rest the curry 5 minutes so the flavors meld.
8. Serve warm with bajra roti and a glass of buttermilk.

title: Panchratna Dal
ingredients: Chopped coriander and lemon wedges to serve
instructions:
1. Wash all five dals together and soak for 20 minutes.
2. Pressure cook the dals with turmeric, salt and 3.5 cups water for 4-5 whistles until very soft; mash lightly.
3. Heat ghee in a pan; add cumin seeds, dried red chilies and asafoetida.
4. Add chopped onion and saute until golden, then add ginger-garlic paste and cook 1 minute.
5. Add tomatoes with coriander, cumin, chili powder and garam masala; cook until the ghee separates.
6. Pour the tadka into the cooked dal and simmer 10 minutes, adding hot water to reach a pouring consistency.
7. Stir in cream and simmer 2 more minutes; adjust salt.
8. Garnish with coriander and a squeeze of lemon; serve hot with steamed rice or roti.

title: Shami Kabab
ingredients: 4 cloves, 4 green cardamom, 1 cinnamon stick, 1 bay leaf
instructions:
1. Combine mince, chana dal, sliced onion, whole spices, chili powder, salt and water in a pot.
2. Cook covered on medium heat 40-45 minutes until the dal is soft and all water is absorbed; cool completely.
3. Grind the mixture to a smooth, thick paste without adding water.
4. Mix in chopped green chilies and fresh coriander.
5. Shape into flat round patties about 8 cm wide.
6. Dip each patty in beaten egg and coat lightly with breadcrumbs.
7. Shallow fry on medium heat 3-4 minutes per side until golden and heated through.
8. Serve hot with mint chutney and onion rings.

title: Gola Kabab
instructions:
1. Rub the raw papaya paste into the mince and rest 30 minutes to tenderize.
2. Add all remaining ingredients and knead 8-10 minutes until very smooth and sticky.
3. Cover and marinate in the refrigerator at least 4 hours.
4. Shape the mince into round balls (gola) around skewers, or roll into golf-ball sized spheres.
5. Grill over charcoal or bake at 200 C, or pan-fry, turning often, for 12-15 minutes until browned and cooked through.
6. Baste with melted butter or oil during cooking.
7. Optionally smoke with a hot charcoal piece for 2 minutes.
8. Serve hot with mint chutney and naan.

title: Malai Boti
ingredients: 600 g chicken breast or thigh, boneless cubes
instructions:
1. Whisk yogurt, cream, cheese, ginger-garlic paste, all spices, lemon juice, oil and salt into a smooth marinade.
2. Add the chicken cubes and coat thoroughly.
3. Cover and marinate 4-6 hours, preferably overnight, in the refrigerator.
4. Thread the cubes onto skewers, leaving small gaps.
5. Grill over charcoal or bake at 220 C for 15-18 minutes, turning and basting with melted butter.
6. Char the edges 2-3 minutes at the end over high heat.
7. Rest 2 minutes off the heat.
8. Serve hot with mint chutney, onion rings and lemon.

title: Chicken Tikka Boti
ingredients: 1 tsp chaat masala, plus extra to finish
instructions:
1. Whisk yogurt, ginger-garlic paste, all spices, lemon juice, oil, food color and salt into a marinade.
2. Add chicken cubes and coat well.
3. Cover and marinate 4 hours or overnight in the refrigerator.
4. If using wooden skewers, soak them in water 30 minutes.
5. Grill over charcoal or bake at 220 C for 15-18 minutes, turning and basting with oil.
6. Finish 2-3 minutes over high heat for light charring.
7. Sprinkle chaat masala over the hot boti.
8. Rest 2 minutes and serve with mint chutney, naan and salad.

title: Beef Kebab Masala
instructions:
1. Mix beef mince with besan, egg, cumin, coriander, chili powder and salt; shape into 10-12 small flat patties.
2. Shallow fry the patties on medium heat until browned on both sides; set aside.
3. In the same pan, heat 3 tbsp oil, add cumin seeds and sliced onions; fry until golden.
4. Add ginger-garlic paste and saute 1 minute.
5. Add tomato puree, turmeric and salt; bhunofy until the masala thickens and oil separates.
6. Lower the heat and stir in the whisked yogurt gradually; cook 3-4 minutes.
7. Add 1 cup hot water and simmer 10 minutes to a thick gravy, then slide in the kebabs and simmer gently 10 minutes on low.
8. Garnish with green chilies and coriander; serve with naan or steamed rice.

title: Chicken Walnut
ingredients: 3/4 cup walnut halves, soaked in warm water 30 minutes
instructions:
1. Soak walnuts in warm water for 30 minutes and rub off any loose skins.
2. Heat oil or ghee in a heavy pan and temper cardamom, cloves, cinnamon and bay leaf.
3. Add chicken pieces and sear 5 minutes until lightly browned.
4. Whisk the yogurt with fennel powder, ginger powder, turmeric, Kashmiri chili and salt.
5. Lower the heat and add the yogurt mixture gradually, stirring constantly to prevent curdling.
6. Add 1.5 cups water, cover and simmer 20 minutes.
7. Add the walnuts and simmer 10-12 more minutes until the gravy turns creamy and the chicken is cooked through.
8. Serve hot with steamed rice.

title: Mutton Karahi
instructions:
1. Heat oil in a karahi and add cumin seeds.
2. Sear the mutton on high heat 6-8 minutes until well browned.
3. Add ginger-garlic paste and saute 2 minutes.
4. Add 1 cup water and salt; pressure cook 25-30 minutes (or simmer covered 1.5 hours) until tender.
5. Return to high heat, add tomatoes and chili powder; cover and cook 15 minutes until the tomatoes collapse.
6. Bhunofy on high heat until the oil separates from the masala.
7. Add crushed black pepper, green chilies and julienned ginger; toss 2 minutes.
8. Garnish with fresh coriander and serve with naan.

title: Charga
ingredients: 1 tsp chaat masala, plus extra to finish
instructions:
1. Prick the chicken all over with a fork and make deep slits on the legs and breast.
2. Mix yogurt, ginger-garlic paste, vinegar, lemon juice, all spices and salt into a marinade.
3. Rub the marinade all over and inside the chicken; marinate 6-8 hours or overnight in the refrigerator.
4. Steam the chicken in a steamer or covered pot with 2 cm of water for 25-30 minutes until partially cooked; cool and pat dry.
5. Brush with the reserved marinade mixed with a little oil.
6. Heat oil to 170 C in a deep wok.
7. Deep fry the chicken 12-15 minutes, turning carefully, until deep golden and cooked through (internal temperature 74 C).
8. Drain, sprinkle with chaat masala and lemon juice; serve with raita and naan.

title: Brain Masala
ingredients: Fresh coriander and julienned ginger to garnish
instructions:
1. Remove all membranes from the brains and soak in salted water for 20 minutes.
2. Boil the brains in water with turmeric and a little salt for 8-10 minutes until firm; drain and cut into chunks.
3. Heat oil in a pan, add cumin seeds and chopped onion; fry until golden.
4. Add ginger-garlic paste and saute 1 minute.
5. Add tomatoes with red chili, coriander and turmeric powders; cook until the masala thickens and oil separates.
6. Add green chilies and salt.
7. Gently fold in the brain chunks and cook 5 minutes on low heat, tossing carefully so they hold their shape.
8. Garnish with coriander and ginger juliennes; serve hot with naan or paratha.

title: Kaleji Masala
ingredients: 500 g mutton or chicken liver, cleaned and cubed
Fresh coriander, ginger juliennes and lemon to finish
instructions:
1. Soak the liver in milk for 20 minutes to remove bitterness; drain and pat dry.
2. Heat oil and fry onions until golden brown.
3. Add cumin seeds and ginger-garlic paste; saute 1 minute.
4. Add tomatoes with chili, coriander and turmeric powders; bhunofy until oil separates.
5. Lower the heat and stir in the whisked yogurt; cook 3-4 minutes to a thick masala.
6. Add the liver and sear on high heat 2 minutes, then cover and cook on medium 8-10 minutes only, so it stays tender.
7. Add green chilies, black pepper and garam masala; toss 2 minutes on high.
8. Garnish with coriander, ginger and a squeeze of lemon; serve hot with naan.

title: Maghaz Fry
instructions:
1. Clean the brains, removing all membranes, and soak in salted water 20 minutes.
2. Boil in water with turmeric and a little salt for 8-10 minutes until just firm; drain and cut into pieces.
3. Heat ghee in a frying pan and fry the onions until deep golden.
4. Add cumin seeds and green chilies.
5. Add the brain pieces carefully and fry on medium heat 5-6 minutes, turning gently.
6. Sprinkle chili flakes, black pepper, garam masala, kasuri methi and salt over the pieces.
7. Fry 3-4 more minutes until the edges are lightly crisp.
8. Finish with lemon juice and coriander; serve hot with paratha.

title: Pyaz-Gosht
instructions:
1. Fry the sliced onions in oil until deep golden; remove half and set aside.
2. In the remaining oil and onions, add cardamom, cloves, cinnamon and bay leaf.
3. Add the meat and sear on high heat 6-8 minutes until browned.
4. Add ginger-garlic paste and salt; saute 2 minutes.
5. Add coriander, cumin, chili powder and turmeric with a splash of water; bhunofy 5 minutes.
6. Pour in 2 cups water; pressure cook 30-35 minutes (or simmer covered 1.5 hours) until tender.
7. Uncover, add the reserved fried onions and green chilies; simmer 10 minutes until the gravy thickens and oil rises.
8. Garnish with fresh coriander and serve with roti or naan.

title: Machli ka Salan
ingredients: 750 g firm fish steaks (pomfret, kingfish or tilapia)
1 tsp turmeric powder plus extra for rubbing
1/2 cup tamarind pulp or 2 tbsp lemon juice
instructions:
1. Rub the fish with turmeric and salt; rest 15 minutes.
2. Shallow fry the fish 2-3 minutes per side until lightly golden; set aside gently.
3. In the same pan, add cumin seeds and the onions; fry until golden.
4. Add ginger-garlic paste, then tomatoes with coriander powder, chili powder and cumin powder; cook until the masala thickens and oil separates.
5. Add 2 cups water and simmer 10 minutes to a medium gravy.
6. Stir in tamarind pulp or lemon juice; adjust salt.
7. Slide the fish into the gravy and simmer 6-8 minutes on low, spooning gravy over the fish without stirring hard.
8. Garnish with green chilies and coriander; rest 10 minutes and serve with steamed rice.

title: Peshawari Chicken Karahi
ingredients: 1 kg bone-in chicken, cut into 12 pieces
2-inch piece ginger, cut into fine juliennes
instructions:
1. Heat oil in a heavy karahi or wok over medium-high heat.
2. Add chicken pieces and saute for 5-6 minutes until no longer pink on the outside.
3. Stir in ginger and garlic pastes and cook for 2 minutes.
4. Add chopped tomatoes and salt, cover, and cook on medium heat for 15-20 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the tomatoes collapse into a thick masala.
5. Pick out and discard the loosened tomato skins, then increase heat to high and bhunai (fry) the masala for 8-10 minutes until oil separates at the edges.
6. Add crushed cumin, coriander seeds and black pepper; mix well.
7. Add slit green chillies and half the ginger juliennes; simmer uncovered for 5-7 minutes until chicken is fully cooked and the gravy clings to the pieces.
8. Garnish with remaining ginger and fresh coriander; serve hot with naan or roghni naan.

title: Memoni Biryani
ingredients: 750 g bone-in chicken, cut into 8 pieces
3 medium potatoes, quartered and fried until golden
1 cup mint leaves and 1/2 cup coriander leaves, chopped
2 bay leaves, 6 cloves, 4 green cardamoms, 1 cinnamon stick, 1 tsp cumin seeds (for rice)
instructions:
1. Fry sliced onions in ghee until deep golden; remove half as birista and set aside.
2. In the same pot, add chicken, ginger-garlic paste and all powdered spices; bhunai on high heat for 5 minutes.
3. Add yogurt, tomatoes, green chillies, mint and coriander; cook on medium for 10 minutes until the tomatoes break down.
4. Add 1 cup hot water, cover, and cook the chicken until tender, 20-25 minutes; stir in fried potatoes and garam masala.
5. Meanwhile boil the rice in salted water with bay leaf, cloves, cardamom, cinnamon and cumin until 80 percent done; drain.
6. Layer the chicken masala in a heavy pot, top with rice, birista, kewra and dots of food colour.
7. Seal with a tight lid or foil and steam on very low heat (dum) for 20 minutes.
8. Rest 5 minutes, fluff gently, and serve with raita and salad.

title: Bohri Biryani
ingredients: 750 g bone-in beef, cut into 2-inch pieces
2 bay leaves, 6 cloves, 4 green cardamoms, 1 cinnamon stick (for rice)
1 pinch saffron soaked in 2 tbsp warm milk (optional)
instructions:
1. Fry the onions in ghee until deep golden; remove half as birista.
2. Add beef to the pot with ginger-garlic paste and the powdered spices; bhunai on high heat for 6-8 minutes.
3. Add yogurt, 2 cups hot water and salt; pressure cook or simmer covered until the beef is tender, 45-60 minutes.
4. Add potatoes, dried plums, green chillies, mint and garam masala; cook 10 minutes until the potatoes are just done.
5. Parboil the rice with bay leaf, cloves, cardamom and cinnamon until 80 percent cooked; drain.
6. Layer the rice over the beef masala; top with birista, kewra and saffron milk.
7. Seal and steam on the lowest heat (dum) for 20-25 minutes.
8. Rest 5 minutes, fluff, and serve with plain yogurt or raita, as Bohri biryani is traditionally eaten with cool yogurt to balance the heat.

title: Shinwari Karahi
ingredients: 1 kg mutton (leg or shoulder), bone-in, cut into large pieces
100 g mutton tail fat, diced (or 100 ml oil)
instructions:
1. Heat a heavy karahi over medium-high heat; render the diced fat until it melts and turns golden, or heat the oil.
2. Add mutton pieces and sear for 6-8 minutes until browned on all sides.
3. Add ginger-garlic paste and 1 cup hot water; cover and cook on medium-low until the meat is tender, 45-60 minutes (pressure cook 25 minutes to save time).
4. Uncover and increase the heat; add tomatoes and salt and cook, stirring, until they soften and break down, 12-15 minutes.
5. Press out the tomato skins and continue frying on high heat until the masala thickens and oil rises, 8-10 minutes.
6. Stir in the crushed black pepper and coriander seeds.
7. Add green chillies and ginger juliennes; toss for 3-4 minutes on a high flame.
8. Garnish with fresh coriander and serve immediately with hot naan, as Shinwari karahi relies only on meat, fat, pepper and tomato.

title: Kunna
ingredients: 1 kg mutton, bone-in, cut into large pieces
4 black cardamoms, 6 green cardamoms, 8 cloves, 2 cinnamon sticks, 2 bay leaves, 1 mace blade, 1 tsp cumin seeds, 1 tsp black peppercorns
Flour-and-water dough, to seal the pot
2-inch piece ginger, julienned, and 4 green chillies, to garnish
instructions:
1. Heat ghee in a heavy clay pot (kunna) or Dutch oven; fry the onions until deep golden.
2. Add mutton and sear on high heat for 8 minutes until browned.
3. Add ginger-garlic paste, whole spices and powdered spices; stir for 3 minutes until fragrant.
4. Lower the heat and add yogurt a spoonful at a time, stirring constantly so it does not split; bhunai for 8-10 minutes until oil separates.
5. Pour in hot water and salt; bring to a boil.
6. Seal the lid completely with flour dough to trap the steam.
7. Cook on the lowest possible heat (dum) for 2.5-3 hours without opening, or bake at 150 degrees C for 3 hours.
8. Break the seal at the table, garnish with ginger juliennes and green chillies, and serve with sheermal or naan.

title: Mutton Pulao
ingredients: 750 g bone-in mutton, cut into medium pieces
2 bay leaves, 1 cinnamon stick, 6 cloves, 6 green cardamoms, 1 black cardamom, 1 tsp cumin seeds, 1 tsp black cumin (shahi zeera), 1 tsp black peppercorns
instructions:
1. Heat ghee in a heavy pot; fry the onions until deep golden brown.
2. Add mutton and bhunai on high heat for 6-8 minutes until sealed and browned.
3. Stir in ginger-garlic paste, chilli powder, coriander powder and salt; cook 3 minutes.
4. Add yogurt and cook on medium for 8-10 minutes until the masala thickens and oil separates.
5. Add the whole spices and 4.5 cups hot water; cover and cook until the mutton is tender, 50-60 minutes (pressure cook 30 minutes).
6. Taste the yakhni and adjust salt; it should be slightly saltier than needed since the rice will absorb it.
7. Add the soaked rice and green chillies; stir once, bring to a boil, then cover and cook on low for 10 minutes.
8. Steam on dum with a tight lid on the lowest heat for 10 more minutes; rest 5 minutes, fluff, garnish with coriander, and serve with raita.

title: Chicken Pulao
ingredients: 800 g bone-in chicken, cut into 8 pieces
2 bay leaves, 1 cinnamon stick, 6 cloves, 6 green cardamoms, 1 tsp cumin seeds, 1 tsp black cumin, 1 tsp black peppercorns
2 tbsp chopped coriander and mint, to garnish
instructions:
1. Heat ghee in a heavy pot; fry the onions until deep golden.
2. Add chicken and sear on high heat for 5 minutes until sealed.
3. Add ginger-garlic paste, powdered spices and salt; bhunai for 4-5 minutes.
4. Add yogurt and cook 6-8 minutes until oil separates; add potato cubes if using.
5. Add the whole spices and 4 cups hot water; simmer 15 minutes until the chicken is nearly cooked.
6. Add the soaked rice and green chillies; stir once and bring to a rolling boil.
7. Cover and cook on low heat for 10 minutes, then dum with a sealed lid on the lowest heat for 10 more minutes.
8. Rest 5 minutes, fluff gently, garnish with coriander and mint, and serve with raita or chutney.

title: Beef Yakhni Pulao
ingredients: 750 g bone-in beef, cut into medium pieces
1 tbsp fennel seeds, 1 tbsp coriander seeds, 1 tbsp cumin seeds, 2 bay leaves, 1 cinnamon stick, 8 cloves, 8 green cardamoms, 2 black cardamoms, 1 tbsp black peppercorns (for yakhni)
instructions:
1. Boil the beef with quartered onions, yakhni spices, ginger-garlic paste and 5 cups water until tender, 60-75 minutes, skimming the scum.
2. Strain, reserving the stock (yakhni) and beef separately; you need about 4.5 cups stock, so top up with water if short.
3. Heat ghee in a heavy pot; fry the sliced onions until deep golden.
4. Add the boiled beef and bhunai for 5 minutes; stir in garam masala and salt.
5. Pour in the hot yakhni and bring to a boil; it should taste slightly salty.
6. Add the soaked rice; stir once and cook until the water is absorbed to surface level.
7. Sprinkle kewra and green chillies, cover tightly, and steam on the lowest heat (dum) for 20 minutes.
8. Rest 5-10 minutes, fluff gently, garnish with coriander, and serve with raita and salad.

title: Katakat
ingredients: 500 g mixed mutton offal (kidneys, liver and brain), cleaned and cut into chunks
instructions:
1. Heat a heavy tawa or wide iron griddle over medium-high heat and add the oil.
2. Add chopped onions and fry until light golden, 4-5 minutes.
3. Add the offal pieces and ginger-garlic paste; using a heavy katakat chopper or sturdy spatula, chop and crush the pieces while they sear, 8-10 minutes.
4. Sprinkle in chilli powder, coriander, turmeric, cumin and salt; keep chopping and mixing so the spices coat everything.
5. Add tomatoes and yogurt; continue the chopping motion as the tomatoes melt into the masala, 10-12 minutes.
6. Keep working the mixture on the tawa until it is dry, sizzling and the oil separates, another 8-10 minutes.
7. Stir in garam masala, green chillies and half the ginger.
8. Garnish with coriander, remaining ginger and lemon; serve hot with naan or paratha.

title: Kebab Roll
ingredients: 500 g beef mince with some fat
1 small onion, grated and squeezed dry
For parathas: 2 cups all-purpose flour, 1/2 tsp salt, 2 tbsp oil, about 3/4 cup warm water, extra oil for frying
Mint-coriander chutney: 1 cup coriander, 1/2 cup mint, 2 green chillies, 1 tsp cumin, salt, 2 tbsp yogurt, lemon juice
instructions:
1. Knead the paratha dough with flour, salt, oil and warm water; rest 30 minutes.
2. Mix the mince with onion, ginger-garlic paste, chillies, coriander, spices, salt and toasted besan; rest in the fridge for 30 minutes.
3. Blend the chutney ingredients smooth and set aside.
4. Shape the mince around 4 skewers as long seekh kebabs, or form thick fingers by hand.
5. Cook the kebabs on a grill pan or under the broiler, turning, until browned and cooked through, 12-15 minutes, basting with a little oil.
6. Roll the dough into 4 thin ovals and cook on a hot tawa with oil until golden spots form on both sides.
7. Place a kebab on each paratha, top with chutney, onion rings and a squeeze of lemon.
8. Roll tightly, wrap the bottom half in foil or paper, and serve immediately.

title: Ash-e Reshteh
ingredients: 1/2 cup cooked green or brown lentils
2 cups mixed chopped herbs (parsley, coriander, dill)
1/2 cup kashk (or thick yogurt or sour cream)
3 tbsp oil, plus extra for frying mint
instructions:
1. Fry the sliced onion in oil until deep golden; remove half for garnish.
2. Add garlic and turmeric to the pot; stir 1 minute until fragrant.
3. Add tomato paste and fry 2 minutes until it darkens.
4. Add the herbs, green onions and all the cooked beans and lentils; stir 3 minutes.
5. Pour in the water, salt and pepper; simmer covered for 30 minutes, stirring occasionally.
6. Add the noodles and cook 8-10 minutes, stirring often, until soft and the soup is thick.
7. Stir in most of the kashk and adjust salt; simmer 5 more minutes.
8. Serve in bowls swirled with extra kashk, topped with the fried onions and dried mint crisped for 30 seconds in hot oil.

title: Afghan Kebab
ingredients: 800 g lamb mince with fat (leg or shoulder)
1 medium onion, grated and squeezed very dry
Sliced onion, tomato and cucumber, to serve
Sumac and lemon wedges, to serve
instructions:
1. Knead the mince with onion, garlic, salt, pepper, coriander, cumin and cold water for 5-8 minutes until sticky and smooth.
2. Cover and refrigerate for at least 1 hour so the mixture firms up.
3. Soak wooden skewers in water for 30 minutes if using.
4. With wet hands, press handfuls of mince onto each skewer into a long, even kebab, pressing a ridge down the middle.
5. Grill over charcoal or a hot grill pan for 10-12 minutes, turning every few minutes, until browned outside and juicy inside.
6. In the last minute, hold a naan over the grill to warm and smoke it.
7. Rest the kebabs 2 minutes, then slide them off onto the naan.
8. Shower with sumac, add the salad and lemon, and squeeze over before eating.

title: Kofta-e Kebab
ingredients: 1 small onion, grated and squeezed dry
For the sauce: 1 onion finely chopped, 3 cloves garlic minced, 2 tbsp oil, 1 tsp turmeric, 1 tsp coriander powder, 2 cups tomato passata, 1 tsp salt, 1/2 tsp chilli flakes
Naan or chalaw (white rice), to serve
instructions:
1. Knead the beef with onion, garlic, spices, salt and coriander for 5 minutes until smooth; rest 30 minutes.
2. Shape into 12 small flattened patties with wet hands.
3. Heat oil in a wide pan; brown the kofta on both sides, 2-3 minutes per side, then remove.
4. In the same pan, fry the onion until golden; add garlic, turmeric and coriander powder.
5. Add tomato passata, salt and chilli flakes; simmer 8 minutes until the sauce thickens slightly.
6. Return the kofta to the pan, spooning sauce over them.
7. Cover and simmer gently for 15 minutes until the kofta are cooked through and the oil rises.
8. Serve hot with naan or chalaw and a bowl of cool yogurt.

title: Badenjan Borani
ingredients: 3 large eggplants, peeled in stripes and cut into 2 cm rounds
2 tbsp salt, for drawing out bitterness
instructions:
1. Salt the eggplant rounds and leave for 30 minutes; pat dry thoroughly.
2. Shallow-fry the eggplant in hot oil until deep golden on both sides, 4-5 minutes per side, and drain well (or brush with oil and bake at 220 degrees C for 25 minutes).
3. In a wide pan, fry the garlic in 2 tbsp oil for 30 seconds; add tomato passata, turmeric, salt and chilli.
4. Simmer the sauce 8-10 minutes until it thickens and the oil rises.
5. Layer the eggplant into the sauce and simmer gently 5 minutes so it absorbs the flavour.
6. Whisk the yogurt with crushed garlic and salt.
7. Spread half the yogurt on a serving dish, add the warm eggplant with its sauce, then top with the remaining yogurt.
8. Sprinkle dried mint generously, drizzle with hot oil, and serve warm or at room temperature with naan.

title: Shorwa
ingredients: 1 kg lamb shank or neck, bone-in, cut into pieces
2 medium carrots, cut into thick chunks
2 bay leaves, 4 green cardamoms, 1 cinnamon stick
1/2 cup chopped coriander and dill, to finish
Naan and lemon wedges, to serve
instructions:
1. Heat oil in a heavy pot; sear the lamb on high heat until browned all over, about 8 minutes.
2. Add onions and garlic; saute 5-6 minutes until soft and golden.
3. Stir in turmeric, coriander, cumin, bay leaf, cardamom and cinnamon; cook 2 minutes.
4. Add the grated tomatoes and cook until they darken and the oil separates, about 5 minutes.
5. Pour in 8 cups water and salt; bring to a boil, skim, then cover and simmer gently for 1.5 hours until the lamb is tender.
6. Add carrots and potatoes; simmer uncovered 25-30 minutes until the vegetables are soft and the shorwa has deepened in colour.
7. Adjust salt and pepper; the broth should be rich but drinkable.
8. Finish with chopped coriander and dill; serve in deep bowls with naan for dipping and lemon on the side.

title: Tikka-e Kebab
ingredients: 800 g boneless lamb leg, cut into 4 cm cubes
1 large onion, grated and squeezed dry
2 tbsp oil, plus extra for basting
Naan and sliced salad, to serve
instructions:
1. Whisk the onion, yogurt, ginger-garlic paste, oil, salt, pepper, coriander and cumin into a marinade.
2. Toss the lamb cubes in the marinade; cover and refrigerate at least 2 hours, preferably overnight.
3. Soak wooden skewers in water for 30 minutes if using.
4. Thread 5-6 cubes per skewer, leaving small gaps for even cooking.
5. Grill over hot charcoal or a grill pan for 10-12 minutes, turning every 2-3 minutes.
6. Baste with a little oil as they cook, aiming for charred edges and juicy, fully cooked centres.
7. Rest the skewers 2-3 minutes off the heat.
8. Slide the tikka onto warm naan, add salad, squeeze lemon over, and serve immediately.

title: Shola
ingredients: 500 g bone-in lamb, cut into small cubes
400 g short-grain or basmati rice, rinsed
Garlic-yogurt to serve: 2 cups yogurt, 2 cloves garlic crushed, 1/2 tsp salt
instructions:
1. Heat oil in a heavy pot; brown the lamb with the onions on high heat for 8-10 minutes.
2. Add garlic, turmeric, coriander, cumin, salt and pepper; stir 2 minutes.
3. Pour in 4 cups hot water; cover and simmer until the lamb is tender, about 60 minutes.
4. Add the drained mung beans and cook 20 minutes until soft but not splitting.
5. Add the rinsed rice and 5 cups hot water, adjusted so the liquid covers everything by about 2 cm.
6. Cook uncovered on medium heat, stirring frequently from the bottom, for 15-18 minutes.
7. When the rice swells and the mixture turns thick and creamy like risotto, reduce the heat to low, cover, and steam 15 minutes, stirring once or twice to keep it sticky.
8. Rest 5 minutes; serve hot topped with garlic-yogurt and coriander, as shola should be soft, sticky and spoonable.

title: Kadu Bouranee
ingredients: 1 kg pumpkin or butternut squash, peeled and cut into thick wedges
1/2 cup oil, for shallow-frying (or 3 tbsp for baking)
instructions:
1. Peel the pumpkin and cut into thick 4 cm wedges.
2. Shallow-fry the wedges in hot oil until golden and tender at the edges, 4-5 minutes per side, or brush with oil and bake at 220 degrees C for 30 minutes.
3. In a wide pan, fry the minced garlic for 30 seconds; add tomato passata, sugar, turmeric, salt and chilli flakes.
4. Simmer the sweet-tomato sauce 8-10 minutes until slightly thickened.
5. Add the pumpkin wedges to the sauce and simmer gently 5-7 minutes, spooning the sauce over so they glaze without breaking.
6. Whisk the yogurt with crushed garlic and salt.
7. Spread the yogurt on a serving platter; arrange the glazed pumpkin on top and spoon over the remaining sauce.
8. Dust generously with dried mint, drizzle with hot oil, and serve warm with naan or chalaw.

title: Sabzi Chalao
ingredients: For the chalaw: 2 cups basmati rice soaked 30 minutes, 3 cups water, 1.5 tsp salt, 2 tbsp oil
800 g fresh spinach (or frozen), washed and roughly chopped
1 tbsp dried dill or 1/4 cup fresh dill (optional)
instructions:
1. Cook the chalaw: bring the salted water to a boil, add the rice, cook until just tender, then drain, dot with oil, cover, and steam on the lowest heat for 15 minutes.
2. Meanwhile heat the oil in a wide pan; fry the onion until golden, 6-8 minutes.
3. Add garlic, turmeric, coriander and cumin; stir 1 minute until fragrant.
4. Add tomato paste and fry 2 minutes until it darkens and the oil separates.
5. Add the spinach in handfuls, letting each batch wilt down before adding more.
6. Season with salt, cover, and simmer on low heat for 20-25 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the sabzi is dark, soft and glistening with oil.
7. Stir in fresh coriander and dill; simmer 5 more minutes.
8. Plate the sabzi alongside or over the chalaw and serve hot, with naan if you like.

title: Moshawa
ingredients: 1 tbsp dried dill (or 1/4 cup fresh, chopped)
Dried mint and chili flakes to garnish
instructions:
1. Heat oil in a large pot and fry the onions until deep golden.
2. Add garlic, ginger and the beef; saute until the meat is browned on all sides.
3. Stir in turmeric, coriander and black pepper; cook 1 minute.
4. Pour in 8 cups water, bring to a boil, skim the foam, then simmer covered for 45 minutes.
5. Add the soaked mung beans and chickpeas; simmer 45-60 minutes until the beans are soft.
6. Stir in the noodles and cook 8-10 minutes until tender.
7. Whisk the yogurt with a ladle of hot broth, then slowly stir it back into the pot over low heat without boiling.
8. Add dill, cilantro and mint; simmer 5 minutes and adjust salt.
9. Serve hot garnished with dried mint and chili flakes, alongside Afghan naan.

title: Chalow Murgi
instructions:
1. Soak the basmati rice for 30 minutes, then drain.
2. Boil 8 cups water with 2 tsp salt; parboil the rice until 3/4 cooked (about 6 minutes), then drain.
3. For the chicken, heat oil in a wide pot and fry the onions until deep golden.
4. Add garlic, ginger, cinnamon, black cardamom and green cardamom; saute 1 minute until fragrant.
5. Add the chicken pieces and sear until coated and lightly browned.
6. Add coriander, turmeric, black pepper, salt and tomatoes; cook until the tomatoes break down, 5-7 minutes.
7. Pour in 1 cup water, cover, and simmer 25-30 minutes until the chicken is tender and oil separates.
8. For the chalow, return the parboiled rice to the pot with 1/2 cup water and a drizzle of oil; seal with a foil-covered lid and steam on the lowest heat for 20 minutes.
9. Serve the chicken qorma spooned over the chalow, garnished with fresh cilantro.

title: Bamya
instructions:
1. Trim the okra tops, rinse and pat completely dry to prevent sliminess.
2. Fry the okra in 2 tbsp oil over medium-high heat until lightly golden, 5-7 minutes; remove and set aside.
3. In the same pot add remaining oil and saute the onions until golden.
4. Add garlic and the meat; brown on all sides.
5. Stir in turmeric, coriander, black pepper and tomato paste; cook 1 minute.
6. Add the chopped tomatoes and cook until softened.
7. Pour in water, add salt, cover and simmer 40-50 minutes until the meat is tender.
8. Return the okra to the pot and simmer gently 15 minutes more, stirring carefully so the okra holds shape.
9. Finish with lemon juice and cilantro; serve with Afghan naan or chalow rice.

title: Sri Lankan Chicken Curry
instructions:
1. Marinate the chicken with turmeric, 1 tsp curry powder, salt and a splash of thin coconut milk for 20 minutes.
2. Heat coconut oil in a pot and saute the onion until soft and golden.
3. Add garlic, ginger, curry leaves, pandan, cinnamon and cardamom; fry until fragrant.
4. Add the marinated chicken and sear for 5 minutes, turning to coat.
5. Add the remaining curry powder and chili powder; stir 2 minutes.
6. Pour in the thin coconut milk, cover and simmer 20 minutes.
7. Add the slit green chilies and thick coconut milk; simmer uncovered 10 minutes until the gravy thickens.
8. Finish with lime juice and rest 5 minutes.
9. Serve hot with rice, string hoppers or roti.

title: Sri Lankan Fish Curry
ingredients: 750g firm fish steaks (tuna or seer fish), cut into chunks
1 tsp goraka paste (or 1 tbsp lime juice)
instructions:
1. Rub the fish with turmeric, salt and goraka or lime juice; rest 15 minutes.
2. Heat coconut oil in a clay pot or pan and fry the onion until golden.
3. Add garlic, ginger, curry leaves, pandan and cinnamon; fry until fragrant.
4. Add curry powder, chili powder and black pepper; fry on low for 1 minute.
5. Pour in the thin coconut milk and bring to a gentle simmer.
6. Slide in the fish pieces and simmer 8-10 minutes, spooning gravy over without stirring hard.
7. Add the green chilies and thick coconut milk; simmer 5 minutes.
8. Adjust salt and sourness to taste and rest 5 minutes.
9. Serve with red rice or string hoppers.

title: Prawn Devilled
ingredients: 2 capsicums (1 green, 1 red), cut into triangles
instructions:
1. Marinate the prawns with chili powder, turmeric and salt for 15 minutes.
2. Mix ketchup, chili sauce, soy sauce, sugar, vinegar and water in a bowl; set aside.
3. Heat oil in a wok and sear the prawns 1-2 minutes per side until just pink; remove.
4. In the same wok stir-fry the onions and capsicums on high heat for 2 minutes, keeping them crunchy.
5. Add garlic, ginger, green chilies and curry leaves; fry 1 minute.
6. Add the tomato wedges and toss 1 minute.
7. Pour in the sauce and simmer 2 minutes until glossy.
8. Return the prawns and toss 2-3 minutes until coated and cooked through.
9. Serve hot with rice or as a spicy party starter.

title: Sri Lankan Crab Curry
ingredients: 2 large crabs (about 1.2kg), cleaned, cut into pieces, claws cracked
3 tsp Sri Lankan roasted curry powder
instructions:
1. Marinate the crab pieces with turmeric, salt and 1 tsp chili powder for 15 minutes.
2. Heat coconut oil in a large pot and saute the onion until golden.
3. Add garlic, ginger, curry leaves, pandan and cinnamon; fry until fragrant.
4. Add roasted curry powder, remaining chili powder and black pepper; fry 1 minute on low.
5. Add the crab and toss well to coat in the spice base, searing 5 minutes.
6. Pour in the thin coconut milk, cover and simmer 15 minutes.
7. Add the thick coconut milk and green chilies; simmer uncovered 10 minutes until the gravy is rich.
8. Finish with lime juice and adjust salt.
9. Serve hot with rice or crusty bread, with crab crackers on the side.

title: Kottu Roti
ingredients: 6 godamba rotis (or plain flaky parathas), cut into thin strips
1 leek or 1/2 small cabbage, finely shredded
instructions:
1. Cut the rotis into thin strips and set aside.
2. Heat oil on a large flat griddle or wide pan; saute onion, garlic, green chilies and curry leaves.
3. Add carrots, leek and capsicum; stir-fry 3-4 minutes.
4. Add curry powder, turmeric and salt; mix well.
5. Push the vegetables to one side and scramble the eggs on the griddle.
6. Add the roti strips and toss everything together.
7. Pour in the curry gravy and chop and mix rhythmically with two metal spatulas, 5-7 minutes, until finely chopped and well coated.
8. Add spring onion and adjust salt.
9. Serve hot, straight off the griddle.

title: Hoppers
ingredients: 1 egg per hopper (optional, for egg hoppers)
instructions:
1. Blend the warm cooked rice with the thin coconut milk until smooth.
2. Mix the rice flour, sugar and yeast in a bowl; add the rice-coconut mixture and whisk into a thick batter.
3. Gradually add the thick coconut milk until the batter is the consistency of pouring cream.
4. Cover and ferment 6-8 hours or overnight until bubbly and slightly sour.
5. Stir in salt and baking soda; rest 10 minutes.
6. Heat a hopper pan on medium heat and wipe lightly with oil.
7. Pour in a ladleful and swirl to coat the sides into a bowl shape, letting the excess pool in the center.
8. Cover and cook 3-4 minutes until the edges are lacy and crisp and the center is set; for egg hoppers, crack an egg into the center before covering.
9. Slide out and repeat; serve with pol sambol and lunu miris.

title: String Hoppers
instructions:
1. Mix the salt into the rice flour.
2. Add boiling water gradually, stirring with a spoon until a soft dough forms.
3. Knead briefly while warm until smooth and pliable but not sticky.
4. Fill a string-hopper press with the dough.
5. Press thin noodle circles onto greased string-hopper mats or banana leaf rounds.
6. Bring water to a rolling boil in a steamer.
7. Steam the hoppers on their mats for 5-7 minutes until cooked through.
8. Remove and slide the string hoppers off the mats.
9. Serve warm with kiri hodi (coconut milk gravy), pol sambol and dhal curry.

title: Devilled Chicken
ingredients: 700g boneless chicken thighs, cut into chunks
instructions:
1. Marinate the chicken with chili powder, turmeric, soy sauce and salt for 30 minutes.
2. Mix ketchup, chili sauce, soy sauce, sugar, vinegar and water; set aside.
3. Heat oil in a wok and fry the chicken until golden and cooked through, 8-10 minutes; remove.
4. Stir-fry the onions and capsicums on high heat for 2 minutes.
5. Add garlic, ginger, green chilies and curry leaves; fry 1 minute.
6. Pour in the sauce and simmer 2 minutes until slightly thickened.
7. Return the chicken and toss 2-3 minutes until glossy and coated.
8. Adjust salt and spice to taste.
9. Serve hot with fried rice or as a starter.

title: Sri Lankan Mutton Curry
ingredients: 1kg mutton (goat) on the bone, cut into pieces
instructions:
1. Marinate the mutton with turmeric, 2 tsp curry powder, salt and goraka or vinegar for at least 1 hour.
2. Heat coconut oil in a heavy pot and brown the onions.
3. Add garlic, ginger, curry leaves, pandan, cinnamon, cardamom and cloves; fry until fragrant.
4. Add the mutton and sear 5-6 minutes, turning well.
5. Add the remaining curry powder, chili powder and black pepper; fry 2 minutes.
6. Pour in the thin coconut milk, cover and simmer 45-50 minutes until nearly tender, adding water if it dries out.
7. Add the thick coconut milk and green chilies; simmer 15 minutes more.
8. Adjust salt; the gravy should coat the back of a spoon.
9. Rest 10 minutes and serve with rice, string hoppers or roti.

title: Pol Sambol
ingredients: A few curry leaves, finely chopped (optional)
instructions:
1. Place the grated coconut in a mixing bowl.
2. Add chili powder, salt, pepper and Maldive fish if using; rub together with your fingertips until the coconut turns orange-red.
3. Add the chopped onion and green chilies; mix through.
4. Squeeze in the lime juice and toss well.
5. Adjust chili and salt to taste.
6. Rest 10 minutes so the flavors meld.
7. Serve alongside rice and curry, hoppers or string hoppers.

title: Chicken Kottu
ingredients: 6 godamba rotis (or parathas), cut into strips
400g chicken, marinated, cooked and chopped small
instructions:
1. Season the chicken with salt, pepper and a little curry powder; grill or pan-fry until cooked, then chop into small pieces.
2. Cut the rotis into thin strips.
3. Heat oil on a large flat griddle; saute onion, garlic, green chilies and curry leaves.
4. Add carrots, leek and capsicum; stir-fry 3 minutes.
5. Add curry powder, turmeric and salt; mix.
6. Push aside and scramble the eggs on the griddle.
7. Add the roti strips and chopped chicken; toss together.
8. Pour in the chicken gravy and chop and mix with two spatulas for 5-7 minutes until everything is finely cut and coated.
9. Finish with spring onion and serve hot.

title: Chicken Momo
ingredients: For jhol achar: 2 roasted tomatoes, 2 soaked dried red chilies, 1 garlic clove, 1 tbsp roasted sesame seeds, 1 tsp roasted cumin seeds, 1 tbsp vinegar, 1/2 cup water, salt, cilantro
instructions:
1. Knead the flour, salt and water into a soft dough; rest 30 minutes.
2. Mix all the filling ingredients thoroughly and rest 15 minutes.
3. Roll the dough into thin 8-9cm circles, slightly thicker in the center.
4. Place 1 tbsp filling in each wrapper, pleat and seal the edges.
5. Line a greased steamer and arrange the momos without touching.
6. Steam 12-15 minutes until the wrappers turn translucent and the filling is cooked.
7. Blend the roasted tomatoes, chilies, garlic, sesame, cumin, vinegar, water, salt and cilantro into a smooth jhol achar.
8. Serve the hot momos with the dipping sauce.

title: Buff Choila
ingredients: 500g buffalo meat (halal), boneless, cut into thick chunks
instructions:
1. Boil or steam the buffalo chunks with turmeric and salt for 15-20 minutes until just cooked but firm.
2. Char or sear the boiled meat over a flame or hot pan until the edges are smoky; cool slightly.
3. Slice the meat into thin pieces and place in a bowl.
4. Heat the mustard oil until it smokes, then let it cool for 1 minute.
5. Toss the meat with cumin, coriander, chili powder, timur, garlic, ginger and green chilies.
6. Pour the hot mustard oil over the spiced meat and mix well.
7. Add onion, cilantro and lemon juice; toss again.
8. Temper the fenugreek seeds in 1 tsp oil until dark and pour sizzling over the choila.
9. Rest 15 minutes and serve with beaten rice (chiura).

title: Sekuwa
ingredients: Sliced onion, lemon wedges and cilantro to serve
instructions:
1. Mix all the marinade ingredients in a bowl and coat the meat cubes well.
2. Marinate for at least 2 hours, preferably overnight in the fridge.
3. If using wooden skewers, soak them in water for 30 minutes.
4. Thread the meat onto skewers, leaving small gaps between pieces.
5. Grill over charcoal or broil in the oven at 220C.
6. Cook 12-15 minutes, turning often and basting with a little oil.
7. Let the edges char slightly for a smoky flavor.
8. Rest the skewers for 2 minutes off the heat.
9. Serve hot with sliced onion, lemon wedges, cilantro and chiura.

title: Thakali Khana
instructions:
1. Cook the rice with 4 cups water until fluffy.
2. Boil the lentils with turmeric and salt until soft, then lightly mash; temper with ghee, cumin seeds and dried red chilies poured over the top.
3. For the tarkari, heat oil and fry the onion until golden; add ginger-garlic paste and the powdered spices.
4. Add the potatoes with 1 cup water, cover and cook 15 minutes; stir in the greens at the end.
5. For the saag, stir-fry the extra greens with garlic and a pinch of salt until wilted.
6. Mash the roasted tomatoes with green chili, salt, timur and cilantro to make a fresh achar.
7. Assemble a large plate: rice in the center, dal pooled around it.
8. Arrange the tarkari, saag and achar around the plate.
9. Serve immediately, mixing as you eat.

title: Dal Bhat Tarkari
ingredients: 1 cup split lentils (masoor or moong dal)
instructions:
1. Cook the rice with 4 cups water until soft and fluffy.
2. Boil the lentils with turmeric, salt and 3.5 cups water for 15-20 minutes until soft.
3. Heat ghee, crackle the cumin, fry the garlic and dried chilies with tomato, then pour this tempering into the dal.
4. For the tarkari, heat oil in a pan and fry the onion until golden.
5. Add ginger-garlic paste and all the powdered spices; fry 1 minute.
6. Add potatoes, cauliflower, salt and 1 cup water; cover and cook 15-18 minutes until tender with a thick gravy.
7. Adjust the dal to a pourable consistency.
8. Serve the rice with dal poured over and tarkari on the side, plus pickle if desired.

title: Chicken Thukpa
ingredients: Spring onion and cilantro to garnish
instructions:
1. Boil the noodles until just tender; drain, rinse and toss with a little oil.
2. Heat oil in a large pot and sear the chicken until lightly browned; remove.
3. Saute the onion, garlic, ginger and green chilies in the same pot.
4. Add the carrot and cabbage; stir-fry 2 minutes.
5. Add the spices and tomato; cook until the tomato breaks down.
6. Pour in the stock, return the chicken and simmer 12-15 minutes until cooked through.
7. Season with soy sauce, salt, pepper and timur.
8. Place noodles in bowls and ladle the hot soup and chicken over them.
9. Garnish with spring onion and cilantro; serve with chili sauce on the side.

title: Aloo Tama
ingredients: 1 cup tama (fermented bamboo shoots), drained and rinsed
1/2 cup black-eyed peas, soaked and boiled until just tender
instructions:
1. Soak the black-eyed peas for 2 hours and boil until just tender.
2. Rinse the tama well and drain.
3. Heat mustard oil and crackle the cumin seeds.
4. Fry the onion until golden; add ginger-garlic paste and green chilies.
5. Add turmeric, cumin, coriander, chili powder and tomato; cook into a masala paste.
6. Add the potatoes and coat in the masala for 2-3 minutes.
7. Add the tama, boiled beans, water and salt; cover and simmer 15-20 minutes until the potatoes are tender.
8. Adjust salt; the curry should be pleasantly tangy from the bamboo shoots.
9. Garnish with cilantro and serve with rice or chiura.

title: Newari Khaja Set
ingredients: 1 tsp turmeric and salt for boiling
1 tbsp cumin powder, 1 tbsp coriander powder, 1 tsp chili powder, 1/2 tsp timur, 3 garlic cloves minced, 1 tbsp ginger grated
1 tbsp roasted sesame paste, 1 tsp chili powder, 1 tbsp mustard oil, lemon juice for aloo achar
Handful of cilantro, 1 green chili, 1 garlic clove, 1 tomato for green achar
instructions:
1. Make the choila: boil the buffalo meat with turmeric and salt until just cooked, char the pieces in a hot pan, slice thin and toss with the ground spices, garlic, ginger and hot mustard oil.
2. Make the aloo achar: mix the potato cubes with sesame paste, chili powder, mustard oil, lemon juice and salt.
3. Make the green achar: blend cilantro, green chili, garlic, tomato and salt into a coarse paste.
4. Dry-roast the soybeans in a pan until they crackle and turn lightly browned; sprinkle with salt.
5. Boil the eggs for 10 minutes, cool and halve.
6. Lightly crisp the beaten rice in a dry pan if desired.
7. Assemble a large plate: pile the chiura on one side.
8. Arrange the choila, aloo achar, green achar, soybeans, egg halves and onion slices around it.
9. Drizzle a little mustard oil over the chiura and serve immediately, eaten by hand.

title: Chicken Chowmein
instructions:
1. Boil the noodles until just tender; drain, rinse under cold water and toss with 1 tsp oil.
2. Season the chicken with a pinch of salt, pepper and 1 tsp soy sauce.
3. Heat oil in a wok on high and stir-fry the chicken until cooked; remove.
4. Fry the garlic and ginger for 30 seconds in the same wok.
5. Add the onion and green chilies; fry 1 minute.
6. Add the carrot, cabbage and capsicum; stir-fry 2-3 minutes on high heat.
7. Return the chicken, add the noodles, soy sauce, chili sauce, vinegar and pepper.
8. Toss everything together for 2-3 minutes until well combined and steaming hot.
9. Finish with spring onion and sesame oil; serve hot.

title: Beef Biryani
ingredients: 750g beef (bone-in stew pieces or boneless chunks)
2 bay leaves, 1 cinnamon stick, 4 black cardamom, 6 green cardamom, 6 cloves, 1 tsp cumin seeds
1/2 cup warm milk with a pinch of saffron
2 tbsp salt for rice boiling water
instructions:
1. Fry the sliced onions in oil until deep golden; remove half as crispy birista.
2. In the same pot add the whole spices, then the beef and ginger-garlic paste; brown well.
3. Add the coriander, cumin, chili powder, turmeric, salt, tomatoes and yogurt; cook until the beef is coated and oil separates.
4. Add 2 cups water, cover and simmer 60-75 minutes (or pressure cook 35 minutes) until the beef is tender and the masala is thick.
5. Boil the drained rice in plenty of salted water with a bay leaf until 3/4 cooked; drain.
6. Layer half the rice in a large pot, spread the beef masala over it, then top with mint, cilantro, green chilies, birista and the remaining rice.
7. Sprinkle the saffron milk, kewra water and dots of ghee over the top.
8. Seal the pot with foil and a tight lid; steam on the lowest heat (dum) for 20-25 minutes.
9. Rest 10 minutes, fluff gently and serve with raita and kachumber salad.

title: Beef Karahi
ingredients: 1kg beef, boneless cubes or small bone-in pieces
instructions:
1. Heat the oil in a karahi or heavy wok and add the cumin seeds.
2. Add the beef and sear on high heat until browned on all sides.
3. Stir in the ginger and garlic pastes; fry 1-2 minutes.
4. Add the crushed coriander seeds, half the black pepper and salt; mix well.
5. Add the tomatoes and 1/2 cup water; cover and cook 45-60 minutes until the beef is tender, stirring occasionally.
6. Uncover, mash the tomatoes with the spatula and bhunai (fry hard) on high heat until the oil separates and the gravy thickens.
7. Add the green chilies and remaining black pepper; cook 5 minutes.
8. Garnish with ginger juliennes and cilantro.
9. Serve sizzling hot with naan or roti.

title: Beef Boti
ingredients: 800 g boneless beef (undercut or sirloin), cut into 4 cm cubes
1 small piece natural charcoal, for smoking (optional)
1 onion, sliced into rings, to serve
1 lemon, cut into wedges, to serve
instructions:
1. Pat the beef cubes dry with paper towels and place in a large mixing bowl.
2. Whisk together yogurt, papaya paste, ginger-garlic paste, chili powder, coriander, cumin, garam masala, turmeric, mustard oil, lemon juice, and salt into a thick marinade.
3. Coat the beef thoroughly, cover, and refrigerate for at least 8 hours or overnight.
4. Thread 4-5 cubes onto each metal or soaked wooden skewer, leaving small gaps between pieces.
5. Grill over hot charcoal or under a preheated broiler at 220°C for 15-20 minutes, turning every 5 minutes, until charred at the edges and cooked through.
6. Optional: place a burning charcoal piece in a small bowl among the cooked boti, drizzle with a few drops of oil, and cover for 3 minutes to infuse smoke.
7. Rest the skewers 5 minutes, then slide the boti off.
8. Serve hot with onion rings, lemon wedges, and mint chutney.

title: Chicken Croquettes
ingredients: 2 medium potatoes (about 300 g), boiled and peeled
3 cups vegetable oil, for deep frying
instructions:
1. Boil the chicken in salted water for 15 minutes until fully cooked, then drain and shred finely.
2. Mash the boiled potatoes until completely smooth.
3. Combine chicken, potato, onion, green chilies, cilantro, black pepper, garam masala, salt, and 1 beaten egg in a bowl; mix well.
4. Shape the mixture into 10-12 finger-length cylinders.
5. Beat the second egg in a shallow bowl and spread breadcrumbs on a plate.
6. Roll each croquette in breadcrumbs, dip in beaten egg, then coat again in breadcrumbs for a double crust.
7. Chill the coated croquettes in the freezer for 20 minutes so they hold their shape.
8. Heat oil to 170°C and fry croquettes in batches until deep golden brown, 4-5 minutes, turning as needed.
9. Drain on paper towels and serve hot with ketchup or garlic mayo.

title: Chicken Pot Pie
ingredients: 400 g boneless chicken breast, cut into 2 cm cubes
1 sheet all-butter puff pastry (about 250 g), thawed
instructions:
1. Melt butter in a large pan over medium heat and sauté onion and carrots for 5 minutes until softened.
2. Add chicken cubes and cook until no longer pink, 6-7 minutes.
3. Sprinkle flour over the mixture and stir constantly for 2 minutes to cook out the raw taste.
4. Gradually pour in chicken stock and milk while stirring, and simmer until a thick creamy sauce forms, about 5 minutes.
5. Stir in peas, thyme, salt, and pepper; cook 2 minutes, then cool the filling for 15 minutes.
6. Preheat oven to 200°C and spoon the filling into a 20 cm pie dish.
7. Drape the puff pastry over the dish, trim the excess, press the edges with a fork to seal, and cut 2-3 slits on top for steam.
8. Brush the pastry with beaten egg.
9. Bake 30-35 minutes until the pastry is puffed and deep golden; rest 10 minutes before serving.

title: Chicken Noodle Soup
ingredients: 300 g boneless chicken thighs or breast
2 tbsp fresh cilantro or parsley, chopped
instructions:
1. Heat oil in a large pot over medium heat and sauté onion until translucent, 4 minutes.
2. Add garlic and ginger and cook 1 minute until fragrant.
3. Add chicken and sear until lightly golden on the outside, 4 minutes.
4. Pour in chicken stock, bring to a boil, then simmer uncovered for 20 minutes until the chicken is cooked through.
5. Lift out the chicken, shred it with two forks, and return it to the pot.
6. Add carrots and simmer 5 minutes.
7. Add egg noodles and cook 6-8 minutes until just tender.
8. Season with soy sauce, black pepper, and salt.
9. Ladle into bowls, top with spring onions and cilantro, and serve with lemon wedges.

title: Chicken Shawarma
ingredients: 1/2 cup tahini sauce (tahini, lemon juice, garlic, water, salt)
instructions:
1. Slice the chicken thighs into thin strips.
2. Whisk yogurt, olive oil, vinegar, all spices, garlic, and salt into a marinade.
3. Coat the chicken well, cover, and marinate in the refrigerator for at least 4 hours, preferably overnight.
4. Heat a heavy skillet or grill pan over high heat until very hot.
5. Cook the chicken in a single layer until charred at the edges and cooked through, 8-10 minutes total.
6. Rest 5 minutes, then chop into smaller pieces.
7. Warm the flatbreads on a dry pan for 30 seconds per side.
8. Spread each bread with tahini sauce, then layer chicken, tomato, onion, and pickles.
9. Roll tightly, wrap in foil, and toast the wrapped rolls seam-side down on the pan for 2-3 minutes.
10. Slice in half and serve hot with extra tahini sauce.

title: Lamb Shawarma
ingredients: 700 g boneless lamb leg or shoulder, sliced very thin
1/2 cup garlic sauce (toum) or tahini sauce
instructions:
1. Toss the thin lamb slices with yogurt, olive oil, vinegar, spices, garlic, and salt.
2. Cover and marinate in the refrigerator for at least 8 hours or overnight.
3. Preheat oven to 220°C and spread the lamb in a single layer on a large roasting tray.
4. Roast 25-30 minutes, stirring twice, until the edges are browned and crisp and the lamb is cooked through.
5. Alternatively, sear the lamb in batches on a very hot grill pan, 4-5 minutes per batch.
6. Rest 5 minutes, then chop into smaller pieces.
7. Warm the flatbreads and spread each generously with garlic or tahini sauce.
8. Pile on the lamb, tomato, pickles, and parsley.
9. Roll tightly, wrap in foil, and heat on a pan or in a 180°C oven for 5 minutes.
10. Serve hot with extra pickles and sauce.

title: Falafel
ingredients: 250 g dried chickpeas, soaked overnight in plenty of water
4 cups vegetable oil, for deep frying
Pita bread, tahini sauce, and salad, to serve
instructions:
1. Drain the soaked chickpeas thoroughly and pat dry.
2. Grind the chickpeas with onion, garlic, parsley, and cilantro in a food processor to a coarse, grainy paste — do not over-process into a smooth paste.
3. Transfer to a bowl and mix in cumin, coriander, chili flakes, baking powder, flour, salt, and pepper.
4. Rest the mixture in the refrigerator for 30 minutes.
5. Shape into 18-20 small balls, roll each in sesame seeds, and flatten slightly.
6. Heat oil to 175°C in a deep pot.
7. Fry falafel in small batches for 3-4 minutes until deep golden and crisp, turning occasionally.
8. Drain on paper towels.
9. Serve hot stuffed into pita with tahini sauce, tomato, and pickles.

title: Hummus
ingredients: 250 g dried chickpeas, soaked overnight (or 400 g canned chickpeas, drained)
1/2 tsp baking soda, for boiling dried chickpeas
2 tbsp whole cooked chickpeas and chopped parsley, to garnish
instructions:
1. Drain the soaked chickpeas and boil in fresh water with baking soda for 45-60 minutes until very soft; drain, reserving a few for garnish (if using canned chickpeas, skip to step 3).
2. Blend the warm boiled chickpeas alone for 1 minute.
3. In a food processor, blend tahini, lemon juice, and garlic for 1 minute until pale and whipped.
4. Add chickpeas, cumin, and salt; blend 3-4 minutes, scraping down the sides.
5. With the motor running, add ice water a tablespoon at a time until the hummus is silky and light.
6. Taste and adjust lemon juice and salt.
7. Spread on a shallow plate and swirl with the back of a spoon.
