8. Drizzle with olive oil and garnish with paprika, whole chickpeas, and parsley.
9. Serve at room temperature with warm pita bread.

title: Baba Ganoush
instructions:
1. Prick the eggplants all over with a fork.
2. Roast directly over a gas flame or in a 220°C oven, turning often, for 30-40 minutes until the skin is charred and the flesh completely collapses.
3. Let cool, peel off the skin, and let the flesh drain in a colander for 10 minutes to remove bitterness.
4. Chop the flesh finely with a knife — keep it chunky rather than blending smooth.
5. Mix the eggplant with tahini, lemon juice, garlic, cumin, olive oil, and salt.
6. Taste and adjust lemon and salt.
7. Spread on a plate and drizzle with extra olive oil.
8. Garnish with parsley, pomegranate seeds, and smoked paprika.
9. Serve with warm pita or fresh vegetable sticks.

title: Tabbouleh
instructions:
1. Place bulgur in a bowl and cover with 1 cup boiling water; soak 20 minutes until tender.
2. Drain well in a fine sieve, pressing out excess water with a spoon.
3. Whisk olive oil, lemon juice, salt, and pepper into a dressing.
4. Combine parsley, mint, tomatoes, cucumber, and spring onions in a large bowl.
5. Add the drained bulgur and the dressing; toss thoroughly.
6. Rest in the refrigerator for 15 minutes so the flavors meld.
7. Taste and adjust lemon and salt.
8. Serve chilled, scooped onto romaine lettuce leaves.

title: Kibbeh
ingredients: For the shell: 250 g fine bulgur wheat
For the shell: 400 g very finely ground halal beef or lamb (double-ground)
For the shell: 1 small onion, grated
For the shell: 1 tsp cumin powder
For the shell: 1/2 tsp black pepper
For the shell: 2 tbsp ice water
For the filling: 300 g ground halal beef or lamb
For the filling: 1 onion, finely chopped
For the filling: 1/3 cup pine nuts
For the filling: 2 tbsp olive oil
4 cups vegetable oil, for deep frying
instructions:
1. Rinse the bulgur, soak in cold water for 15 minutes, then drain and squeeze out all water with your hands.
2. Knead the bulgur with the shell meat, grated onion, cumin, allspice, salt, and pepper for 10 minutes into a smooth, pliable paste, adding ice water as needed.
3. For the filling, brown the onion in olive oil, add the ground meat, allspice, cinnamon, and salt, and cook 8 minutes until done; stir in toasted pine nuts and cool.
4. With wet hands, take a ball of shell mixture (about 60 g) and hollow it with your finger into a thin-walled cup.
5. Place 1 tablespoon of filling inside, seal the opening, and shape into a pointed oval like a lemon.
6. Repeat with the remaining mixture and chill the kibbeh for 30 minutes.
7. Heat frying oil to 175°C.
8. Fry kibbeh in batches for 4-5 minutes until deep brown and crisp.
9. Drain on paper towels and serve hot with yogurt-mint sauce.

title: Fattoush
ingredients: 2 khubz or pita flatbreads, torn into bite-size pieces
1/4 cup extra virgin olive oil, for dressing
instructions:
1. Fry the torn pita pieces in 3 tbsp olive oil over medium heat until golden and crisp, 3-4 minutes; drain on paper towels (or bake at 200°C for 8 minutes).
2. Whisk the dressing olive oil, lemon juice, garlic, 1 tsp sumac, pomegranate molasses, and salt.
3. Combine tomatoes, cucumbers, radishes, bell pepper, romaine, parsley, mint, and spring onions in a large bowl.
4. Pour the dressing over and toss well.
5. Add the crispy pita pieces and toss lightly so they stay crunchy.
6. Sprinkle the remaining sumac on top.
7. Serve immediately before the bread softens.

title: Manakish
ingredients: 1 cup warm water, plus more as needed
1/4 cup olive oil, for the topping
instructions:
1. Stir yeast and sugar into the warm water; rest 10 minutes until foamy.
2. Mix flour and salt in a large bowl, add olive oil and the yeast water, and knead 8-10 minutes into a soft, smooth dough, adding water a spoonful at a time if needed.
3. Cover and let rise in a warm place for 1-1.5 hours until doubled.
4. Mix the za'atar with 1/4 cup olive oil into a spreadable paste.
5. Divide the dough into 4 balls, rest 15 minutes, then roll each into a 20 cm round about 5 mm thick.
6. Spread 2-3 tablespoons of za'atar paste over each round, leaving a 1 cm border.
7. Preheat the oven to 230°C with a baking tray or pizza stone inside.
8. Bake the manakish 8-10 minutes until the edges are golden and the bottoms are crisp.
9. Brush the crusts with olive oil and serve warm with tomatoes, olives, and white cheese.

title: Aloo Tikki
ingredients: 4 large potatoes (about 500 g), boiled and peeled
3 tbsp vegetable oil, for shallow frying
Tamarind chutney, mint chutney, and whisked yogurt, to serve
instructions:
1. Mash the boiled potatoes until completely smooth with no lumps.
2. Mix in onion, green chilies, cilantro, ginger, chaat masala, garam masala, cumin powder, cornflour, and salt.
3. Shape into 8 round, flat patties about 1.5 cm thick.
4. Coat each patty lightly with breadcrumbs and chill for 20 minutes.
5. Heat oil in a wide pan over medium heat.
6. Shallow fry the tikkis 4-5 minutes per side until deep golden and crisp.
7. Drain briefly on paper towels.
8. Serve hot topped with yogurt, tamarind chutney, mint chutney, and a pinch of chaat masala.

title: Vegetable Chop
ingredients: 3 medium potatoes (about 350 g), boiled and peeled
1 tsp chaat masala or Bengali bhaja masala
2 tbsp mustard oil or vegetable oil
1 egg, beaten (or 2 tbsp cornflour mixed with 3 tbsp water)
Kasundi and tomato ketchup, to serve
instructions:
1. Heat 2 tbsp oil in a pan and sauté onion, ginger, and green chilies for 3 minutes.
2. Add grated carrot, beetroot, and peas; cook 5 minutes until the mixture is dry.
3. Mash in the boiled potatoes, then season with cumin powder, chaat masala, salt, and sugar; stir in the crushed peanuts.
4. Cool the mixture completely, then shape into 8 oval chops.
5. Roll each chop in breadcrumbs, dip in beaten egg, then coat again in breadcrumbs.
6. Chill for 15 minutes to firm up.
7. Heat oil to 175°C and fry the chops in batches until deep golden brown, 4-5 minutes.
8. Drain on paper towels.
9. Serve hot with kasundi (Bengali mustard sauce) and ketchup.

title: Chicken Roll
ingredients: 300 g boneless chicken, cut into thin strips
2 eggs, beaten with a pinch of salt
instructions:
1. Marinate the chicken strips with yogurt, ginger-garlic paste, chili powder, garam masala, turmeric, lemon juice, and salt for 30 minutes.
2. Heat 1 tbsp oil in a pan and cook the chicken on high heat 8-10 minutes until browned at the edges and cooked through; set aside.
3. Make soft parathas (or use ready ones) and keep them warm.
4. Brush a hot tawa with oil, pour a thin layer of beaten egg, and immediately lay a paratha on top so the egg sticks to its underside.
5. Cook 1-2 minutes, flip, and cook the egg side 1 minute until set and golden.
6. Repeat with the remaining parathas and egg.
7. Spread green chutney over each egg-coated paratha.
8. Pile on the chicken strips, raw onion slices, and a sprinkle of chaat masala.
9. Roll each paratha tightly and wrap the lower half in foil.
10. Serve hot immediately.

title: Kathi Roll
ingredients: 300 g boneless chicken, cut into 2 cm pieces
4 skewers (or wooden skewers soaked in water)
instructions:
1. Marinate the chicken pieces with yogurt, ginger-garlic paste, chili powder, coriander powder, garam masala, mustard oil, and salt for 1 hour.
2. Thread the chicken onto skewers.
3. Cook over a hot grill pan, open flame, or under a broiler for 12-15 minutes, turning often, until charred outside and cooked through; slide off the skewers.
4. Make flaky parathas and keep them warm.
5. On a lightly oiled tawa, pour a thin layer of beaten egg and lay a paratha over it so the egg coats the underside; cook until set, then flip briefly.
6. Spread green chutney over the egg-coated side of each paratha.
7. Place the chicken kebab pieces in the center, top with onion rings, green chilies, and a squeeze of lemon.
8. Sprinkle with chaat masala.
9. Roll each paratha tightly around the filling and wrap in paper or foil.
10. Serve hot.

title: Egg Roll
ingredients: 2 tablespoons vegetable oil, plus more for frying
instructions:
1. Mix flour, salt and 2 tablespoons oil; add water gradually to make a soft dough; knead 5 minutes, cover and rest 30 minutes.
2. Beat the eggs with chopped onion, green chilies and a pinch of salt.
3. Toss the sliced onion, cucumber and tomato with chaat masala; set the salad aside.
4. Divide the dough into 4 balls and roll each into a thin 8-inch round.
5. Heat a tawa; cook each paratha with a little oil until lightly golden on both sides; remove.
6. Pour a quarter of the egg mixture onto the tawa and immediately lay a paratha on top, pressing gently so the egg sticks; cook 2 minutes.
7. Drizzle oil around the edges, flip, and cook the egg side 1-2 minutes until golden.
8. Transfer egg-side up, spread ketchup and mustard, add the salad, roll tightly, wrap the bottom in paper and serve hot.

title: Butter Naan
ingredients: 1/2 cup warm milk, plus more as needed
instructions:
1. Stir the yeast and sugar into the warm milk; rest 5-10 minutes until foamy.
2. Combine flour, salt, yogurt and oil; add the yeast mixture and knead 8-10 minutes into a soft dough.
3. Cover and let rise in a warm place for 1-1.5 hours until doubled.
4. Punch down, divide into 4 balls and rest 10 minutes.
5. Roll each ball into an oval about 1/4 inch thick.
6. Bake at 250°C/480°F on a preheated baking stone or inverted tray for 3-4 minutes until puffed with golden spots (or cook on a hot tawa 2 minutes per side, then char over a flame).
7. Brush the hot naan generously with melted butter.
8. Sprinkle with nigella seeds and serve warm.

title: Payesh
ingredients: 1/4 cup gobindobhog or any short-grain rice
instructions:
1. Wash and soak the rice for 20 minutes, then drain.
2. Heat the ghee and fry the rice with the bay leaf for 2 minutes; set aside.
3. Bring the milk to a boil and simmer 10 minutes, stirring.
4. Add the rice and cook on low for 30-35 minutes until soft and the milk thickens, stirring often.
5. Add sugar, jaggery and cardamom; simmer 10 more minutes.
6. Fry the raisins and nuts in a little ghee and stir half into the payesh.
7. Serve warm, or chill and serve cold, garnished with the remaining nuts.

title: Rasmalai
instructions:
1. Curdle 1 liter of hot milk with lemon juice; strain, wash and hang the chenna for 30 minutes.
2. Knead the chenna 8-10 minutes until smooth; divide into 8 and roll into flat discs.
3. Boil 5 cups water with 1 1/2 cups sugar; slide in the discs, cover and simmer 15-18 minutes until they puff and double.
4. Meanwhile simmer the second liter of milk until reduced by a third; add 1/4 cup sugar, saffron and cardamom and cook to a thick rabri.
5. Remove the discs from the syrup and gently press each to squeeze out the syrup.
6. Soak the discs in the warm rabri for 30 minutes.
7. Chill for at least 2 hours.
8. Serve cold, garnished with pistachios and almonds.

title: Shahi Tukda
instructions:
1. Simmer the milk with saffron, stirring, until reduced to a thick rabri (about one-third of the volume), 25-30 minutes.
2. Stir in the sugar and cardamom; cook 5 minutes and set aside.
3. Cut each bread slice into 2 triangles.
4. Shallow-fry the bread in ghee on medium heat until crisp and golden on both sides; drain.
5. Arrange the fried bread on a serving platter while warm.
6. Pour the rabri evenly over the pieces so they soak.
7. Rest 20 minutes, then garnish with almonds, pistachios and cashews.
8. Serve warm, or chill 1 hour and serve cold.

title: Sandesh
ingredients: 1/2 cup powdered sugar (or 1/2 cup grated nolen gur/jaggery)
instructions:
1. Curdle the hot milk with lemon juice; strain, wash and hang the chenna for 30 minutes.
2. Knead the chenna until completely smooth with no lumps of moisture.
3. Cook the chenna with sugar (or jaggery) in a non-stick pan on low for 6-8 minutes, stirring, until it comes together as a soft dough.
4. Mix in the khoya and cardamom; cook 2 minutes and cool until just warm.
5. Knead briefly again and divide into 10 portions.
6. Press each portion into sandesh molds or shape into flat discs by hand.
7. Garnish each with chopped pistachios.
8. Chill 1 hour and serve cold.

title: Kulfi
instructions:
1. Simmer the milk, stirring often, until reduced by half, 25-30 minutes.
2. Add the condensed milk, milk powder and sugar; cook 5 minutes, whisking until smooth.
3. Add saffron, cardamom, rose water and half the nuts; cook 2 minutes and cool to room temperature.
4. Whisk once more to remove any skin that formed.
5. Pour into kulfi molds or small paper cups.
6. Freeze 6-8 hours or overnight until fully set.
7. To unmold, dip the molds briefly in warm water and pull out the kulfi.
8. Slice, sprinkle with the remaining nuts and serve immediately.

title: Garlic Naan
ingredients: 1/2 cup warm water, plus more as needed
instructions:
1. Bloom the yeast and sugar in warm water for 5-10 minutes.
2. Mix the flour, salt, yogurt and oil; add the yeast mixture and knead into a soft dough; rise 1-1.5 hours.
3. Stir the minced garlic into the melted butter and set aside.
4. Divide the dough into 4 balls and rest 10 minutes.
5. Roll each into an oval about 1/4 inch thick.
6. Bake on a preheated stone at 250°C/480°F for 3-4 minutes until puffed (or tawa-cook and flame-char).
7. Immediately brush generously with the garlic butter and scatter coriander on top.
8. Serve warm.

title: Tandoori Roti
ingredients: 3/4 cup warm water, plus more as needed
instructions:
1. Mix the flours, salt and yogurt; add water gradually and knead into a medium-soft dough.
2. Cover and rest 30 minutes.
3. Divide into 6 balls.
4. Roll each into a thick 5-6 inch round, slightly thicker than a chapati.
5. Heat a heavy tawa on medium-high; place a roti on it and cook 1 minute until the base sets.
6. Flip and cook the other side 1 minute, then, using tongs, hold the roti directly over a medium flame for 30 seconds until it chars and puffs (or bake at 250°C/480°F on a preheated tray for 5-6 minutes).
7. Brush with melted ghee.
8. Serve hot with curry or dal.

title: Lachha Paratha
ingredients: 2 cups whole wheat flour (or 1 cup each whole wheat and all-purpose)
1/2 cup warm water, plus more as needed
4 tablespoons softened ghee or butter (for layering)
instructions:
1. Knead the flour, salt, oil and water into a soft dough; rest 30 minutes.
2. Divide into 4 balls and rest 10 minutes.
3. Roll one ball into a thin 10-inch circle.
4. Brush generously with softened ghee and sprinkle a light dusting of dry flour.
5. Pleat the circle into a fan, then coil the pleated strip into a spiral, tucking the end underneath.
6. Gently roll the spiral out to a 6-7 inch round, pressing lightly to preserve the layers.
7. Cook on a medium-hot tawa with a little ghee, 2-3 minutes per side, pressing the edges, until crisp and golden.
8. Crush lightly between your palms to fluff the layers and serve hot.

title: Aloo Paratha
instructions:
1. Knead the flour, salt and water into a soft dough; rest 30 minutes.
2. Mash the potatoes and mix in onion, chilies, coriander, cumin, amchur, chili powder and salt.
3. Divide the dough into 6 balls and the filling into 6 portions.
4. Roll a dough ball to a 4-inch round and place a portion of filling in the center.
5. Bring the edges over the filling, pinch to seal, and roll gently to a 6-7 inch round, dusting with flour.
6. Cook on a medium-hot tawa for 1 minute, flip, spread ghee and cook 2 minutes.
7. Flip again, spread ghee on the other side and cook until both sides are golden with brown spots.
8. Serve hot with yogurt, pickle or butter.

title: Peshawari Naan
ingredients: 1/2 cup warm milk, plus more as needed
1/4 cup mixed almonds, cashews and pistachios, chopped
instructions:
1. Bloom the yeast and sugar in warm milk for 5-10 minutes.
2. Mix the flour, salt, yogurt and oil; add the yeast mixture and knead into a soft dough; rise 1-1.5 hours.
3. Mix the nuts, raisins, coconut, sugar and cardamom for the filling.
4. Divide the dough into 4 balls and flatten each into a 4-inch disc.
5. Place a quarter of the filling in the center, bring the edges up and seal tightly.
6. Gently roll into a 6-inch round so the filling stays inside.
7. Bake at 250°C/480°F on a preheated stone for 4-5 minutes until golden with dark spots (or tawa-cook and flame-char).
8. Brush with melted butter and serve warm.

title: Cheese Naan
ingredients: 1/2 cup warm water, plus more as needed
1 cup shredded mozzarella or processed cheese
instructions:
1. Bloom the yeast and sugar in warm water for 5-10 minutes.
2. Mix the flour, salt, yogurt and oil; add the yeast mixture and knead to a soft dough; rise 1-1.5 hours.
3. Divide the dough into 4 balls and rest 10 minutes.
4. Flatten a ball into a 4-inch disc and place a quarter of the cheese in the center.
5. Gather the edges, seal well and gently roll into a 6-inch round.
6. Bake at 250°C/480°F on a preheated stone for 3-4 minutes until puffed and golden (or tawa-cook and flame-char).
7. Brush the hot naan with melted butter (mixed with garlic if using) and scatter coriander.
8. Serve immediately while the cheese is stretchy.

title: Puri
ingredients: 3/4 cup water, approximately, for a stiff dough
2 cups vegetable oil for deep frying
instructions:
1. Knead the flour, salt, oil and just enough water into a stiff, firm dough; rest 20-30 minutes.
2. Divide into 12 balls and keep them covered.
3. Roll each into a 3-4 inch disc, slightly thick and even (thin puris do not puff).
4. Heat the oil for deep frying to about 190°C/375°F; a pinch of dough should sizzle and rise instantly.
5. Slide one puri into the oil and press gently with a slotted spoon so it puffs up.
6. Once puffed, flip and fry the other side 20-30 seconds until light golden.
7. Drain on paper towels.
8. Fry the remaining puris and serve hot with aloo bhaji, chana masala or halwa.

title: Masala Chai
ingredients: 2 teaspoons loose black tea leaves (or 2 tea bags)
instructions:
1. Crush the cardamom and grate the ginger.
2. Boil the water with ginger, cardamom, cinnamon and cloves for 3-4 minutes so the spices infuse.
3. Add the tea leaves and simmer 1-2 minutes until the water turns deep amber.
4. Add the milk and sugar.
5. Bring to a boil, stirring, then lower the heat and simmer 2-3 minutes; repeat one boil-and-simmer cycle for a stronger brew.
6. Strain into cups through a fine sieve.
7. Serve hot with biscuits or pakoras.

title: Mango Lassi
ingredients: 1 1/2 cups ripe mango flesh, chopped (or 1 cup mango pulp)
2-3 tablespoons sugar or honey, to taste
chopped pistachios and a few saffron strands, to garnish
instructions:
1. Blend the mango until smooth.
2. Add the yogurt, milk, sugar and cardamom.
3. Blend 1-2 minutes until thick, creamy and frothy.
4. Taste and adjust the sweetness.
5. Add a few ice cubes and pulse once more if you like it colder.
6. Pour into tall glasses.
7. Garnish with pistachios and saffron strands.
8. Serve chilled.

title: Kashmiri Chai
ingredients: 2 tablespoons Kashmiri pink tea leaves (gulabi chai patti; or 1 tablespoon green tea leaves)
1/2 teaspoon salt for traditional noon chai, or 2 tablespoons sugar
instructions:
1. Boil the tea leaves, baking soda, cardamom and star anise with 2 cups of the cold water.
2. Boil hard for 15-20 minutes, stirring often, until the brew turns deep red and reduces to about 1 cup.
3. Add the remaining 1/2 cup cold water and boil 2 more minutes; the cold shock deepens the pink color.
4. Strain the concentrate (it can be refrigerated up to 2 days at this stage).
5. Return the concentrate to the pan and add the milk and salt (or sugar).
6. Boil 5-6 minutes, whisking or pouring back and forth between two pans to build a frothy foam.
7. Pour into cups.
8. Top each with crushed almonds and pistachios and serve hot.

title: Soda Shikanji
ingredients: 2 cups chilled lemon-lime soda or club soda
instructions:
1. Squeeze the lemons and strain 1/2 cup fresh juice into a jug.
2. Add sugar to the juice and stir until fully dissolved.
3. Add chilled water, chaat masala, roasted cumin powder, black salt, and regular salt; stir well.
4. Tear mint leaves and drop them in; chill the mixture in the fridge for 10 minutes.
5. Fill 4 glasses with ice cubes and pour the shikanji base until each glass is two-thirds full.
6. Top each glass slowly with chilled soda to keep the fizz.
7. Stir gently once, garnish with lemon slices and mint, and serve immediately.

title: Chicken Biryani
ingredients: 1 tbsp biryani masala or garam masala
2 bay leaves, 4 green cardamom, 4 cloves, 1 cinnamon stick, 1 black cardamom
1 pinch saffron soaked in 1/4 cup warm milk
1/4 cup chopped mint, 1/4 cup chopped coriander
instructions:
1. Heat oil and fry sliced onions until deep golden; reserve half as birista.
2. Marinate chicken with yogurt, ginger garlic paste, chili powder, turmeric, coriander powder, biryani masala, salt, and half the birista for 1 hour.
3. Cook the marinated chicken with chopped tomatoes on medium heat for 20 minutes until oil separates; keep the gravy thick.
4. Boil 8 cups water with bay leaves, cardamom, cloves, cinnamon, cumin, and salt; add rice and cook until 80 percent done, then drain.
5. Layer half the rice over the chicken, sprinkle mint, coriander, green chilies, and birista.
6. Add remaining rice, drizzle saffron milk on top, and cover with a tight lid.
7. Cook on high heat 5 minutes, then on very low heat (dum) for 20 minutes.
8. Rest 10 minutes, fluff gently, and serve hot with raita and salad.

title: Mutton Biryani
ingredients: 2 bay leaves, 4 green cardamom, 4 cloves, 1 cinnamon stick, 1 star anise
1 pinch saffron soaked in 1/4 cup warm milk
1/4 cup chopped mint, 1/4 cup chopped coriander
instructions:
1. Fry onions in ghee until deep golden; reserve half as birista.
2. Marinate mutton with yogurt, ginger garlic paste, chili powder, turmeric, coriander powder, biryani masala, and salt for 2 hours or overnight.
3. Cook marinated mutton with tomatoes and 1 cup hot water on low heat for 60-75 minutes until tender and oil separates.
4. Boil water with whole spices and salt; add rice and cook to 80 percent done, then drain.
5. Layer rice over mutton with mint, coriander, green chilies, and birista.
6. Top with remaining rice, kewra water, and saffron milk; seal with a tight lid.
7. Dum on high heat 5 minutes, then lowest heat 25 minutes.
8. Rest 10 minutes, fluff gently, and serve with raita and kachumber salad.

title: Chicken Karahi
instructions:
1. Heat oil in a karahi or wok; add cumin seeds until they sizzle.
2. Add chicken and ginger garlic paste; sear on high heat 5 minutes until no longer pink.
3. Add chopped tomatoes, chili powder, turmeric, crushed coriander, black pepper, and salt.
4. Cover and cook 15 minutes, stirring occasionally, until tomatoes break down into a thick masala.
5. Uncover and fry the masala on high heat 8-10 minutes until oil separates at the sides.
6. Sprinkle garam masala, add green chilies and half the ginger juliennes; cook 3 minutes.
7. Garnish with coriander leaves and remaining ginger; serve hot with naan or roti.

title: Chicken Boti Kabab
ingredients: 750 g boneless chicken, cut in 2 inch cubes
1 onion and 1 lemon, cut into wedges, for serving
instructions:
1. Whisk yogurt with ginger garlic paste, lemon juice, chili powder, cumin, coriander, garam masala, paprika, oil, and salt.
2. Add chicken cubes, coat well, and marinate at least 2 hours (overnight is best).
3. Soak wooden skewers in water for 30 minutes, or use metal skewers.
4. Thread 4-5 chicken cubes onto each skewer, leaving small gaps.
5. Grill over charcoal or under a hot oven broiler for 12-15 minutes, turning every 4 minutes.
6. Baste lightly with melted butter or oil halfway through for juiciness.
7. Rest 2 minutes, then serve hot with onion rings, lemon wedges, and mint chutney.

title: Beef Boti Kabab
ingredients: 750 g beef, cut in 2 inch cubes (sirloin or stew beef)
Onion rings, lemon wedges, and mint chutney for serving
instructions:
1. Mix beef with raw papaya paste and salt; rest 30 minutes to tenderize.
2. Whisk yogurt, ginger garlic paste, lemon juice, chili powder, cumin, coriander, garam masala, and oil into a marinade.
3. Coat beef in the marinade, cover, and refrigerate overnight.
4. Thread beef onto metal skewers, leaving small gaps between pieces.
5. Grill over medium-hot charcoal 15-18 minutes, turning every 4-5 minutes for even browning.
6. Baste with oil or melted butter during the last 5 minutes.
7. Check doneness: beef should be tender with a lightly charred crust.
8. Rest 3 minutes and serve hot with onion rings, lemon, and mint chutney.

title: Mutton Boti Kabab
ingredients: 750 g mutton leg, cut in 2 inch cubes
Onion rings, lemon wedges, and mint chutney for serving
instructions:
1. Massage mutton cubes with raw papaya paste and salt; rest 45 minutes.
2. Combine yogurt, ginger garlic paste, lemon juice, chili powder, cumin, coriander, garam masala, black pepper, and oil.
3. Coat mutton in the marinade and refrigerate overnight for best results.
4. Thread onto metal skewers with small gaps between cubes.
5. Grill over medium charcoal 18-20 minutes, turning every 5 minutes.
6. Baste with ghee in the final 5 minutes until edges char lightly.
7. Rest 3 minutes off the heat to keep the meat juicy.
8. Serve hot with onion rings, lemon wedges, and mint chutney.

title: Chicken Chapli Kabab
ingredients: Lemon wedges and raita for serving
instructions:
1. Dry-roast gram flour in a pan for 2 minutes until lightly golden; cool.
2. Mix chicken mince with egg, roasted gram flour, tomato, spring onions, coriander, and green chilies.
3. Add anardana, crushed coriander, cumin, chili powder, garam masala, black pepper, and salt.
4. Knead the mixture well for 5 minutes until sticky, then rest 30 minutes in the fridge.
5. With oiled hands, flatten portions into thin round patties about 1/2 inch thick.
6. Shallow fry in medium-hot oil 4-5 minutes per side until deep golden and cooked through.
7. Drain on paper towels.
8. Serve hot with lemon wedges, raita, and naan, or use as a burger patty.

title: Beef Chapli Kabab
ingredients: 750 g beef mince with some fat
Lemon wedges and raita for serving
instructions:
1. Roast gram flour until golden and let it cool completely.
2. Combine beef mince, egg, roasted gram flour, tomatoes, spring onions, coriander, and green chilies.
3. Season with anardana, crushed coriander, cumin, chili powder, garam masala, black pepper, and salt.
4. Knead vigorously 5-7 minutes until the mince is sticky; chill for 1 hour.
5. Press into thin 1/2 inch patties with oiled hands.
6. Fry in medium-hot oil 5-6 minutes per side until dark golden and crisp at the edges.
7. Drain on paper towels to remove excess oil.
8. Serve hot with naan, lemon wedges, raita, and sliced onions.

title: Mutton Chapli Kabab
ingredients: 1/2 cup oil or ghee for frying
Lemon wedges and raita for serving
instructions:
1. Roast gram flour until lightly golden; cool completely.
2. Mix mutton mince with egg, gram flour, tomatoes, spring onions, coriander, and green chilies.
3. Add anardana, crushed coriander, cumin, chili powder, garam masala, black pepper, and salt.
4. Knead well until sticky and uniform; refrigerate 1 hour.
5. Shape into thin round patties about 1/2 inch thick.
6. Shallow fry on medium heat 5-6 minutes per side until browned and fully cooked.
7. Drain on paper towels.
8. Serve hot with raita, lemon wedges, and naan or paratha.

title: Beef Pulao
ingredients: 750 g beef, bone-in or stew pieces
2 bay leaves, 4 green cardamom, 4 cloves, 1 cinnamon stick, 1 black cardamom
instructions:
1. Pressure cook beef with water, bay leaves, cardamom, cloves, cinnamon, black cardamom, peppercorns, and salt for 40-45 minutes until tender; reserve the stock (yakhni).
2. Heat oil in a large pot; fry onions until deep golden; remove half for garnish.
3. Add ginger garlic paste and beef; fry 5 minutes on high heat.
4. Add yogurt, garam masala, and half the herbs; cook until oil separates.
5. Add soaked rice and stir gently for 2 minutes to coat the grains.
6. Pour in 6 cups of hot beef stock; taste and adjust salt.
7. Bring to a boil, then cover and cook on low heat 15-18 minutes until rice is done and liquid absorbed.
8. Rest 10 minutes, fluff gently, garnish with fried onions, remaining herbs, and green chilies; serve with raita.

title: Chicken Curry
instructions:
1. Heat oil; add cumin seeds and bay leaves until fragrant.
2. Fry onions until golden brown, about 8-10 minutes.
3. Add ginger garlic paste and cook 1 minute.
4. Add chicken and sear on high heat 5 minutes until lightly browned.
5. Stir in turmeric, chili powder, coriander powder, and salt; cook 2 minutes.
6. Add tomatoes and cook until soft, then whisk in yogurt gradually, stirring to prevent splitting.
7. Fry the masala 8 minutes until oil separates, then pour in hot water.
8. Cover and simmer 15-20 minutes until chicken is cooked and gravy thickens.
9. Finish with garam masala, green chilies, and coriander; serve with rice or roti.

title: Beef Curry
instructions:
1. Heat oil; sizzle cumin seeds and bay leaves.
2. Fry onions until deep golden, about 10 minutes.
3. Add ginger garlic paste, then beef; sear on high heat 6-8 minutes.
4. Add turmeric, chili powder, coriander powder, and salt; stir 2 minutes.
5. Add tomatoes and cook until soft, then whisk in yogurt slowly.
6. Fry on high heat 10 minutes until oil separates from the masala.
7. Add hot water, cover, and simmer 60-75 minutes (or pressure cook 30 minutes) until beef is tender.
8. Uncover and reduce the gravy to desired consistency; sprinkle garam masala and coriander.
9. Serve hot with roti, naan, or steamed rice.

title: Mutton Curry
ingredients: 1/2 cup mustard oil or vegetable oil
instructions:
1. Heat oil; add cumin, bay leaves, cardamom, and cloves until aromatic.
2. Fry onions until golden brown.
3. Add ginger garlic paste and mutton; sear 6-8 minutes on high heat.
4. Mix in turmeric, chili powder, coriander powder, and salt.
5. Add tomatoes; cook until mushy, then stir in yogurt gradually.
6. Fry the masala 10 minutes until it darkens and oil separates.
7. Add hot water; pressure cook 25-30 minutes or simmer covered 75-90 minutes until mutton is tender.
8. Adjust gravy thickness, sprinkle garam masala and fresh coriander.
9. Serve hot with rice, roti, or paratha.

title: Chicken Nihari
ingredients: Garnish: 2 inch ginger julienned, 4 green chilies sliced, lemon wedges, chopped coriander, chaat masala
instructions:
1. Heat ghee; add bay leaves and chicken; sear 5 minutes on high heat.
2. Add ginger garlic paste and cook 2 minutes.
3. Mix in turmeric, chili powder, coriander, fennel, cumin, and salt; cook 3 minutes.
4. Pour in water, cover, and simmer 30 minutes until chicken is tender.
5. Whisk flour with 1/2 cup water into a smooth slurry.
6. Stir the slurry into the pot and simmer 15 minutes, stirring often, until the gravy thickens to a silky consistency.
7. Add garam masala, nutmeg, and mace; simmer 5 more minutes.
8. Serve hot topped with ginger juliennes, green chilies, coriander, a squeeze of lemon, and a pinch of chaat masala, with naan.

title: Mutton Nihari
ingredients: Garnish: ginger juliennes, green chilies, lemon wedges, chopped coriander, chaat masala
instructions:
1. Heat ghee; sear mutton shanks on high heat 6 minutes until browned.
2. Add ginger garlic paste, bay leaves, and all ground spices with salt; cook 3 minutes.
3. Add water, bring to a boil, then cover and simmer on low heat 2.5-3 hours (or pressure cook 45 minutes) until the meat is tender.
4. Whisk atta with 1 cup water to a smooth slurry.
5. Stir the slurry into the pot and simmer 20 minutes until the gravy thickens.
6. Add garam masala, nutmeg, and mace; simmer 5 minutes.
7. Adjust salt and consistency; the gravy should coat a spoon lightly.
8. Serve hot with ginger juliennes, green chilies, coriander, lemon, and chaat masala alongside naan.

title: Chicken Haleem
ingredients: 2 tbsp each: chana dal, masoor dal, moong dal, mash dal, soaked 2 hours
For garnish: 1 fried onion (birista), ginger juliennes, mint leaves, lemon wedges, chaat masala, green chilies
instructions:
1. Pressure cook soaked wheat, barley, and lentils with 6 cups water and 1 tsp salt for 40 minutes until very soft.
2. Blend or mash the cooked grains to a coarse paste; set aside.
3. Heat ghee; add ginger garlic paste and chicken; sear 5 minutes.
4. Add turmeric, chili powder, coriander powder, cumin, garam masala, and salt; cook 3 minutes.
5. Add 2 cups water and cook chicken 20 minutes until tender; shred it finely with two forks.
6. Combine shredded chicken and its masala with the grain paste in a large pot.
7. Cook on low heat 30-40 minutes, stirring often, adding hot water as needed until thick and smooth.
8. Finish by frying with 2 tbsp ghee for 10 minutes until the haleem turns glossy.
9. Serve hot topped with birista, ginger, mint, green chilies, lemon, and chaat masala.

title: Beef Haleem
ingredients: 2 tbsp each: chana dal, masoor dal, moong dal, mash dal, soaked 2 hours
For garnish: fried onions, ginger juliennes, mint leaves, lemon wedges, chaat masala, green chilies
instructions:
1. Pressure cook beef with ginger garlic paste, turmeric, half the chili powder, and salt in 4 cups water for 45 minutes until falling apart.
2. Shred the beef; strain and reserve the stock.
3. In the same cooker, add soaked wheat, barley, lentils, and 5 cups of the reserved stock; cook 40 minutes until mushy.
4. Mash or blend the grain mixture to a coarse, sticky paste.
5. Heat ghee; add shredded beef, remaining chili powder, coriander, cumin, and garam masala; fry 5 minutes.
6. Combine the grain paste with the beef mixture in a large pot.
7. Simmer on low 40-50 minutes, stirring frequently, adding hot water if it gets too thick.
8. Finish with a final fry in ghee until the haleem is smooth, thick, and glossy.
9. Serve hot with fried onions, ginger, mint, lemon, green chilies, and chaat masala.

title: Mutton Haleem
ingredients: 2 tbsp each: chana dal, masoor dal, moong dal, mash dal, soaked 2 hours
For garnish: fried onions, ginger juliennes, mint leaves, lemon wedges, chaat masala, green chilies
instructions:
1. Pressure cook mutton with ginger garlic paste, turmeric, half the chili powder, and salt in 4 cups water for 45-50 minutes until very tender.
2. Remove bones, shred the meat, and reserve the stock.
3. Cook soaked wheat, barley, and lentils in 5 cups reserved stock for 40 minutes until soft and mushy.
4. Mash or blend the grains into a coarse paste.
5. Heat ghee; add shredded mutton, remaining chili powder, coriander, cumin, and garam masala; fry 5 minutes.
6. Mix the grain paste with the mutton in a heavy pot.
7. Simmer on low heat 40-50 minutes, stirring often, thinning with hot water as needed.
8. Finish with a final fry in ghee until thick, smooth, and glossy.
9. Serve hot garnished with fried onions, ginger, mint, lemon, green chilies, and chaat masala.

title: Chicken Shashlik
ingredients: 750 g boneless chicken, cut in 1.5 inch cubes
2 green bell peppers, cut in squares
For sauce: 1/2 cup ketchup, 2 tbsp chili sauce, 1 tbsp soy sauce, 1 tsp sugar, 1/4 cup water
instructions:
1. Marinate chicken with soy sauce, chili sauce, vinegar, ketchup, ginger garlic paste, black pepper, cornflour, and salt for 1 hour.
2. Soak wooden skewers in water 30 minutes or use metal ones.
3. Thread chicken alternately with bell pepper, onion, and tomato onto skewers.
4. Heat oil in a large pan or grill pan on medium-high heat.
5. Cook skewers 12-15 minutes, turning every 3-4 minutes, until charred and cooked through.
6. Meanwhile, simmer all sauce ingredients in a small pan for 3-4 minutes until slightly thick.
7. Brush the sauce over the cooked skewers or serve it on the side.
8. Serve hot with fried rice, French fries, or naan.

title: Beef Shashlik
ingredients: 750 g beef sirloin or tenderloin, cut in 1.5 inch cubes
2 green bell peppers, cut in squares
For sauce: 1/2 cup ketchup, 2 tbsp chili sauce, 1 tbsp soy sauce, 1 tsp sugar, 1/4 cup water
instructions:
1. Tenderize beef with raw papaya paste and salt for 45 minutes.
2. Marinate with soy sauce, chili sauce, vinegar, ginger garlic paste, black pepper, and cornflour for 2 hours or overnight.
3. Soak wooden skewers in water for 30 minutes.
4. Thread beef alternately with bell peppers, onions, and tomatoes.
5. Grill over charcoal or a hot grill pan 15-18 minutes, turning every 4 minutes.
6. Baste with oil during cooking to keep the meat moist.
7. Simmer sauce ingredients in a small pan 3-4 minutes until glossy and slightly thick.
8. Serve skewers hot, drizzled or dipped in the sauce, with fried rice or fries.

title: Mutton Shashlik
ingredients: 750 g mutton leg, cut in 1.5 inch cubes
2 green bell peppers, cut in squares
For sauce: 1/2 cup ketchup, 2 tbsp chili sauce, 1 tbsp soy sauce, 1 tsp sugar, 1/4 cup water
instructions:
1. Massage mutton cubes with raw papaya paste and salt; rest 45 minutes.
2. Marinate with soy sauce, chili sauce, vinegar, ginger garlic paste, black pepper, and cornflour overnight.
3. Soak wooden skewers 30 minutes or use metal skewers.
4. Thread mutton alternately with bell peppers, onions, and tomatoes.
5. Grill over medium-hot charcoal 18-20 minutes, turning every 4-5 minutes.
6. Baste with oil in the last 5 minutes until edges char lightly.
7. Simmer sauce ingredients 3-4 minutes until slightly thickened.
8. Serve hot with the sauce, fried rice, or naan.

title: Chicken Aloo Gosht
instructions:
1. Heat oil; sizzle cumin seeds and bay leaves.
2. Fry onions until golden brown.
3. Add ginger garlic paste and chicken; sear 5 minutes.
4. Stir in turmeric, chili powder, coriander powder, and salt; cook 2 minutes.
5. Add tomatoes and yogurt; fry 8-10 minutes until oil separates.
6. Add potatoes and hot water; cover and simmer 20-25 minutes until potatoes are fork-tender.
7. Sprinkle garam masala and simmer 5 minutes to thicken the gravy.
8. Garnish with coriander leaves and serve with roti, naan, or rice.

title: Beef Aloo Gosht
instructions:
1. Heat oil; add cumin seeds and bay leaves until fragrant.
2. Fry onions until deep golden.
3. Add ginger garlic paste and beef; sear on high heat 6-8 minutes.
4. Mix in turmeric, chili powder, coriander powder, and salt.
5. Add tomatoes and yogurt; fry 10 minutes until oil separates.
6. Pour in hot water, cover, and simmer 60-75 minutes (or pressure cook 30 minutes) until beef is tender.
7. Add potatoes and cook 20 minutes more until soft and the gravy thickens.
8. Sprinkle garam masala and coriander; simmer 5 minutes.
9. Serve hot with roti, naan, or steamed rice.

title: Mutton Aloo Gosht
ingredients: 1 kg mutton (goat or lamb) on the bone, cut into medium pieces
3 medium tomatoes, finely chopped or pureed
Fresh coriander leaves, chopped, for garnish
instructions:
1. Heat oil in a large heavy-bottomed pot or karahi over medium-high heat. Add cumin seeds, bay leaves, black cardamom, green cardamom, cinnamon stick, and cloves; sauté for 30 seconds until fragrant.
2. Add the sliced onions and fry, stirring often, for 10-12 minutes until deep golden brown.
3. Add the ginger-garlic paste and cook for 1 minute, then add the mutton pieces and sear on high heat for 5-6 minutes until the meat is browned on all sides.
4. Add red chili powder, coriander powder, turmeric, and salt. Stir well, then add the chopped tomatoes. Cook, stirring frequently, for 8-10 minutes until the tomatoes break down and oil separates from the masala at the sides.
5. Lower the heat and add the whisked yogurt a spoonful at a time, stirring constantly to prevent curdling. Bhunao (fry) the masala for another 5-7 minutes until thick and glossy.
6. Pour in 2 cups of hot water, bring to a boil, then cover and simmer on low heat for 45-50 minutes, or pressure cook for 25-30 minutes, until the mutton is nearly tender.
7. Add the potato quarters and slit green chilies, stir gently, cover again, and cook for 15-20 minutes until the potatoes are soft and have absorbed the flavors of the gravy.
8. Uncover, sprinkle in the garam masala, and simmer uncovered for 5 minutes to let the gravy thicken to a medium consistency.
9. Garnish with fresh coriander leaves and ginger juliennes. Serve hot with roti, naan, or steamed basmati rice.

title: Chicken Rezala
ingredients: 1 kg halal chicken, cut into 8 pieces
instructions:
1. Marinate chicken with yogurt, ginger-garlic paste, salt, white pepper, and half the green chilies for 30 minutes.
2. Heat ghee and oil in a heavy pot; add bay leaves, green cardamoms, black cardamoms, and cinnamon until fragrant.
3. Add onion paste and cook on medium heat until pale golden and the raw smell disappears.
4. Stir in poppy seed paste and cashew paste; cook 2-3 minutes without browning.
5. Add marinated chicken and cook on high heat for 5 minutes, turning to seal the pieces.
6. Lower heat, cover, and simmer 20-25 minutes until chicken is tender, stirring occasionally.
7. Add remaining green chilies, sugar, and a splash of water if needed; simmer 5 minutes until gravy is glossy.
8. Finish with kewra water and 1 tbsp ghee; rest 5 minutes and serve with pulao or paratha.

title: Beef Rezala
ingredients: 1 kg halal beef, cut into 1.5-inch cubes
instructions:
1. Pressure cook beef with ginger-garlic paste, salt, and 1 cup water for 20-25 minutes until tender; reserve stock.
2. Heat ghee and oil in a pot; add bay leaves, green cardamoms, black cardamoms, and cinnamon.
3. Add onion paste and cook until light golden and aromatic.
4. Stir in poppy seed paste and cashew paste; cook 2 minutes on low heat.
5. Add boiled beef and sear on high heat for 4-5 minutes.
6. Add yogurt, white pepper, green chilies, sugar, and reserved beef stock; mix well.
7. Cover and simmer 15-20 minutes until beef is soft and gravy is thick and glossy.
8. Finish with kewra water and 1 tbsp ghee; rest 5 minutes before serving.

title: Chicken Handi
ingredients: 1 kg halal chicken, cut into pieces
instructions:
1. Heat oil and ghee in a handi or heavy pan; fry onions until golden brown.
2. Add ginger-garlic paste and cook 1 minute until raw smell disappears.
3. Add tomatoes, red chili, turmeric, cumin, coriander, and salt; cook until tomatoes soften.
4. Add chicken and sear on high heat for 5-6 minutes.
5. Lower heat, add yogurt, and cook 8-10 minutes until oil separates.
6. Add 1/2 cup water, cover, and simmer 15 minutes until chicken is tender.
7. Stir in cream, green chilies, garam masala, and kasuri methi; simmer 5 minutes.
8. Rest 5 minutes and serve hot with naan or roti.

title: Mutton Handi
ingredients: 1 kg halal mutton, cut into pieces
instructions:
1. Heat oil and ghee in a handi; fry onions until deep golden.
2. Add ginger-garlic paste and cook 1 minute.
3. Add tomatoes and dry spices; cook until tomatoes break down.
4. Add mutton and sear on high heat for 6-8 minutes.
5. Add yogurt and cook until it thickens and oil separates.
6. Add 2 cups water, cover, and simmer 60-75 minutes until mutton is tender.
7. Stir in cream, green chilies, garam masala, and kasuri methi; simmer 8 minutes.
8. Rest 5 minutes and serve with naan or boiled rice.

title: Beef Handi
ingredients: 1 kg halal beef, cut into 1.5-inch cubes
instructions:
1. Pressure cook beef with 1 tsp salt and 1 cup water for 20-25 minutes until tender; reserve stock.
2. Heat oil and ghee in a handi; fry onions until golden.
3. Add ginger-garlic paste, tomatoes, red chili, turmeric, cumin, and coriander; cook until thick.
4. Add boiled beef and sear 5 minutes.
5. Add yogurt and cook 8 minutes until oil separates.
6. Add reserved stock, cover, and simmer 15 minutes.
7. Stir in cream, green chilies, garam masala, and kasuri methi; simmer 5 minutes.
8. Rest 5 minutes and serve hot with naan or rice.

title: Chicken Kofta Curry
instructions:
1. Mix minced chicken, grated onion, ginger-garlic, green chilies, coriander, garam masala, cumin, red chili, gram flour, egg, and salt.
2. Shape into small kofta balls and refrigerate 15 minutes.
3. Heat 2 tbsp oil and lightly fry koftas until browned; set aside.
4. In another pan, heat remaining oil and fry chopped onions until golden.
5. Add ginger-garlic paste, tomato puree, red chili, turmeric, coriander, and salt; cook until oil separates.
6. Whisk yogurt and add to gravy; cook 5 minutes on low heat.
7. Add 1 cup water and simmer 5 minutes, then gently add koftas.
8. Cover and cook 10-12 minutes on low heat; garnish with coriander and serve with rice or roti.

title: Beef Kofta Curry
instructions:
1. Mix minced beef, grated onion, ginger-garlic, green chilies, coriander, garam masala, cumin, red chili, gram flour, egg, and salt.
2. Form into smooth kofta balls and chill 15 minutes.
3. Heat 2 tbsp oil and brown koftas on all sides; remove and set aside.
4. Heat remaining oil and fry chopped onions until golden.
5. Add ginger-garlic paste, tomato puree, red chili, turmeric, coriander, and salt; cook until oil separates.
6. Add whisked yogurt and cook 5 minutes, stirring continuously.
7. Add 1 cup water, bring to simmer, and gently slide in koftas.
8. Cover and cook 12-15 minutes until koftas are cooked through; garnish with coriander and serve.

title: Fish Kofta Curry
instructions:
1. Mix minced fish, chopped onion, ginger, garlic, green chilies, coriander, turmeric, red chili, cumin, egg, breadcrumbs, and salt.
2. Shape into small koftas and refrigerate 20 minutes.
3. Steam koftas for 8-10 minutes or shallow fry lightly until firm; set aside.
4. Heat mustard oil in a pan and fry onion paste until golden.
5. Add ginger-garlic paste, turmeric, red chili, cumin, coriander, and tomato puree; cook until oil separates.
6. Add yogurt and cook 4-5 minutes on low heat.
7. Add 1 cup water and simmer 5 minutes, then gently add fish koftas and green chilies.
8. Cover and cook 8-10 minutes on low heat; serve with steamed rice.

title: Chicken.Changezi
ingredients: 1 kg halal chicken, cut into pieces
instructions:
1. Marinate chicken with yogurt, ginger-garlic paste, red chili, turmeric, and salt for 1 hour.
2. Heat 1 tbsp oil in a grill pan and sear chicken pieces until lightly charred; set aside.
3. Heat ghee and remaining oil in a pan; fry onions until golden.
4. Add tomato puree and cook until oil separates.
5. Add garam masala and a splash of water; cook 2 minutes.
6. Add seared chicken and cook 8-10 minutes, turning to coat in gravy.
7. Stir in cream and kasuri methi; simmer 5 minutes until chicken is tender.
8. Garnish with coriander and serve with naan or jeera rice.

title: Chicken Wings (Fried)
ingredients: 1 kg halal chicken wings, separated at joints
instructions:
1. Wash and pat dry chicken wings; make small slits if desired.
2. Mix yogurt, ginger-garlic, red chili, turmeric, cumin, coriander, garam masala, lemon juice, and salt.
3. Coat wings with marinade and refrigerate 2 hours.
4. Add gram flour, cornflour, and egg to the wings; mix until evenly coated.
5. Heat oil in a deep pan to medium-high.
6. Fry wings in batches for 6-8 minutes until golden and cooked through.
7. Drain on paper towels and rest 2 minutes.
8. Serve hot with lemon wedges and mint chutney.

title: Chicken Lollipop
instructions:
1. Prepare chicken lollipops by pushing meat down the bone; pat dry.
2. Marinate with ginger-garlic, soy sauce, chili sauce, ketchup, red chili, black pepper, and salt for 1 hour.
3. Dip each lollipop in beaten egg, then coat with cornflour and breadcrumbs.
4. Heat oil and fry lollipops in batches until golden and cooked through; drain.
5. For sauce, heat 1 tbsp oil and sauté garlic until fragrant.
6. Add chili sauce, ketchup, soy sauce, honey, and water; simmer 2 minutes.
7. Toss fried lollipops in sauce until coated.
8. Serve hot with extra sauce or mint chutney.

title: Mutton Chops
instructions:
1. Mix yogurt, ginger-garlic, red chili, turmeric, cumin, coriander, garam masala, lemon juice, and salt.
2. Coat mutton chops with marinade and refrigerate 4 hours or overnight.
3. Pressure cook chops with 1/2 cup water for 15-18 minutes until tender; reserve liquid.
4. Heat oil and ghee in a pan; add boiled chops and fry until browned.
5. Add fried onions and reserved cooking liquid.
6. Cook on high heat until liquid thickens and coats the chops.
7. Sprinkle a pinch of garam masala and lemon juice.
8. Rest 5 minutes and serve with naan or pulao.

title: Beef Chaap
ingredients: 750 g halal beef undercut or chaap slices
instructions:
1. Pound beef slices lightly with a mallet to tenderize.
2. Mix raw papaya paste, yogurt, ginger-garlic, red chili, turmeric, cumin, coriander, garam masala, lemon juice, and salt.
3. Coat beef slices with marinade and refrigerate 4 hours.
4. Heat mustard oil and ghee in a heavy pan.
5. Sear beef slices on high heat for 2 minutes per side.
6. Add remaining marinade and 1/2 cup water; cover and cook 20-25 minutes until tender.
7. Uncover and bhuna on high heat until masala clings to the beef.
8. Rest 5 minutes and serve with paratha or rice.

title: Chicken Chaap
ingredients: 1 kg halal chicken, cut into large pieces
instructions:
1. Mix yogurt, cashew paste, poppy paste, onion paste, ginger-garlic, white pepper, mace, sugar, and salt.
2. Coat chicken with marinade and refrigerate 2 hours.
3. Heat ghee in a heavy pot; add bay leaves and green cardamoms.
4. Add marinated chicken and cook on high heat 5 minutes.
5. Lower heat, cover, and cook 20 minutes until chicken is tender.
6. Add saffron milk and green chilies; mix gently.
7. Simmer uncovered 8-10 minutes until gravy is thick and glossy.
8. Rest 5 minutes and serve with kacchi biryani rice or paratha.

title: Grill Chicken (Desi Style)
instructions:
1. Make deep slits in chicken breast, thighs, and legs.
2. Mix yogurt, ginger-garlic, red chili, cumin, coriander, garam masala, turmeric, lemon juice, oil, gram flour, and salt.
3. Rub marinade all over chicken and inside slits; refrigerate 4 hours or overnight.
4. Preheat oven or grill to 200 C.
5. Place chicken on a rack over a baking tray.
6. Grill 45-50 minutes, turning every 15 minutes and basting with remaining marinade.
7. Increase heat to 220 C for last 8 minutes to char the skin.
8. Rest 10 minutes, cut into pieces, and serve with raita and salad.

title: Roast Chicken Bangladeshi
instructions:
1. Prick chicken all over with a fork and make small slits.
2. Mix yogurt, onion paste, ginger-garlic, red chili, turmeric, cumin, coriander, garam masala, mustard oil, lemon juice, and salt.
3. Rub marinade over chicken and inside cavity; marinate 4 hours.
4. Heat ghee in a heavy pot and sear chicken on all sides until lightly browned.
5. Add remaining marinade, green chilies, and 1/2 cup water.
6. Cover and cook on low heat 35-40 minutes, turning once.
7. Uncover and roast on medium heat until sauce thickens and chicken is glossy.
8. Rest 10 minutes, then cut and serve with polao or plain rice.

title: Chicken Jhal Fry Makhani
ingredients: 1 kg halal chicken, cut into pieces
instructions:
1. Heat oil in a pan and fry onions until golden.
2. Add ginger-garlic paste and cook 1 minute.
3. Add tomato puree, turmeric, red chili, cumin, coriander, and salt; cook until oil separates.
4. Add chicken and sear on high heat 5 minutes.
5. Add yogurt and green chilies; cook 8 minutes until chicken is coated.
6. Add 1/2 cup water, cover, and simmer 15 minutes until chicken is tender.
7. Stir in butter and cream; simmer 5 minutes until gravy is rich and glossy.
8. Garnish with coriander and serve with naan or rice.

title: Mutton Kosha
ingredients: 1 kg halal mutton, cut into pieces
instructions:
1. Heat mustard oil and ghee in a pressure cooker; add bay leaves, cardamoms, and cinnamon.
2. Add sliced onions and fry until deep golden.
3. Add ginger-garlic paste and cook 1 minute.
4. Add mutton and sear on high heat 6-8 minutes.
5. Add turmeric, red chili, cumin, coriander, sugar, salt, and yogurt; cook until oil separates.
6. Add potatoes and 1 cup water; pressure cook 20-25 minutes until mutton is tender.
7. Uncover and bhuna on high heat until gravy is dark, thick, and clings to the meat.
8. Sprinkle garam masala, rest 5 minutes, and serve with paratha or rice.

title: Mutton Bhuna
ingredients: 1 kg halal mutton, cut into pieces
instructions:
1. Heat oil in a pressure cooker; add bay leaves, cardamoms, and cinnamon.
2. Add onions and fry until golden brown.
3. Add ginger-garlic paste and cook 1 minute.
4. Add mutton and sear on high heat 6-8 minutes.
5. Add tomatoes, red chili, turmeric, cumin, coriander, and salt; cook until tomatoes soften.
6. Add yogurt and cook until oil separates.
7. Add 1 cup water and pressure cook 20-25 minutes until mutton is tender.
8. Uncover and bhuna on high heat until gravy is thick and oil separates; sprinkle garam masala and serve.

title: Chicken Rezala Kolkata
ingredients: 1 kg halal chicken, cut into pieces
instructions:
1. Marinate chicken with yogurt, ginger-garlic, salt, white pepper, and half the green chilies for 30 minutes.
2. Heat ghee in a heavy pot; add bay leaves, green cardamoms, black cardamoms, and cinnamon.
3. Add onion paste and cook until pale golden.
4. Stir in poppy seed paste and cashew paste; cook 2 minutes on low heat.
5. Add marinated chicken and cook on high heat 5 minutes.
6. Lower heat, cover, and simmer 20 minutes until chicken is tender.
7. Add remaining green chilies, sugar, and a splash of water; simmer 5 minutes.
8. Finish with kewra water and serve with Kolkata-style pulao or paratha.

title: Beef Gateko
ingredients: 1 kg halal beef, cut into bite-size pieces
1 tbsp timur or Sichuan pepper, crushed
instructions:
1. Pressure cook beef with turmeric, salt, and 1 cup water for 20-25 minutes until tender; reserve stock.
2. Heat mustard oil in a pan; add bay leaves and onions.
3. Fry onions until golden brown.
4. Add ginger-garlic paste and cook 1 minute.
5. Add tomatoes, red chili, cumin, coriander, and timur; cook until oil separates.
6. Add boiled beef and reserved stock; mix well.
7. Simmer 15-20 minutes until gravy thickens and coats the beef.
8. Add green chilies, garnish with coriander, and serve with rice or roti.

title: Beef Tehri
ingredients: 500 g halal beef, cut into small cubes
instructions:
1. Heat ghee in a pressure cooker; add bay leaves, cardamoms, and cinnamon.
2. Add onions and fry until golden.
3. Add ginger-garlic paste, beef, tomato, turmeric, red chili, cumin, coriander, and salt; sear 5 minutes.
4. Add yogurt and cook until oil separates.
5. Add 1 cup water and pressure cook 20 minutes until beef is tender.
6. Add potatoes and peas; cook 5 minutes.
7. Add soaked rice, garam masala, and 3.5 cups water; bring to a boil.
8. Cover and cook on low 15-18 minutes until rice is done; rest 10 minutes and fluff.

title: Chicken Yakhni Pulao
ingredients: 1 kg halal chicken, cut into pieces
instructions:
1. In a pot, add chicken, ginger-garlic, green cardamoms, black cardamoms, bay leaves, cinnamon, cloves, fennel, cumin, coriander, salt, and 6 cups water.
2. Boil 20 minutes until chicken is tender; strain and reserve yakhni stock and chicken separately.
3. Heat ghee in a heavy pot and fry onion until golden.
4. Add boiled chicken and yogurt; cook 5 minutes.
5. Add green chilies and 4.5 cups reserved yakhni; bring to a boil.
6. Add soaked rice and stir gently.
7. Cook uncovered until water reduces to rice level, then cover and steam on low 15 minutes.
8. Rest 10 minutes, fluff with a fork, and serve with raita.

title: Mutton Rib Curry
instructions:
1. Heat oil in a pressure cooker; add bay leaves, cardamoms, and cinnamon.
2. Add onions and fry until deep golden.
3. Add ginger-garlic paste and cook 1 minute.
4. Add mutton ribs and sear on high heat 6-8 minutes.
5. Add tomatoes, red chili, turmeric, cumin, coriander, and salt; cook until tomatoes soften.
6. Add yogurt and cook until oil separates.
7. Add 1.5 cups water and pressure cook 25-30 minutes until ribs are tender.
8. Uncover and simmer until gravy is thick; sprinkle garam masala and serve with naan or rice.

title: Beef Riyasht
instructions:
1. Mix ground beef, grated onion, garlic, coriander, cumin, coriander powder, turmeric, red chili, chickpea flour, egg, and salt.
2. Knead well and shape into small meatballs.
3. Heat 1 tbsp oil in a pan and brown meatballs on all sides; remove and set aside.
4. Heat remaining oil and fry chopped onions until golden.
5. Add garlic, tomato puree, cumin, coriander, turmeric, and salt; cook until oil separates.
6. Add yogurt and cook 5 minutes on low heat.
7. Add 1 cup water and simmer 5 minutes, then gently add meatballs.
8. Cover and cook 15 minutes until meatballs are tender; garnish with coriander and serve with naan or rice.

title: Kalo Bhuna
ingredients: halal beef chuck 1 kg, cut into 1.5 inch cubes
instructions:
1. In a bowl, mix beef with yogurt, turmeric, red chili, coriander, cumin, black pepper, ginger garlic paste, and salt. Marinate 30 minutes.
2. Heat mustard oil in a heavy pot over medium heat. Fry onions until deep golden brown, about 8-10 minutes.
3. Add the marinated beef and cook on high heat for 5 minutes, stirring, until the meat changes color.
4. Reduce heat to low, cover, and cook 40 minutes, stirring occasionally so it does not stick.
5. Add 1 cup water, cover, and simmer 30-40 minutes until beef is tender and liquid has reduced.
6. Uncover, increase heat, and bhuna the beef for 10-12 minutes until the masala is very dark, thick, and oil separates.
7. Add green chilies, garam masala, and sugar. Stir and cook 3 minutes.
8. Rest 5 minutes, then serve hot with paratha or plain rice.

title: Beef Hatkhora
ingredients: halal beef 1 kg, cut into 1.5 inch cubes
instructions:
1. Soak bamboo shoots in warm water for 30 minutes, then boil 10 minutes and drain well.
2. Heat mustard oil in a pressure cooker or heavy pot. Add bay leaves, black cardamom, and cinnamon.
3. Add onions and fry until golden brown, about 8 minutes.
4. Add ginger garlic paste, turmeric, red chili, coriander, cumin, and salt. Stir 1 minute.
5. Add beef and cook on high heat 5 minutes, then add yogurt and cook until it thickens.
6. Add drained bamboo shoots and mix well. Add 2 cups water.
7. Cover and pressure cook 25 minutes, or simmer covered 1 hour until beef is tender.
8. Uncover and bhuna on high heat until the gravy is thick and oil separates. Add green chilies and garam masala, cook 3 minutes, and serve.

title: Panshi Macher Jhal
ingredients: panshi fish 700 g, cleaned and cut into pieces
instructions:
1. Rub fish with a pinch of turmeric, red chili, and salt. Rest 15 minutes.
2. Heat mustard oil in a pan and lightly fry the fish 2 minutes per side. Remove and set aside.
3. In the same oil, add onion paste, ginger paste, and garlic paste. Fry until raw smell disappears.
4. Add turmeric, red chili, cumin, coriander, and tomato. Cook 5 minutes until thick.
5. Add 1 1/2 cups water and bring to a simmer. Cook 5 minutes to make a jhal gravy.
6. Gently slide in the fried fish and green chilies. Simmer 8 minutes without stirring roughly.
7. Taste for salt, sprinkle cilantro, and serve hot with steamed rice.

title: Koral Macher Jhal
ingredients: koral fish 700 g, cut into steaks
instructions:
1. Marinate koral fish with turmeric, red chili, and salt for 15 minutes.
2. Heat mustard oil and fry fish lightly, about 2 minutes per side. Remove carefully.
3. In the same oil, fry onion until soft and light golden.
4. Add ginger garlic paste, turmeric, red chili, cumin, coriander, and tomato. Cook 5-6 minutes.
5. Add 1 1/2 cups water and simmer 5 minutes to form a spicy jhal gravy.
6. Add fried fish and green chilies. Cover and simmer 8 minutes on low heat.
7. Adjust salt, garnish with cilantro, and serve with plain rice.

title: Teli Koi
ingredients: koi fish 4 whole, about 800 g, cleaned and scored
instructions:
1. Rub koi fish with turmeric, red chili, and salt. Rest 15 minutes.
2. Heat 1/2 cup mustard oil in a wide pan and fry fish until golden on both sides. Remove.
3. Add remaining oil to the pan and fry onions until golden brown.
4. Add ginger garlic paste, turmeric, red chili, cumin, and coriander. Stir 1 minute.
5. Add tomatoes and cook until soft and oil separates.
6. Add 2 cups water and bring to a boil, then simmer 5 minutes.
7. Gently add fried fish and green chilies. Cover and simmer 10 minutes.
8. Drizzle 2 tbsp raw mustard oil on top, rest 5 minutes, and serve with rice.

title: Koi Macher Tel Jhol
ingredients: koi fish 4 whole, about 800 g, cleaned
instructions:
1. Rub koi fish with turmeric, red chili, and salt. Rest 15 minutes.
2. Heat mustard oil and lightly fry fish 2 minutes per side. Remove.
3. In the same oil, add nigella seeds and let them sizzle.
4. Add ginger paste, turmeric, red chili, and tomato. Cook 4 minutes.
5. Add 2 cups water and simmer 5 minutes to make a thin tel jhol.
6. Add fried fish and green chilies. Simmer 8-10 minutes on low heat.
7. Drizzle 1 tbsp raw mustard oil, garnish with cilantro, and serve with hot rice.

title: Shol Macher Kalia
ingredients: shol fish 800 g, cut into thick pieces
instructions:
1. Marinate shol fish with turmeric, red chili, and salt for 15 minutes.
2. Heat mustard oil and fry fish lightly, about 2 minutes per side. Remove.
3. In the same oil, add bay leaves, green cardamom, and cinnamon. Sizzle 30 seconds.
4. Add onion paste and ginger garlic paste. Fry until golden and fragrant.
5. Add turmeric, red chili, coriander, cumin, and yogurt. Cook until oil separates.
6. Add 1 1/2 cups water and simmer 5 minutes to make kalia gravy.
7. Gently add fried fish and green chilies. Cover and simmer 10 minutes.
8. Sprinkle garam masala, rest 5 minutes, and serve with polao or rice.

title: Hilsa Bhapa
ingredients: banana leaves or foil for wrapping
instructions:
1. In a bowl, mix yellow mustard paste, black mustard paste, poppy seed paste, turmeric, red chili, onion paste, ginger paste, yogurt, salt, and 2 tbsp mustard oil.
2. Coat hilsa pieces gently with the mustard mixture. Marinate 20 minutes.
3. Cut banana leaves into squares and soften them over flame, or use foil.
4. Place fish with marinade on each leaf and top with green chilies.
5. Wrap tightly into parcels so steam does not escape.
6. Steam in a steamer or covered pan with water for 15-20 minutes until fish is cooked.
7. Open carefully, heat remaining mustard oil until smoking, pour over fish, and serve with steamed rice.

title: Chingri Posto
instructions:
1. Drain poppy seeds and grind with 2-3 tbsp water into a smooth paste.
2. Rub prawns with turmeric, red chili, and salt. Rest 10 minutes.
3. Heat mustard oil and lightly fry prawns 2 minutes. Remove and set aside.
4. In the same oil, fry onion until soft, then add ginger paste and garlic paste.
5. Add turmeric, red chili, tomato, and salt. Cook 5 minutes until thick.
6. Add poppy seed paste and 1 cup water. Simmer 6-8 minutes, stirring often.
7. Add fried prawns and green chilies. Cook 5 minutes until prawns are tender and gravy is thick.
8. Drizzle 1 tsp mustard oil, rest 2 minutes, and serve with rice.

title: Chingri Bhapa
ingredients: banana leaf or foil for wrapping
instructions:
1. In a bowl, mix mustard paste, poppy seed paste, coconut, turmeric, red chili, yogurt, salt, green chilies, and 2 tbsp mustard oil.
2. Add prawns and coat well. Marinate 15 minutes.
3. Prepare banana leaf squares or foil pieces.
4. Place prawn mixture in the center of each leaf and wrap tightly.
5. Steam in a steamer or covered pan with water for 12-15 minutes.
6. Check that prawns are opaque and cooked through.
7. Open parcels, drizzle remaining mustard oil, and serve hot with plain rice.

title: Chingri Malai
instructions:
1. Rub prawns with turmeric, red chili, and salt. Rest 10 minutes.
2. Heat mustard oil and lightly fry prawns 2 minutes. Remove.
3. In the same oil, fry onion paste and ginger garlic paste until soft and fragrant.
4. Add turmeric, red chili, cumin, coriander, and salt. Cook 3 minutes.
5. Pour in coconut milk and cream. Stir and simmer 5 minutes.
6. Add fried prawns and green chilies. Simmer 5-6 minutes until prawns are cooked.
7. Add garam masala and sugar. Mix gently.
8. Rest 3 minutes and serve with steamed rice or paratha.

title: Golda Chingri Curry
ingredients: golda prawns 500 g, peeled and deveined
instructions:
1. Rub golda prawns with turmeric, red chili, and salt. Rest 10 minutes.
2. Heat mustard oil and lightly fry prawns 2 minutes per side. Remove.
3. In the same oil, fry onion paste until golden, then add ginger garlic paste.
4. Add turmeric, red chili, cumin, coriander, and tomato puree. Cook 6-8 minutes until oil separates.
5. Add coconut milk and 1/2 cup water. Simmer 5 minutes.
6. Add fried prawns and green chilies. Simmer 6 minutes until prawns are tender.
7. Add sugar and adjust salt. Cook 2 minutes.
8. Rest 3 minutes and serve with rice or luchi.

title: Daal Makhani Methi
instructions:
1. Wash urad dal and rajma, then soak in plenty of water for 8 hours or overnight.
2. Drain and pressure cook with 4 cups water and salt until very soft, about 6-8 whistles.
3. Heat butter and oil in a pan. Add cumin seeds and let them crackle.
4. Add onion and fry until golden, then add ginger garlic paste and green chilies.
5. Add tomato puree, red chili, turmeric, and coriander. Cook 8-10 minutes until thick.
6. Add the cooked dal with its liquid. Simmer on low heat 30 minutes, stirring often.
7. Add chopped fenugreek leaves and cook 8 minutes until wilted.
8. Stir in garam masala, remaining butter, and cream. Simmer 5 minutes and serve hot.

title: Methi Chicken
ingredients: halal chicken 1 kg, cut into pieces
instructions:
1. Mix chicken with yogurt, turmeric, red chili, ginger garlic paste, and salt. Marinate 30 minutes.
2. Heat oil in a pot and fry onions until golden brown.
3. Add marinated chicken and cook on high heat 6-8 minutes until color changes.
4. Add tomatoes, coriander, cumin, and remaining red chili. Cook 5 minutes.
5. Cover and cook on low heat 20 minutes until chicken is tender.
6. Add fresh fenugreek leaves and cook 8 minutes until wilted and oil separates.
7. Sprinkle kasuri methi and garam masala. Stir and cook 3 minutes.
8. Rest 5 minutes and serve with naan, roti, or rice.

title: Kesar Makhani Paneer
instructions:
1. Soak saffron in warm milk and set aside 10 minutes.
2. Heat butter in a pan and sauté onion paste until soft and light golden.
3. Add ginger garlic paste and cook 1 minute, then add tomato puree, cashew paste, red chili, and turmeric.
4. Cook 10-12 minutes until the masala thickens and oil separates.
5. Add cream, saffron milk, sugar, and salt. Stir and simmer 5 minutes.
6. Add paneer cubes and gently mix. Simmer 5 minutes on low heat.
7. Crush kasuri methi between palms and add with garam masala.
8. Rest 5 minutes and serve with naan or jeera rice.

title: Methi Malai Paneer
instructions:
1. Blanch fenugreek leaves in salted boiling water 2 minutes, then drain and squeeze lightly.
2. Heat butter and oil in a pan. Add onion paste and cook until soft.
3. Add ginger garlic paste and green chilies. Cook 1 minute.
4. Add turmeric, red chili, coriander, and cumin. Stir 1 minute.
5. Add blanched fenugreek leaves and cook 4-5 minutes.
6. Pour in cream and milk. Simmer 5 minutes until slightly thick.
7. Add paneer cubes, salt, sugar, and garam masala. Simmer 5 minutes on low heat.
8. Rest 5 minutes and serve with roti or naan.

title: Aloo Methi
instructions:
1. Heat oil in a pan and add cumin seeds. Let them crackle.
2. Add onion, ginger, and garlic. Fry until onion is soft and light golden.
3. Add potatoes, turmeric, red chili, coriander, and salt. Stir well.
4. Add 1/2 cup water, cover, and cook 10-12 minutes until potatoes are almost tender.
5. Add chopped fenugreek leaves and mix gently.
6. Cook uncovered 5-6 minutes until methi is wilted and potatoes are fully cooked.
7. Turn off heat, add lemon juice, and serve with roti or paratha.

title: Aloo Palak
instructions:
1. Blanch spinach in boiling water 2 minutes, then transfer to cold water, drain, and blend into a smooth puree.
2. Heat oil in a pan and fry potatoes until golden and almost cooked. Remove and set aside.
3. In the same oil, add cumin seeds, onion, ginger garlic paste, and green chilies. Fry until soft.
4. Add turmeric, red chili, coriander, and salt. Stir 1 minute.
5. Add spinach puree and cook 5 minutes until thick.
6. Add fried potatoes and mix gently. Simmer 6-8 minutes.
7. Add garam masala and cream if using. Stir and cook 2 minutes.
8. Serve hot with roti, naan, or rice.

title: Aloo Jeera
instructions:
1. Parboil potatoes until just tender, then peel and cube them.
2. Heat oil in a pan and add cumin seeds. Fry until they crackle and smell nutty.
3. Add potato cubes and toss well to coat with cumin oil.
4. Sprinkle turmeric, red chili, coriander, and salt. Mix gently.
5. Cook on medium heat 8-10 minutes, turning occasionally, until potatoes are lightly crisp.
6. Add green chilies and cook 2 minutes.
7. Turn off heat, add lemon juice and cilantro, and serve hot with puri or roti.

title: Aloo Dam
instructions:
1. Boil baby potatoes until just tender, then peel and prick lightly with a fork.
2. Heat mustard oil in a pan and add panch phoron and bay leaf. Let them sizzle.
3. Add ginger paste, turmeric, red chili, cumin, and coriander. Stir 1 minute.
4. Add yogurt and tomato puree. Cook 5 minutes until oil separates.
5. Add boiled potatoes and toss to coat with masala.
6. Add 1 cup water, salt, and sugar. Cover and simmer 15 minutes on low heat.
7. Add green chilies and cook uncovered until the gravy is thick and clings to potatoes.
8. Rest 5 minutes and serve with luchi, paratha, or rice.

title: Adrak Gosht
ingredients: halal mutton 1 kg, cut into pieces
instructions:
1. Mix mutton with yogurt, ginger garlic paste, turmeric, red chili, coriander, cumin, black pepper, and salt. Marinate 1 hour.
2. Heat oil or ghee in a heavy pot and fry onions until golden brown.
3. Add marinated mutton and cook on high heat 8 minutes, stirring, until color changes.
4. Add 1 cup water, cover, and pressure cook 30 minutes or simmer 1 1/2 hours until tender.
5. Uncover and bhuna on high heat until the gravy is thick and oil separates.
6. Add half the julienned ginger and green chilies. Cook 5 minutes.
7. Sprinkle garam masala and remaining ginger on top.
8. Rest 5 minutes and serve with naan, roti, or rice.

title: Mushroom Matar
instructions:
1. Heat 1 tbsp oil in a pan and sauté mushrooms until browned and moisture evaporates. Remove.
2. Add remaining oil to the pan and add cumin seeds if desired, then onion. Fry until soft.
3. Add ginger garlic paste and cook 1 minute.
4. Add tomato puree, turmeric, red chili, coriander, cumin, and salt. Cook 6-8 minutes.
5. Add green peas and 1/2 cup water. Cover and cook 8 minutes until peas are tender.
6. Add sautéed mushrooms and mix gently.
7. Simmer 5 minutes, then add garam masala and cream if using.
8. Cook 2 minutes and serve with roti, paratha, or rice.

title: Mushroom Bhuna
instructions:
1. Heat mustard oil in a pan and fry onions until deep golden brown.
2. Add ginger garlic paste, turmeric, red chili, coriander, and cumin. Stir 1 minute.
3. Add tomato and cook until soft and oil separates.
4. Add mushrooms and salt. Mix well.
5. Cook on high heat 8-10 minutes until mushrooms release moisture.
6. Continue bhuna until the moisture evaporates and mushrooms are coated with thick masala.
7. Add green chilies and garam masala. Cook 3 minutes.
8. Serve hot with paratha or plain rice.

title: Mushroom Pepper Fry
instructions:
1. Heat oil in a pan and add fennel seeds and curry leaves. Let them sizzle.
2. Add onion, ginger garlic paste, and green chilies. Fry until onion is golden.
3. Add mushrooms and cook on high heat 5 minutes.
4. Add turmeric, red chili, coriander, cumin, and salt. Mix well.
5. Continue frying until mushrooms are cooked and moisture evaporates.
6. Add crushed black pepper and toss for 3-4 minutes until dry and fragrant.
7. Turn off heat and add lemon juice.
8. Serve hot as a side or with roti.

title: Mushroom Manchurian
instructions:
1. In a bowl, mix cornflour, all-purpose flour, salt, black pepper, and enough water to make a thick batter.
2. Dip mushroom pieces in the batter, coating well.
3. Heat oil for frying and fry mushrooms in batches until golden and crisp. Drain on paper.
4. Heat 2 tbsp oil in a wok and add ginger garlic paste and green chilies. Stir 30 seconds.
5. Add onion and capsicum. Stir-fry on high heat 2-3 minutes so they stay crunchy.
6. Add soy sauce, chili sauce, ketchup, and lemon juice. Mix well.
7. Add 1/2 cup water and bring to a simmer. Mix cornstarch with 1 tbsp water and add to thicken.
8. Toss fried mushrooms in the sauce until coated, cook 2 minutes, and serve hot.

title: Gobi Manchurian
ingredients: 1 medium cauliflower (500 g), cut into florets
instructions:
1. Blanch cauliflower florets in salted boiling water for 3 minutes, drain and pat dry.
2. Mix flour, cornstarch, ginger-garlic paste, black pepper, salt and enough water to make a thick batter.
3. Coat florets in batter and deep fry in hot oil until golden and crisp; drain.
4. Heat 2 tbsp oil, add garlic, ginger, onion, bell pepper and green chilies; stir-fry on high heat for 2 minutes.
5. Add ketchup, soy sauce, chili sauce, vinegar and 2 tbsp water; cook until glossy.
6. Add fried cauliflower and toss quickly to coat.
7. Garnish with spring onions and sesame seeds; serve hot.

title: Chilli Paneer
instructions:
1. Toss paneer with cornstarch, flour, ginger-garlic paste, salt and pepper.
2. Shallow fry paneer in hot oil until light golden; drain.
3. Heat 2 tbsp oil, add garlic, ginger, onion, bell pepper and green chilies; stir-fry 2 minutes.
4. Add soy sauce, ketchup, chili sauce, vinegar, sugar and water; simmer 1 minute.
5. Add fried paneer and toss gently.
6. Cook 2 minutes until sauce coats paneer.
7. Garnish with spring onions and serve hot.

title: Chilli Fish
ingredients: 500 g halal boneless fish fillets, cubed
instructions:
1. Marinate fish with ginger-garlic paste, chili powder, turmeric and salt for 15 minutes.
2. Mix egg, cornstarch and flour into a batter; coat fish pieces.
3. Deep fry fish in hot oil until golden and crisp; drain.
4. Heat 2 tbsp oil, stir-fry garlic, ginger, onion, bell pepper and green chilies for 2 minutes.
5. Add soy sauce, ketchup, chili sauce, vinegar, sugar and water; simmer.
6. Add fried fish and toss gently to coat.
7. Garnish with spring onions and serve hot.

title: Chilli Beef
instructions:
1. Marinate beef with soy sauce, cornstarch, ginger-garlic paste and black pepper for 20 minutes.
2. Heat 2 tbsp oil in a wok and sear beef on high heat until browned; remove.
3. Add garlic, ginger, onion, bell pepper and green chilies; stir-fry 2 minutes.
4. Add soy sauce, ketchup, chili sauce, vinegar, sugar and stock; simmer 2 minutes.
5. Return beef to wok and toss.
6. Cook 3-4 minutes until beef is tender and coated.
7. Garnish with spring onions and serve hot.

title: Egg Curry
instructions:
1. Lightly prick boiled eggs and set aside.
2. Heat oil, add cumin seeds and onion; fry until golden.
3. Add ginger-garlic paste and cook 1 minute.
4. Add tomatoes, turmeric, chili powder, coriander powder, garam masala and salt; cook until oil separates.
5. Lower heat, stir in yogurt and cook 2 minutes.
6. Add water and green chilies; bring to a simmer.
7. Add eggs and simmer 8-10 minutes.
8. Garnish with coriander and serve with rice or roti.

title: Egg Bhuna
instructions:
1. Heat oil and fry sliced onion until deep golden.
2. Add ginger-garlic paste and cook 1 minute.
3. Add cumin, coriander, turmeric, chili powder, garam masala and salt; stir.
4. Add tomatoes and cook until soft and oil separates.
5. Stir in yogurt and cook 2 minutes.
6. Add water and green chilies; simmer.
7. Add boiled eggs and bhuna on medium heat until gravy is thick and clings to eggs.
8. Garnish with coriander and serve.

title: Dimer Devil
instructions:
1. Heat 2 tbsp oil, fry onion until soft.
2. Add ginger-garlic paste, beef mince, turmeric, chili powder, garam masala and salt; cook until dry.
3. Mix cooked keema with mashed potatoes and cool.
4. Flatten a portion of keema-potato mixture in your palm, place a boiled egg in center and wrap to cover completely.
5. Repeat with remaining eggs.
6. Dip each covered egg in beaten egg, then roll in breadcrumbs.
7. Deep fry in hot oil until golden brown.
8. Drain and serve hot with chutney.

title: Deviled Egg Curry Bengali
instructions:
1. Heat oil, add panch phoron and bay leaf; let crackle.
2. Add onion and fry until golden.
3. Add ginger-garlic paste and cook 1 minute.
4. Add turmeric, chili powder, cumin, coriander and salt; stir.
5. Add tomatoes and potato; cook 5 minutes.
6. Add water and green chilies; simmer until potato is tender.
7. Add boiled eggs and simmer 5 minutes.
8. Garnish with coriander and serve with rice.

title: Mughlai Paratha
instructions:
1. Mix flour, salt, oil and water into a soft dough; rest 30 minutes.
2. Heat 2 tbsp oil, cook onion, ginger-garlic paste, beef mince, turmeric, chili powder, garam masala and salt until dry.
3. Divide dough into balls and roll each into a thin square.
4. Beat one egg with green chili and coriander; spread over paratha.
5. Spread a portion of keema over half the paratha.
6. Fold into a square or envelope, sealing edges.
7. Fry in hot oil until golden and crisp on both sides.
8. Drain and serve hot with chutney.

title: Keema Paratha
instructions:
1. Mix flour, salt and water into a soft dough; rest 30 minutes.
2. Heat 2 tbsp oil, fry onion until soft.
3. Add ginger-garlic paste, beef mince, coriander powder, turmeric, chili powder, garam masala and salt; cook until dry.
4. Stir in coriander and cool.
5. Divide dough into balls; roll one into a small circle.
6. Place keema filling in center, bring edges together and seal.
7. Roll gently into a flat paratha.
8. Fry on a hot tawa with ghee until golden on both sides.
9. Serve hot with yogurt or pickle.

title: Chicken Kathi Roll
ingredients: 500 g halal boneless chicken, cut into strips
instructions:
1. Marinate chicken with yogurt, ginger-garlic paste, chili powder, turmeric, garam masala and salt for 30 minutes.
2. Heat oil and cook chicken until browned and cooked through; set aside.
3. In same pan, stir-fry onion, bell pepper and green chilies for 2 minutes.
4. Beat eggs with a pinch of salt; cook thin omelettes.
5. Warm parathas and place an omelette on each.
6. Spread mint chutney, add chicken and stir-fried vegetables.
7. Add onion rings and lemon juice; roll tightly.
8. Wrap in paper and serve.

title: Beef Kathi Roll
instructions:
1. Marinate beef with yogurt, ginger-garlic paste, chili powder, turmeric, garam masala and salt for 30 minutes.
2. Heat oil and cook beef on high heat until browned and tender; set aside.
3. Stir-fry onion, bell pepper and green chilies for 2 minutes.
4. Beat eggs with salt and cook thin omelettes.
5. Warm parathas and place an omelette on each.
6. Spread mint chutney, add beef and vegetables.
7. Add onion rings and lemon juice; roll tightly.
8. Wrap and serve hot.

title: Keema Mattar
instructions:
1. Heat oil and fry onion until golden.
2. Add ginger-garlic paste and cook 1 minute.
3. Add beef mince and cook until browned.
4. Add turmeric, chili powder, coriander, cumin, garam masala and salt; stir.
5. Add tomatoes and cook until soft.
6. Add green peas and water; cover and simmer 15-20 minutes.
7. Add green chilies and cook until oil separates.
8. Garnish with coriander and serve with roti or rice.

title: Keema Biryani
ingredients: 1/2 tsp saffron soaked in 2 tbsp milk
Whole spices: 1 bay leaf, 3 cardamom, 4 cloves, 1 cinnamon stick
instructions:
1. Heat ghee, add whole spices and half the fried onion.
2. Add ginger-garlic paste, beef mince, chili powder, turmeric, coriander, garam masala and salt; cook until browned.
