6. Add potatoes, cover, and simmer until beef is tender.
7. Uncover and cook until gravy thickens.
8. Sprinkle garam masala and coriander, then serve.

title: Idli Sambar
instructions:
1. Soak rice, urad dal, and fenugreek 6 hours.
2. Grind to a smooth batter and ferment 8 hours.
3. Pour batter into idli molds and steam 10-12 minutes.
4. Cook toor dal with turmeric until soft.
5. Make sambar by boiling tamarind, vegetables, sambar powder, and cooked dal.
6. Temper mustard seeds and curry leaves in oil.
7. Add tempering to sambar and simmer 5 minutes.
8. Serve hot idlis with sambar.

title: Vada Sambar
instructions:
1. Soak urad dal 4 hours and drain.
2. Grind with green chilies, ginger, curry leaves, and salt to a thick batter.
3. Shape into small vadas.
4. Deep fry until golden and crisp.
5. Cook toor dal with turmeric until soft.
6. Make sambar with tamarind, vegetables, sambar powder, and cooked dal.
7. Temper mustard seeds and curry leaves, then add to sambar.
8. Soak fried vadas in hot sambar 5 minutes.
9. Serve with extra sambar.

title: Uttapam
instructions:
1. Soak rice, urad dal, and fenugreek 6 hours.
2. Grind to a slightly coarse batter.
3. Ferment 8 hours until risen.
4. Heat a flat tawa and lightly oil it.
5. Pour a ladle of batter and spread thick.
6. Sprinkle onion, tomato, green chilies, and coriander.
7. Drizzle oil around edges.
8. Cook until bottom is golden, flip, and cook 1 minute.
9. Serve hot with chutney.

title: Rava Dosa
instructions:
1. Mix semolina, rice flour, all-purpose flour, yogurt, and water.
2. Add cumin, green chili, ginger, curry leaves, and salt.
3. Rest batter 30 minutes.
4. Heat a tawa until hot and sprinkle with water.
5. Pour batter thinly from a ladle, moving in circles.
6. Drizzle oil around edges.
7. Cook until crisp and golden without flipping.
8. Fold and serve with coconut chutney.

title: Masala Puri
ingredients: 1 cup dried green peas, soaked overnight
instructions:
1. Boil soaked green peas until soft.
2. Mash peas and boiled potatoes together.
3. Grind coriander, mint, tamarind, chaat masala, red chili, cumin, black salt, and salt into a chutney.
4. Mix pea-potato mash with the chutney.
5. Crush 3-4 puris on a serving plate.
6. Spoon pea mixture over the puris.
7. Top with onion, tomato, sev, and yogurt if using.
8. Serve immediately.

title: Pav Bhaji
instructions:
1. Mash boiled potatoes, peas, cauliflower, and carrot.
2. Heat 2 tbsp butter and sauté onions until soft.
3. Add ginger garlic and capsicum, cook 2 minutes.
4. Add tomatoes, pav bhaji masala, red chili, turmeric, and salt.
5. Cook until tomatoes break down.
6. Add mashed vegetables and mash everything together.
7. Simmer 10 minutes, adding water if needed.
8. Toast pav buns with remaining butter.
9. Serve bhaji with pav, coriander, and lemon.

title: Misal Pav
instructions:
1. Boil sprouts with turmeric and salt until soft.
2. Heat oil and add cumin seeds.
3. Add onion and fry until golden.
4. Add ginger garlic, goda masala, red chili, and salt.
5. Add tomatoes and cook until soft.
6. Add boiled sprouts and 2 cups water, then simmer 15 minutes.
7. Assemble in bowls with farsan, chopped onion, coriander, and lemon.
8. Serve with pav buns.

title: Pakistani Nihari Masala
instructions:
1. Dry roast coriander, fennel, cumin, cardamom, cloves, cinnamon, bay leaves, mace, nutmeg, dried ginger, black pepper, poppy seeds, and ajwain.
2. Cool completely.
3. Grind to a fine powder.
4. Sieve the ground masala.
5. Mix in red chili powder and turmeric.
6. Store in an airtight jar for up to 3 months.

title: Paya boiled
instructions:
1. Wash trotters thoroughly under running water.
2. Blanch in boiling water 5 minutes, then drain.
3. Place trotters in a pressure cooker.
4. Add onions, ginger garlic, turmeric, salt, red chili, whole spices, and water.
5. Pressure cook 45-60 minutes until trotters are very tender.
6. Release pressure naturally.
7. Separate meat from bones.
8. Strain broth and use as needed.

title: Paye Soup
ingredients: 4 mutton trotters, boiled and meat separated
instructions:
1. Heat oil and add whole spices.
2. Add onions and fry until golden.
3. Add ginger garlic and cook 1 minute.
4. Add tomatoes, turmeric, red chili, coriander, and salt.
5. Stir in yogurt and cook until oil separates.
6. Add trotters and reserved broth.
7. Mix flour with 1/2 cup water and add to pot.
8. Simmer 20 minutes until soup thickens.
9. Add garam masala, coriander, and green chilies.
10. Serve hot with naan.

title: Kaleji Curry
ingredients: 500 g mutton liver, rinsed and cubed
instructions:
1. Heat oil and add cumin seeds.
2. Add onions and fry until golden.
3. Add ginger garlic and cook 1 minute.
4. Add tomatoes, coriander, turmeric, red chili, and salt.
5. Stir in yogurt and cook until oil separates.
6. Add liver pieces and toss gently.
7. Cook 8-10 minutes until liver is just done.
8. Sprinkle garam masala and coriander.
9. Serve hot with roti.

title: Chicken Paya
instructions:
1. Wash chicken feet thoroughly and blanch 5 minutes.
2. Pressure cook with turmeric, salt, and 4 cups water for 20 minutes.
3. Heat oil and add whole spices.
4. Add onions and fry until golden.
5. Add ginger garlic, red chili, coriander, and salt.
6. Add tomatoes and yogurt, then cook until oil separates.
7. Add chicken feet with broth.
8. Simmer 15 minutes until gravy thickens.
9. Sprinkle garam masala and coriander.
10. Serve hot.

title: Mutton Biryani Kashmiri
ingredients: 1/2 tsp saffron soaked in 1/2 cup warm milk
instructions:
1. Marinate mutton with yogurt, ginger garlic, red chili, fennel, cumin, coriander, turmeric, and salt.
2. Heat ghee and add whole spices.
3. Add mutton and cook until browned.
4. Add 1 cup water, cover, and simmer until mutton is tender.
5. Parboil soaked rice in salted water until 70 percent cooked, then drain.
6. Layer rice and mutton in a heavy pot, adding fried onions and saffron milk between layers.
7. Cover tightly and cook on low dum 20 minutes.
8. Rest 10 minutes.
9. Fluff gently and serve.

title: Kashmiri Dum Aloo
ingredients: 500 g baby potatoes, boiled and pricked
instructions:
1. Heat mustard oil until smoking, then cool slightly.
2. Fry potatoes until lightly browned, then remove.
3. Add cloves, black cardamom, and cinnamon.
4. Add ginger, garlic, fennel, red chili, turmeric, and salt.
5. Add whisked yogurt and cook until oil separates.
6. Add potatoes and 1/2 cup water.
7. Cover and cook on low dum 15 minutes.
8. Sprinkle garam masala and coriander.
9. Serve hot with rice.

title: Kashmiri Rogan Josh
instructions:
1. Heat ghee and add cloves, black cardamom, cinnamon, and bay leaf.
2. Add mutton and brown well.
3. Add ginger, garlic, fennel, red chili, turmeric, cumin, and salt.
4. Stir in yogurt and cook until oil separates.
5. Add 2 cups water and bring to a boil.
6. Cover and simmer until mutton is tender.
7. Uncover and cook until gravy is thick.
8. Sprinkle garam masala and serve.

title: Chole Chaat
ingredients: 2 cups boiled white chickpeas (kabuli chana), drained
1 large boiled potato, peeled and cubed
instructions:
1. In a large bowl, combine boiled chickpeas and boiled potato cubes.
2. Add red onion, tomato, green chili, chaat masala, roasted cumin, black salt, red chili powder, and salt; toss well.
3. Add whisked yogurt, tamarind chutney, mint-coriander chutney, and lemon juice; mix gently until coated.
4. Taste and adjust chaat masala, black salt, or lemon juice.
5. Transfer to serving bowls and top with chopped coriander.
6. Sprinkle fine sev and crushed papdi over each portion just before serving.
7. Serve immediately so the sev stays crunchy.

title: Rajma Chawal
ingredients: 1 cup dried red kidney beans (rajma), soaked overnight
2 cups basmati rice, rinsed and soaked 20 minutes
3 cups water for rajma, plus more as needed
instructions:
1. Drain soaked rajma, add to pressure cooker with 3 cups water and 1/2 tsp salt; pressure cook until soft, about 6-8 whistles, then set aside with cooking liquid.
2. Heat oil or ghee in a pot, add cumin seeds and let splutter.
3. Add onion and sauté until golden brown; add ginger-garlic paste and green chilies, cook 1 minute.
4. Add tomato puree, coriander powder, turmeric, red chili powder, cumin powder, and salt; cook until oil separates.
5. Add cooked rajma with its liquid and simmer 15-20 minutes, mashing a few beans to thicken; stir in garam masala and coriander.
6. Meanwhile, cook soaked rice with 4 cups water and salt until tender but separate; drain if needed.
7. Serve hot rajma over steamed rice with extra coriander.

title: Kadi Pakora
instructions:
1. For pakoras, mix besan, onion, potato, spinach, ajwain, red chili, turmeric, salt, and enough water to make a thick batter.
2. Heat oil in a deep pan; drop small spoonfuls of batter and fry until golden and crisp; drain on paper towels.
3. For kadi, whisk yogurt, besan, turmeric, red chili, coriander powder, salt, and water in a bowl until smooth.
4. Pour mixture into a heavy pot and cook on low heat, stirring continuously, until it thickens and comes to a gentle boil, about 15-20 minutes.
5. Add fried pakoras to the kadi and simmer 5 minutes so they soften slightly.
6. For tempering, heat oil or ghee in a small pan; add mustard seeds, cumin, fenugreek, dried red chilies, curry leaves, ginger, garlic, and asafoetida; fry 30 seconds.
7. Pour tempering over kadi, stir gently, garnish with coriander, and serve hot with rice or roti.

title: Kashmiri Pulao
ingredients: 2 cups basmati rice, rinsed and soaked 20 minutes
1/4 tsp saffron soaked in 1/4 cup warm milk
instructions:
1. Heat 1 tbsp ghee in a pan; fry cashews, almonds, raisins, and paneer cubes until light golden; set aside.
2. In the same pan, add remaining ghee, cumin, bay leaf, cinnamon, green cardamoms, cloves, and black cardamom; sauté 30 seconds.
3. Add onion and fry until golden; add ginger, green chilies, turmeric, and mixed vegetables; cook 3-4 minutes.
4. Add yogurt and salt; cook 2 minutes, then stir in pineapple and apple.
5. Add soaked rice and gently mix without breaking grains.
6. Pour in water and saffron milk; bring to a boil, then cover and cook on low until rice is tender and water absorbed, about 12-15 minutes.
7. Fluff with a fork, fold in fried nuts, paneer, raisins, and coriander.
8. Serve hot with raita.

title: Kashmiri Tehri
ingredients: 2 cups basmati rice, rinsed and soaked 20 minutes
instructions:
1. Heat oil or ghee in a heavy pot; add cumin, bay leaf, cinnamon, green cardamoms, cloves, and black cardamom; sauté until fragrant.
2. Add onion and fry until golden brown; add ginger-garlic paste and green chilies, cook 1 minute.
3. Add potato, peas, carrots, beans, and cauliflower; stir-fry 4-5 minutes.
4. Add turmeric, red chili, coriander, fennel, and salt; mix well.
5. Reduce heat, add whisked yogurt, and cook 2 minutes until it blends into the masala.
6. Add soaked rice and gently toss to coat with masala.
7. Pour in water, bring to a boil, then cover and cook on low until rice and vegetables are tender, about 15 minutes.
8. Fluff with a fork, garnish with coriander and mint, and serve hot with raita.

title: Zarda
ingredients: 2 cups basmati rice, rinsed and soaked 30 minutes
1/4 tsp orange food color (halal) or 1 tbsp rose water (optional)
instructions:
1. Soak saffron in warm milk and set aside.
2. Boil water in a large pot with cardamoms, cloves, bay leaf, and a pinch of salt.
3. Drain soaked rice and add to boiling water; cook until 70% done, then drain.
4. In a separate pan, heat ghee and lightly fry cashews, almonds, raisins, and coconut; set aside.
5. In the same pot, make sugar syrup with sugar and 1 cup water; simmer until slightly sticky, then add saffron milk and food color or rose water.
6. Gently fold drained rice into the syrup, mixing so grains are coated.
7. Cover tightly and cook on very low heat for dum for 10-12 minutes.
8. Fluff with a fork, fold in fried nuts and raisins, and serve warm.

title: Arcot Biriyani
ingredients: 1 kg halal mutton, cut into medium pieces
4 cups seeraga samba rice or basmati rice, rinsed and soaked 20 minutes
instructions:
1. Marinate mutton with yogurt, ginger-garlic paste, red chili, turmeric, coriander, garam masala, black pepper, salt, and lemon juice for at least 1 hour.
2. Heat oil and half the ghee in a heavy pot; fry sliced onions until deep golden, remove half for garnish.
3. Add whole spices and fennel to the pot; sauté 30 seconds, then add tomatoes, green chilies, mint, coriander, and coconut; cook until soft.
4. Add marinated mutton and cook on high 5 minutes, then cover and simmer on low until mutton is tender, about 45-60 minutes, adding water if needed.
5. Meanwhile, boil 5 cups water with salt and remaining ghee; add soaked rice and cook until 70% done, then drain.
6. Layer cooked mutton masala and parboiled rice in the pot, sprinkling fried onions, cashews, mint, and coriander between layers.
7. Cover tightly with a lid or seal with dough; cook on very low heat for dum for 20-25 minutes.
8. Rest 10 minutes, then gently fluff with a fork and serve hot with raita.
